The eighth unit announces the disambiguation: from the considerations carried through, and from the word's frequent use, the ambiguity of "world" leaps to the eye; disentangling it can become an indication of the phenomena meant in the different significations and of their connection. Four senses follow, each a unit.

First sense: world as an ontic concept — the totality of beings that can be present-at-hand within the world. This is the world of the naive enumeration (unit one), the omnitudo entium of the tradition's cosmology.

Second sense: world as an ontological term — the being of the beings named under the first sense; and "world" can become the title of a region embracing in each case a manifold of beings, as when the "world" of the mathematician means the region of possible objects of mathematics. This is the world of unit two — regional ontology's sense, Husserl's "worlds" of nature, of culture, of mathematics.

Third sense: world in an ontic sense again, but now not as the beings Dasein essentially is not, but as that "wherein" a factical Dasein as this Dasein "lives." World here has a pre-ontologically existentiell signification, with various possibilities: the "public" we-world, or one's "own" and nearest (domestic) environing world. This is the sense of everyday speech — the businessman's world, the world of the theater, my world — and it is the phenomenally rich one: the wherein of factical life, straight from the early Freiburg lectures.

Fourth sense: world as the ontological-existential concept of worldhood — itself modifiable into the respective structural whole of particular "worlds," but enclosing in itself the a priori of worldhood in general. And the terminological decision: the expression "world" is claimed for the third signification; when used in the first sense, it is marked by quotation marks. The four-fold table is a small masterpiece of § 7 B's derivation-method (one word, its senses ordered and grounded), and the notation-rule matters practically for every subsequent page: unquoted world = the wherein of living; "world" in quotes = the totality of things. The fourth sense names the chapter's quarry — the a priori that each particular world (sense three) instantiates.

The thirteenth unit fixes the adjectives: "worldly" (weltlich) then means terminologically a mode of being of Dasein, never of beings present-at-hand "in" the world — these we call world-belonging (weltzugehörig) or innerworldly (innerweltlich). The rule inverts ordinary usage (where "worldly" attaches to things and affairs), and the inversion is the doctrine in miniature: only Dasein is worldly, because only Dasein has world; things are at most within one.

The fourteenth unit indicts the tradition by this measure. A glance at previous ontology shows that missing the constitution of being-in-the-world goes together with skipping over (Überspringen) the phenomenon of worldhood: one attempts instead to interpret the world from the being of innerworldly present-at-hand beings — which moreover are proximally not even discovered — from nature. Nature, understood ontologically-categorially, is a limit case of the being of possible innerworldly beings; Dasein can discover beings as nature only in a determinate mode of its being-in-the-world, a knowing that has the character of a certain de-worlding (Entweltlichung) of the world. "Nature" as the categorial sum of being-structures of a certain innerworldly being can never make worldhood intelligible — and even the phenomenon "nature" in the sense of the Romantic concept of nature is ontologically graspable only from the concept of world, that is, from the analytic of Dasein. The paragraph makes three moves of rank. Nature is demoted to a limit case — the extreme product of stripping worldhood out — inverting the tradition's order (nature as foundation) point for point. Its discovery is named de-worlding: the theoretical attitude of § 13 does not neutrally find nature but actively divests the encountered of its worldly character. And even Romantic nature — the landscape that "grips" us, § 15 will say — is no counter-instance: as a mode of encounter it presupposes world, and so falls to the analytic too.

The fifteenth unit poses the reflexive question the diagnosis demands: with regard to an ontological analysis of worldhood, transmitted ontology — where it sees the problem at all — moves in a dead end; and, on the other side, an interpretation of Dasein's worldhood and of the possibilities and ways of its becoming-worldly will have to show why Dasein, in the mode of being of knowing the world, skips over the phenomenon of worldhood ontically and ontologically. In the fact of this skipping lies at once the indication that special precautions are needed to win, for access to the phenomenon, the right phenomenal point of departure — one that prevents skipping. The demand repeats § 12's deep move: the tradition's failure must itself be explained from Dasein's being (the skipping has an existential ground — absorption in the discovered at the cost of the disclosing), and method must be designed against the object's own tendency to be missed.

The sixteenth unit recalls the precaution already in hand: the methodological directive has been given — being-in-the-world, and so the world too, is to become theme in the horizon of average everydayness as Dasein's nearest mode of being; everyday being-in-the-world is to be pursued, and in phenomenal reliance on it something like world must come into view. Everydayness (§ 9's decision) now earns its methodological keep: the everyday is precisely where the world has not yet been de-worlded — where, if anywhere, worldhood is operative and catchable.

The closing unit sets the itinerary. The nearest world of everyday Dasein is the environing world (Umwelt); the investigation proceeds from this existential character of average being-in-the-world to the idea of worldhood in general, seeking the worldhood of the environing world (Umweltlichkeit) by passing through an ontological interpretation of the beings encountered nearest within it. The expression Umwelt contains, in the "um" (around), a pointer to spatiality; but the "round-about" constitutive for the environing world has no primarily "spatial" sense — the spatial character undeniably belonging to an environing world is rather to be clarified only from the structure of worldhood, whence Dasein's spatiality (indicated in § 12) becomes phenomenally visible. Ontology, however, has attempted precisely the reverse: to interpret the being of the "world" from spatiality, as res extensa — the most extreme tendency toward such an ontology, in counter-orientation to the res cogitans, with which Dasein coincides neither ontically nor ontologically, shows itself in Descartes; hence the analysis clarifies itself in three stages: A, analysis of environmentality and worldhood in general; B, illustrative contrast of the analysis of worldhood against Descartes' ontology of the "world"; C, the aroundness of the environing world and Dasein's "spatiality." Two commitments organize everything that follows: the order space-from-world (against the Cartesian world-from-space — extension as the world's substance), and the chapter's A–B–C architecture, in which the Descartes-confrontation of the unwritten Part Two is partially cashed in as section B.

##### A. The Analysis of Environmentality and Worldhood in General

###### § 15. The Being of the Beings Encountered in the Environing World

The opening unit fixes guide and starting point. The phenomenological exhibition of the being of the beings encountered nearest is accomplished along the guiding thread of everyday being-in-the-world, which we also call dealings (Umgang) in the world and with innerworldly beings; dealings have already dispersed themselves into a manifold of ways of concern. The nearest kind of dealings, as shown, is not merely perceiving cognition but handling, using concern — which has its own "knowledge." The phenomenological question concerns first the being of the beings encountered in such concern; and securing the seeing this demands requires a methodological preliminary. Two § 13 results are activated as premises: the priority of manipulating over perceiving, and — in the pregnant aside — the thesis that praxis has its own knowledge, its own epistēmē, not a deficit of theory: the sentence that licenses reading the whole section as an epistemology of skill.

The second unit gives the methodological preliminary. In the disclosure and explication of being, beings are in each case the pre- and co-thematic, while being stands in the theme proper; in the present analysis the pre-thematic beings are those that show themselves in environmental concern — not objects of theoretical "world"-cognition but the used, the produced, and the like. As so encountered they come pre-thematically into the view of a "knowing" that, as phenomenological, looks primarily at being and co-thematizes the respective beings from that thematization of being. This phenomenological interpreting is accordingly no cognizing of ontic qualities of beings but a determining of the structure of their being — as an investigation of being it becomes the independent and explicit enactment of the understanding of being that always already belongs to Dasein and is "alive" in every dealing with beings. The pre-thematic beings — the used, what is under production — become accessible in a transposing of oneself into such concern; strictly, though, this talk of transposing is misleading, for we do not first need to transpose ourselves into this mode of being: everyday Dasein always already is in it — opening the door, I make use of the latch. Winning phenomenological access consists rather in pushing back the interpretive tendencies that crowd in and run along with us, which cover up the phenomenon of such "concern" altogether and, in one with it, the beings as they are encountered from themselves in concern for it. The traps become clear with the investigative question: which beings are to be pre-theme and established as the pre-phenomenal soil? The paragraph is the finest short statement of the book's method in action: ontology thematizes being at beings (the ontological difference as a rule of procedure); phenomenology is the explicit enactment of the pre-ontological understanding "alive" in latch-using; and access is negative work — not adopting a stance but dismantling the interpretations already underway (§ 7 C's passage through coverings). The latch is the whole argument in an example: I use it constantly and never observe it — the analysis begins where we already are.

The third unit springs the first trap by naming it. One answers: things. But with this self-evident answer the sought pre-phenomenal soil is perhaps already missed, for in addressing beings as "thing" (res) lies an unexpressed, anticipatory ontological characterization: analysis proceeding from such beings toward being hits upon thinghood and reality, and the explication then progressively finds characters like substantiality, materiality, extendedness, side-by-sideness. But the beings encountered in concern are, in this being, pre-ontologically at first concealed; in naming things as the "proximally given" one goes ontologically astray, though ontically one means something else — what one actually means remains undetermined. Or one characterizes these "things" as "value-laden" things: but what does value mean ontologically? how is this "adhering" and being-laden to be grasped categorially? And apart from the obscurity of this structure of value-ladenness — is the phenomenal being-character of what is encountered in concernful dealings thereby reached at all? The critique has two tiers. "Thing" is not innocent: the word carries res, and res delivers the whole Cartesian category-set before analysis begins — a lexical instance of § 6's tradition-as-concealment. And the value-supplement — the era's standard repair (Lotze through Rickert to the early Husserl and Scheler: the thing plus adhering value-predicates) — is refused at both joints: "value" is ontologically dark, and even were it clear, gluing values onto present-at-hand substrates would still start from the wrong being. § 21 will return to demolish the value-laden thing in Descartes' aftermath.

The fourth unit names the right beings by way of the Greeks. The Greeks had an appropriate term for "things": pragmata — that with which one has to do in concernful dealings (praxis); but they left precisely the specifically "pragmatic" character of the pragmata in the dark, determining them "proximally" as "mere things." We call the beings encountered in concern equipment (das Zeug): in dealings one comes upon writing-equipment, sewing-equipment, work-, travel-, measuring-equipment. The mode of being of equipment is to be set forth, along the guiding thread of a prior delimitation of what makes equipment equipment: equipmentality (Zeughaftigkeit). The historical remark is destruction in one sentence: Greek language preserved the practical sense (pragma from praxis) that Greek ontology, guided by pure beholding (§ 6), immediately buried under "mere thing" — the word remembered what the theory forgot. Zeug is chosen with philological cunning: a collective noun (gear, tackle, stuff-for), grammatically resistant to the isolated singular — the resistance the next unit converts into a thesis.

The fifth unit states the holism. Strictly taken, an equipment never "is"; to the being of equipment there always belongs an equipmental whole (Zeugganzes), within which it can be this equipment that it is. Equipment is essentially "something in-order-to..." (um zu); the different ways of the in-order-to — serviceability, conduciveness, usability, handiness — constitute an equipmental totality. In the structure "in-order-to" lies a reference (Verweisung) of something to something — a phenomenon whose ontological genesis can be made visible only in later analyses; provisionally the task is to bring a manifold of references phenomenally into view. Equipment, in accordance with its equipmentality, always is in terms of its belonging to other equipment: writing-equipment, pen, ink, paper, blotter, table, lamp, furniture, windows, doors, room. These "things" never show themselves first for themselves, so as then to fill up a room as a sum of the real: what is encountered nearest, though not thematically grasped, is the room — and this not as the "between-four-walls" in a geometrical spatial sense, but as dwelling-equipment (Wohnzeug); out of it the "arrangement" shows itself, and in the arrangement the respective "individual" equipment. Before this individual item, an equipmental totality is in each case already discovered. This is the section's central ontological claim, and its logical form should be exact: the priority of the whole is not empirical (we happen to notice ensembles) but constitutive — an item is the equipment it is only within its totality, so the isolated tool is an abstraction, not a building block. The room-example runs the priority through three registers at once: against summation (no aggregation of things yields a room), against geometry (the room is not enclosed volume but a wherein of dwelling), and for the order of encounter (totality first, item within it). The deferred "ontological genesis" of reference is § 18's promissory note: reference will be grounded in Bewandtnis and significance.

The sixth unit derives the mode of being from the mode of access. The dealings cut to fit the equipment — in which alone it can show itself genuinely in its being, e.g., hammering with the hammer — neither grasp this being thematically as an occurring thing, nor does the using even know the equipmental structure as such. Hammering does not merely have, in addition, a knowledge of the hammer's equipment-character; it has appropriated this equipment as fittingly as possible. In such using dealings, concern subordinates itself to the in-order-to constitutive for the respective equipment; and the less the hammer-thing is merely gaped at, the more grippingly it is used, the more original the relation to it becomes, the more unveiledly it is encountered as what it is — as equipment. The hammering itself discovers the specific "handiness" of the hammer. The mode of being of equipment, in which it manifests itself from itself, we call readiness-to-hand (Zuhandenheit). Only because equipment has this "being-in-itself," and does not merely still occur, is it handy in the widest sense and available. The sharpest mere looking-at the so-and-so constituted "look" of things cannot discover the ready-to-hand: the merely "theoretically" looking gaze at things lacks the understanding of readiness-to-hand. But using-handling dealings are not blind: they have their own kind of sight, which guides the handling and gives it its specific thing-certainty. Dealings with equipment subordinate themselves to the reference-manifold of the in-order-to; and the sight of such self-accommodating is circumspection (Umsicht). Every clause carries doctrine. The inverse law — less staring, more grip, more original disclosure — is the section's epistemological scandal: engaged use is a better access to the tool's being than observation, which structurally cannot find readiness-to-hand at all. The provocative "An-sich-sein" assigns in-itselfness to the ready-to-hand (developed at § 16's end): the tool's being-in-itself is its inconspicuous availability, not observer-independence. And Umsicht names the section's answer to § 13's "practical = a-theoretical": praxis has sight — a circumspective looking-around that guides the hand — so the theory/practice divide is redrawn as two kinds of sight, not sight versus blindness.

The seventh unit makes that redrawing explicit. "Practical" comportment is not "a-theoretical" in the sense of sightlessness; its difference from theoretical comportment does not lie merely in the one contemplating and the other acting, with action applying theoretical knowledge lest it stay blind — rather, contemplating is as originally a concern as action has its sight. Theoretical comportment is un-circumspective mere looking-at; but because un-circumspective, not rule-less — it forms its canon in method. Both directions of the traditional picture fall: praxis is not applied theory (action has native sight), and theory is not the lifting of practical blindness (it is itself a mode of concern, § 13's tarrying). The closing aphorism — theory's canon is method — compresses § 3 and § 13 into six words: what circumspection does informally for the hand, method does formally for the detached gaze.

The eighth unit adds the phenomenology of inconspicuousness. The ready-to-hand is neither grasped theoretically at all, nor is it itself, for circumspection, at first circumspectively thematic: the peculiarity of what is proximally ready-to-hand is that it withdraws (sich zurückzieht), as it were, in its readiness-to-hand — precisely in order to be authentically ready-to-hand. What everyday dealings dwell alongside at first is not the tools themselves but the work (das Werk): what is to be produced at the time is the primarily concerned and hence the primarily ready-to-hand; the work carries the reference-totality within which the equipment is encountered. The withdrawal-thesis is among the book's most influential discoveries: the tool serves best when unnoticed — its being includes recession from attention — so the ready-to-hand is essentially non-thematic, and any thematizing has already modified it (the ground of § 16's breakdown-methodology and of a whole later literature on transparent coping). The relocation of primacy to the work reorients the field: circumspection looks past the hammer to the shoe being made — the toward-which organizes the workshop.

The ninth unit follows the work's own references forward: the work to be produced, as the what-for of hammer, plane, needle, has in its turn the mode of being of equipment — the shoe to be produced is for wearing (footgear), the finished clock for telling time. The work preeminently encountered in concernful dealings — the work in process — lets be co-encountered, in the usability essentially belonging to it, the what-for of its usability; the commissioned work is, in its turn, only on the ground of its use and of the reference-context of beings discovered in that use. The regress is deliberate: the product is itself equipment — no terminus of mere things is reached by following the in-order-to forward; use grounds the work's being all the way up.

The tenth unit follows the references backward into materials and finds nature. The work is not only usable for...; producing is itself in each case a using of something for something. In the work lies at once the reference to "materials": it is dependent on leather, thread, nails; leather in turn is produced from hides, taken from animals that others breed; animals also occur within the world without breeding, and even in breeding this being in a certain way produces itself. So in the environing world beings become accessible that in themselves need no producing and are always already ready-to-hand: hammer, tongs, nail refer in themselves to — they consist of — steel, iron, ore, stone, wood. In used equipment, "nature" is co-discovered through the use — nature in the light of natural products. The backward chain (shoe, leather, hide, animal, breeding, the unbred) is a genealogy of nature from within the workshop: nature first shows itself as material-for, resource, the self-renewing stock — discovered by use, inside the reference-totality, not behind it.

The eleventh unit protects this discovery from two flattenings. Nature here must not be understood as what is merely still present-at-hand — nor as the power of nature. The forest is timber-forest, the mountain quarry, the river water-power, the wind is wind "in the sails": with the discovered environing world, "nature" so discovered is encountered. One can disregard its mode of being as ready-to-hand and discover and determine it merely in its pure presence-at-hand — but to this nature-discovering, nature as what "stirs and strives," what assails us, what captivates as landscape, remains hidden: the botanist's plants are not the flowers of the hedgerow; the geographically fixed "source" of a river is not the "spring in the ground." The unit stakes out three natures and refuses to reduce any to another: environmental nature (forest-as-timber — the primary phenomenon here), scientific nature (the de-worlded present-at-hand of § 14), and the nature of moods and poetry (what assails and captivates), which is hidden from science not by its complexity but categorially. The two closing antitheses became famous because they perform the point: same entity, different modes of encounter, no common measure — and the third nature, merely gestured at here, waits for the analysis of disposedness (§ 29) and, ultimately, for the later Heidegger's physis.

The twelfth unit widens the reference-totality to others and the public world, then secures the result against subjectivism. In simple craft conditions the work carries also the reference to the wearer and user: it is cut to his body; he "is" co-present in the work's coming-to-be. In the production of ready-made goods this constitutive reference is by no means lacking — only indeterminate, pointing to the arbitrary, the average. With the work, then, there is encountered not only ready-to-hand being but also being of Dasein's mode of being, for whom the produced becomes ready-to-hand in its concern; and in one with this, the world is encountered in which wearers and consumers live — which is at once ours. The work of concern is ready-to-hand not only in the domestic world of the workshop but in the public world; with the public world, environmental nature is discovered and accessible to everyone: in roads, streets, bridges, buildings, concern has discovered nature in a determinate direction — a covered platform reckons with bad weather, public lighting with darkness, that is, with the specific alternation of the presence and absence of daylight, the "position of the sun"; in clocks a determinate constellation in the world-system is reckoned with, so that in looking at the clock we tacitly make use of the "position of the sun," by which the official astronomical regulation of time-measurement is carried out. It belongs to the essence of the discovering function of absorbed concern that, according to the manner of absorption, the innerworldly beings brought along in the work — in its constitutive references — remain discoverable in varying degrees of explicitness and varying range of circumspective penetration. The mode of being of these beings is readiness-to-hand — which, however, must not be understood as a mere character of apprehension, as though such "aspects" were talked onto proximally encountered "beings," as though a world-stuff at first present-at-hand in itself were in this way "subjectively colored." An interpretation so directed overlooks that this would require beings to have been beforehand understood and discovered as purely present-at-hand, with priority and leadership in the course of discovering dealings with the "world" — which already contradicts the ontological sense of knowing, exhibited as a founded mode of being-in-the-world: knowing first presses forward, beyond the ready-to-hand of concern, to the laying-free of what is merely still present-at-hand. Readiness-to-hand is the ontological-categorial determination of beings as they are "in themselves." But the ready-to-hand "is given," after all, only on the ground of the present-at-hand — does it follow, this thesis once conceded, that readiness-to-hand is ontologically founded in presence-at-hand? The long paragraph accomplishes three things. It discovers others inside the tool-analysis — the wearer in the fitted shoe, the average consumer in mass production, the public in the platform — so that being-with (Chapter Four) is phenomenally prepared before it is named: the workshop was never solipsistic. It plants the clock and the sun's position — the seed of § 80's analysis of world-time and public time-reckoning. And its closing dialectic executes the boldest transvaluation yet: the "in itself" is claimed for the ready-to-hand (the subjective-coloring reading is refuted by § 13's founding order — the bare thing is the later product, not the prior stuff), whereupon Heidegger himself voices the strongest counter ("no ready-to-hand without present-at-hand") and leaves it as a question: ontic dependence, yes — but ontological founding? The question hangs deliberately; § 16 and § 18 answer it.

The closing unit turns the section's success into the chapter's problem — and, in the folded-in note, signs its provenance. Even if the further ontological interpretation confirms readiness-to-hand as the mode of being of the beings first discovered innerworldly, even if its originality over against pure presence-at-hand can be demonstrated — is the least thing thereby won for the ontological understanding of the world-phenomenon? In interpreting these innerworldly beings we have always already "presupposed" world: joining these beings together does not yield, as a sum, something like "world." Does any path lead at all from the being of these beings to the exhibition of the world-phenomenon? The note attached to the question records that the author has repeatedly presented the environing-world analysis, and in general the "hermeneutics of facticity" of Dasein, in his lecture courses since the winter semester of 1919/20. The self-objection is exact and structural: § 14's argument against nature applies to equipment too — the ready-to-hand is also innerworldly, so no ontology of it, however superior, is yet an ontology of the world; the totality kept being presupposed (the room, the workshop, the public world) at every step. That presupposed wherein is the quarry, and § 16 will hunt it where it flashes up — in breakdown. The footnote, meanwhile, quietly documents eight years of priority: the tool-analysis and the phrase "hermeneutics of facticity" descend from the earliest Freiburg courses — the book's most celebrated pages are its oldest.

###### § 16. The Worldly Character of the Environing World Announcing Itself in Innerworldly Beings

The opening unit poses the section's question with full precision. World is itself not an innerworldly being, and yet it determines those beings so thoroughly that they can be encountered, and discovered beings can show themselves in their being, only insofar as world "is given." But how "is" world "given"? If Dasein is ontically constituted by being-in-the-world, and an understanding of its own being — however indeterminate — belongs just as essentially to it, does it not have an understanding of world, a pre-ontological one, which lacks and can lack explicit ontological insights? Does not something like world show itself for concernful being-in-the-world with the innerworldly beings it encounters — with their innerworldliness? Does this phenomenon not come into a pre-phenomenological view, does it not always already stand in one, without demanding thematic ontological interpretation? Has Dasein itself, within the compass of its concernful absorption in ready-to-hand equipment, a possibility of being in which, along with the innerworldly beings of its concern, their worldhood in a certain way lights up (aufleuchtet)? The battery of questions converts § 15's impasse into a search-warrant: since world is presupposed by all encounter yet never an item encountered, it can only be caught where it flashes for pre-ontological experience itself — and the verb aufleuchten announces the section's whole method: not construction but the exploitation of moments when the operative background momentarily glows.

The second unit states the plan in one sentence: if such possibilities of Dasein's being can be exhibited within concernful dealings, a way opens to pursue the phenomenon that thus lights up — to attempt, as it were, to "arrest" it and interrogate it as to the structures showing themselves in it. The hunting metaphor (stellen — to bring to bay) is candid about the difficulty: the phenomenon appears only in passing, in the modification of dealings, and must be held still long enough to be questioned.

The third unit produces the first such modification: conspicuousness. Among the modes of concern are those that let the beings of concern be encountered so that the worldly character of the innerworldly comes to the fore. The proximally ready-to-hand can be met in concern as unusable, not fitted for its determinate use: the tool turns out damaged, the material unsuitable — equipment is in each case still ready-to-hand here. But what discovers the unusability is not the observing ascertainment of properties but the circumspection of using dealings: in such discovering of unusability, the equipment becomes conspicuous (fällt auf). Conspicuousness gives the ready-to-hand equipment in a certain unreadiness-to-hand: the unusable just lies there — it shows itself as an equipment-thing that looks thus and so, and that in its readiness-to-hand, as so looking, was constantly present-at-hand as well. Pure presence-at-hand announces itself (meldet sich) in the equipment — only to withdraw again into the readiness-to-hand of what concern attends to, namely of what is under repair. This presence-at-hand of the unusable does not yet lack all readiness-to-hand whatsoever; equipment so present-at-hand is not yet a thing merely occurring somewhere — the damage is not yet a mere alteration of a thing, a change of properties simply occurring in something present-at-hand. Every qualification is doing ontological work. Circumspection, not inspection, discovers the defect — breakdown is registered practically before any property is observed. What surfaces in the broken tool is presence-at-hand announcing itself within readiness-to-hand: a flickering of one mode of being through another, promptly re-absorbed when repair begins. And the double "not yet" guards the phenomenon's fineness: the broken hammer is neither ready-to-hand as before nor a mere physical object — it occupies the revealing in-between the tradition's two-term ontology cannot register.

The fourth unit gives the second modification: obtrusiveness. Concernful dealings do not only strike upon the unusable within what is already ready-to-hand; they also find what is missing — what is not merely not "handy" but not "to hand" at all. Missing something in this way discovers again — as a coming-upon something un-ready-to-hand — the ready-to-hand in a certain merely-being-present-at-hand: the ready-to-hand enters, in the noticing of the un-ready-to-hand, the mode of obtrusiveness (Aufdringlichkeit). The more urgently the missing item is needed, the more authentically it is encountered in its unreadiness-to-hand, the more obtrusive does what is ready-to-hand become — so much so that it seems to lose the character of readiness-to-hand: it reveals itself as merely present-at-hand, as what cannot be budged without the missing piece. The helpless standing-before-it discovers, as a deficient mode of concern, the mere-presence-at-hand of something ready-to-hand. The phenomenology is exact and easily verified: when the one needed tool is absent, everything present loses its serviceability-glow and stares back inertly — absence de-worlds the present. The escalation law (more urgency, more obtrusiveness) shows that the modification is indexed to concern, not to the things: it is the frustrated in-order-to that converts workshop into clutter.

The fifth unit gives the third: what stands in the way. In dealings with the world of concern, the un-ready-to-hand can be encountered not only as unusable or as simply missing, but as un-ready-to-hand precisely without being missing or unusable — as what "lies in the way" of concern. That to which concern cannot turn, for which it "has no time," is un-ready-to-hand in the manner of the not-belonging-here, the unattended-to.

The sixth unit names it: this un-ready-to-hand disturbs, and makes visible the obstinacy (Aufsässigkeit) of what must be attended to first and beforehand; with this obstinacy the presence-at-hand of the ready-to-hand announces itself in a new way — as the being of what still lies before us and calls for settling. The third mode completes a small system: the broken (conspicuous), the absent (obtrusive), the obstructive (obstinate) — defect, lack, and hindrance — three ways breakdown can enter the reference-whole, each precipitating presence-at-hand in a different key: the merely-lying-there, the immovable, the still-outstanding.

The seventh unit gathers the three and marks their limit. The modes of conspicuousness, obtrusiveness, and obstinacy have the function of bringing to the fore, in the ready-to-hand, the character of presence-at-hand. But the ready-to-hand is not thereby merely observed and gaped at as present-at-hand: the presence-at-hand that makes itself known is still bound in the readiness-to-hand of equipment; the equipment does not yet veil itself into mere things. It becomes "gear" in the sense of what one would like to get rid of — but in such a tendency to discard, the ready-to-hand shows itself as still ready-to-hand in its unswerving presence-at-hand. The unit fixes the crucial half-way status: breakdown is not yet theory — the annoying object of the stalled workshop is not the neutral object of science (that requires the fuller de-worlding of § 69b); presence-at-hand here appears within concern, as the recalcitrance of the practical, not as the residue of a completed abstraction.

The eighth unit asks what any of this buys. What is this pointer to the modified encountering of the ready-to-hand — in which its presence-at-hand unveils itself — supposed to accomplish for clarifying the world-phenomenon? Even with the analysis of this modification we still stand with the being of the innerworldly; we have not yet come nearer the world-phenomenon. It is not yet grasped — but we have now brought ourselves into the possibility of bringing it into view. The self-audit is § 2's bookkeeping discipline again: the breakdown-modes as such are still innerworldly ontology; their yield is positional — a vantage, not yet a capture.

The ninth unit makes the capture. In conspicuousness, obtrusiveness, and obstinacy the ready-to-hand in a certain way loses its readiness-to-hand — but this readiness-to-hand is itself understood, though unthematically, in dealings with the ready-to-hand: it does not simply vanish, but in the conspicuousness of the unusable it takes its leave (verabschiedet sich), as it were. Readiness-to-hand shows itself once more — and precisely therein the worldly character of the ready-to-hand also shows itself. This is the section's pivot, and its logic deserves slow statement: what breakdown makes visible is not primarily presence-at-hand but readiness-to-hand itself in departure — the mode of being that had functioned invisibly becomes, in its withdrawal, momentarily conspicuous as what is being lost. The farewell-metaphor is precise: one sees the guest clearly only at the door. And because readiness-to-hand is constituted by references into a totality, its leave-taking drags the totality — and with it worldhood — into the same fleeting visibility.

The tenth unit spells out the mechanism through reference. The structure of the being of the ready-to-hand as equipment is determined by references. The peculiar and self-evident "in-itself" of the nearest "things" is encountered in the concern that uses them without expressly heeding them — and that can strike upon the unusable. That equipment is unusable means: the constitutive reference of the in-order-to to a for-this (Dazu) is disturbed. The references themselves are not observed; they are "there" in concern's placing-itself-under them. But in a disturbance of reference — in unusability-for... — the reference becomes explicit: not yet, even now, as an ontological structure, but ontically, for the circumspection that stumbles on the damaged tool. With this circumspective awakening of the reference to the respective for-this, the for-this itself comes into view, and with it the work-context, the whole "workshop" — and indeed as that wherein concern has always already been dwelling. The equipment-context lights up not as something never seen, but as a whole constantly sighted in advance in circumspection; and with this whole, world announces itself. The paragraph delivers what § 15 could only presuppose: the reference-totality, always operative and never thematic, becomes ontically explicit exactly and only at its tear — the workshop is seen as workshop when work stops. The final clause is the section's harvest in five words: with this whole, world announces itself — the wherein of dwelling flashes up as the background the breakdown foregrounds.

The eleventh unit runs the same derivation through absence, and mints the book's word for the result. Likewise, the missing of something ready-to-hand whose everyday being-at-hand was so self-evident that we never even took notice of it is a breach of the reference-contexts discovered in circumspection: circumspection strikes into emptiness and only now sees what the missing item was ready-to-hand for and with. Again the environing world announces itself. What thus lights up is itself no ready-to-hand thing among others, still less something present-at-hand that founds the ready-to-hand equipment: it is in the "there" before all ascertainment and observation. It is itself inaccessible to circumspection, insofar as circumspection always goes toward beings — but it is for circumspection always already disclosed. "Disclose" (erschließen) and "disclosedness" (Erschlossenheit) are henceforth used terminologically, meaning "to unlock" — "unlockedness"; "disclose" therefore never means anything like "to obtain indirectly by inference." The terminological baptism, tucked into a parenthesis, is among the book's most consequential: Erschlossenheit — the unlocked openness within which beings can be met — receives its charter here, expressly quarantined from Schluß, inference (world is no conclusion from data), and expressly placed before all ascertainment: prior to circumspection's every act, inaccessible to it as an object, presupposed by it as its open field. Truth (§ 44), the Da of Dasein (§ 28), and the whole doctrine of disclosedness stand on this paragraph.

The twelfth unit derives the everyday invisibility of world as a transcendental condition. That the world does not "consist" of the ready-to-hand shows itself, among other things, in this: the lighting-up of world in the interpreted modes of concern goes together with a de-worlding of the ready-to-hand, so that mere-presence-at-hand comes to the fore in it. If, in everyday concern with the "environing world," ready-to-hand equipment is to be encounterable in its "being-in-itself," then the references and reference-totalities in which circumspection "is absorbed" must remain unthematic for circumspection — and all the more for any un-circumspective, "thematic" grasping. The world's not-announcing-itself is the condition of the possibility of the ready-to-hand's not stepping out of its inconspicuousness; and therein is constituted the phenomenal structure of the being-in-itself of these beings. The double thesis is elegant and strict: world shows only as things de-world (visibility of the one is bought with the mode-loss of the other), and, conversely, the smooth in-itself of everyday things requires the world's silence — the background must hold its peace for the tool to recede into serviceable inconspicuousness. Concealment here is not a defect of world but its proper workday mode: worldhood functions best incognito.

The thirteenth unit converts the privatives into positives and settles the "in itself." Privative expressions like inconspicuousness, unobtrusiveness, unobstinacy mean a positive phenomenal character of the being of the proximally ready-to-hand: these "un-"s mean the character of the ready-to-hand's holding-itself-in — what we have in view with being-in-itself, which, characteristically, we "proximally" ascribe to the present-at-hand, as the thematically ascertainable. Oriented primarily and exclusively to the present-at-hand, the "in-itself" cannot be ontologically clarified at all; yet an interpretation must be demanded if talk of the "in-itself" is to carry ontological weight. One appeals, mostly with ontic emphasis, to this in-itself of being — and with phenomenal right; but the ontic appeal does not already satisfy the claim of the ontological assertion supposedly given with it. The analysis so far already makes clear: the being-in-itself of innerworldly beings becomes ontologically graspable only on the ground of the world-phenomenon. The resolution of § 15's dangling paradox arrives: in-itselfness is the positive self-holding-in of the serviceable — constituted by the world's reticence just derived — so that, far from anchoring realism against world, the "in itself" presupposes world for its very sense. Realism's phenomenal right is granted (things are encountered as in themselves) and its ontological pretension refused (that encounter is world-founded): the exact template for § 43's treatment of reality.

The fourteenth unit draws the conclusion about disclosure and priority. If world can light up in a certain way, it must in general be disclosed: with the accessibility of innerworldly ready-to-hand beings for circumspective concern, world is in each case already pre-disclosed (vorerschlossen). World is accordingly something "wherein" Dasein as a being always already was, upon which it can only ever come back in every somehow explicit coming-toward. The temporal grammar of the last sentence carries the doctrine: world is never first arrived at, only returned to — the always-already of disclosure means that every explicit approach to world (including this chapter's) is a homecoming, and Dasein's familiarity with world precedes every act within it.

The fifteenth unit names that familiarity and re-poses the question at depth. Being-in-the-world, according to the interpretation so far, means: the unthematic, circumspective absorption in the references constitutive for the readiness-to-hand of the equipmental whole. Concern is in each case already as it is on the ground of a familiarity (Vertrautheit) with world; in this familiarity Dasein can lose itself to what it encounters innerworldly and be taken in by it. What is it with which Dasein is familiar — why can the worldly character of the innerworldly light up? How, more closely, is the reference-totality to be understood, in which circumspection "moves," and whose possible breaches thrust forward the presence-at-hand of beings? The unit binds § 12's etymology (being-in as dwelling-familiarity) to § 16's findings: familiarity with world is what absorption presupposes and what breakdown momentarily exposes — and the question "familiar with what?" is exactly calibrated: not with things (they are what one loses oneself to) but with the wherein; § 18's answer will be significance.

The closing unit hands the questions on: answering them — questions aimed at working out the phenomenon and problem of worldhood — demands a more concrete analysis of the structures into whose built-up context they inquire. The referral is architectural, not evasive: reference has been exhibited (§ 15) and caught functioning (§ 16); its ontological constitution — what kind of structure a reference is, and how references compose the wherein — is precisely §§ 17–18's assignment.

###### § 17. Reference and Signs

The opening unit takes stock and sets the task. In the provisional interpretation of the being-structure of the ready-to-hand (of "equipment"), the phenomenon of reference became visible — but so much in outline that the necessity was stressed of uncovering this merely indicated phenomenon with regard to its ontological provenance. It became clear, moreover, that reference and reference-totality will in some sense be constitutive for worldhood itself; and world has so far been seen to light up only in and for determinate ways of environmental concern with the ready-to-hand — with its readiness-to-hand. The further we penetrate into the understanding of the being of innerworldly beings, the broader and more secure becomes the phenomenal soil for laying the world-phenomenon free. The strategic logic is stated without disguise: the sign-analysis to come is instrumental — a deepening of the reference-phenomenon in the service of worldhood — which is why the section will end by carefully subordinating signs to reference rather than the reverse.

The second unit selects the specimen: we again take our point of departure from the being of the ready-to-hand, now intending to grasp the phenomenon of reference itself more sharply; to this end we attempt an ontological analysis of an equipment in which "references" can be found in a manifold sense — such "equipment" we find in signs. The choice is methodologically cunning: signs are equipment whose very service is referring, so in them reference is doubled — present both as equipmental constitution and as function — and the analysis can pry the two apart.

The third unit lays out the field and issues the first warning. Signs are at first themselves items of equipment whose specific equipment-character consists in showing (Zeigen): such are waymarkers, boundary-stones, the storm-ball for shipping, signals, flags, mourning-signs, and the like. Showing can be determined as a "kind" of referring; and referring, taken extremely formally, is a relating (Beziehen). But relation does not function as the genus for "kinds" of references that would differentiate themselves into sign, symbol, expression, signification: relation is a formal determination that becomes directly readable, by way of "formalization," in any kind of context whatsoever, of any material content and mode of being — the note citing Husserl's doctrine of formalization (Ideen I § 10 ff., and already the Logical Investigations) for exactly this distinction between formalizing and generalizing. The warning inverts the expected order of analysis: one cannot ascend from sign and reference to "relation" as their common essence, because relation is not a highest genus but a formal skeleton, obtainable from anything by emptying it — Husserl's own insight (formalization is not generalization) turned to Heidegger's purpose: the formal is ontologically last, not first.

The fourth unit fixes the extensional grid and stakes a radical claim. Every reference is a relation, but not every relation is a reference; every showing is a reference, but not every referring is a showing — hence every showing is a relation, but not every relating a showing. Therewith the formal-general character of relation comes to light: for investigating the phenomena of reference, sign, or even signification, nothing is gained by characterizing them as relations. In the end it must even be shown that "relation" itself, because of its formal-general character, has its ontological origin in a reference. The chain of inclusions (showing within reference within relation) is bookkeeping; the last sentence is the bombshell: the formal concept of relation — the backbone of logic and mathematics — is declared ontologically derivative from reference, i.e., from the in-order-to structure of concern. Formalization itself, this implies, is a founded accomplishment of being-in-the-world; the promissory note is never fully redeemed in the book, but it marks how far the founding claims of the tool-analysis reach.

The fifth unit bounds the inquiry. Restricting itself to interpreting the sign in distinction from the reference-phenomenon, the analysis cannot, even within this restriction, adequately investigate the closed manifold of possible signs: among signs there are indications, fore-signs and back-signs, marks and distinguishing-signs, whose showing differs in each case, quite apart from what serves as the sign; and from these "signs" are to be separated: trace, remnant, monument, document, testimony, symbol, expression, appearance, signification. These phenomena are easily formalized thanks to their formal relational character; we today are especially inclined, following the guiding thread of such "relation," to subject all beings to an "interpretation" that always "fits" because at bottom it says nothing — as little as the easily handled schema of form and content. The taxonomy is a map of a whole intellectual landscape (from Anzeichen — Husserl's First Investigation term — through the symbol-theories of the day), and the closing thrust generalizes § 7 B: schemata that fit everything (relation, form/content) explain nothing — vacuity as the price of universality, the standing charge against formal frameworks doing ontology's work.

The sixth unit produces the celebrated example. As exemplar we choose a sign that will later serve as exemplary in another respect: motor-cars have recently been fitted with an adjustable red arrow whose position shows, at a crossing for instance, which way the car will take; the driver regulates the arrow's position. This sign is an item of equipment ready-to-hand not only in the driver's concern (steering): those not travelling in the car — and precisely they — make use of this equipment, namely by giving way to the appropriate side or halting. The sign is innerworldly ready-to-hand within the whole equipment-context of vehicles and traffic-regulations; as equipment, this showing-equipment is constituted by reference — it has the character of the in-order-to, its determinate serviceability: it is for showing. This showing of the sign can be grasped as "referring" — but note well: this "referring" as showing is not the ontological structure of the sign as equipment. The turn-signal is chosen with both eyes open (its second career comes at § 79's analysis of everyday time-interpretation): a sign publicly ready-to-hand, addressed to the non-users above all, embedded in a regulation-totality — every feature the analysis needs. And the closing distinction is sprung immediately: the sign refers twice over, and the two must not be conflated.

The seventh unit executes the disentangling. "Referring" as showing is grounded rather in the being-structure of equipment, in serviceability-for. Serviceability does not yet make a being a sign: the hammer too is constituted by a serviceability, without thereby becoming a sign. The "reference" showing is the ontic concretion of the what-for of a serviceability, determining an equipment to this what-for; the reference "serviceability-for," by contrast, is an ontological-categorial determination of equipment as equipment. That the what-for of serviceability receives its concretion in showing is accidental to the equipment-constitution as such. Already in this example the difference between reference as serviceability and reference as showing becomes roughly visible: the two so little coincide that only in their unity do they make possible the concretion of a determinate kind of equipment. And yet — as surely as showing differs in principle from referring as equipment-constitution — the sign has undeniably a peculiar, even distinctive relation to the mode of being of the environmentally ready-to-hand equipment-whole and its worldly character: showing-equipment has a preeminent use in concernful dealings, and it cannot suffice ontologically to note the fact — ground and sense of this preeminence must be clarified. The distinction is the section's load-bearing wall: serviceability (ontological, constitutive of all equipment) versus showing (ontic, one serviceability among possible ones — the sign's trade, as driving nails is the hammer's). Its point is anti-semiotic in advance: reference is not a sign-relation writ large; signs are a special employment of reference — so no semiotics can ground the ontology of world, though the sign's special status (still to be explained) is conceded as a genuine phenomenon.

The eighth unit asks how signs are properly encountered — and answers from the traffic-crossing. What does a sign's showing amount to? The answer comes only by determining the appropriate manner of dealing with showing-equipment, in which its readiness-to-hand too must become genuinely graspable. Oriented to the arrow: the appropriate comportment (being) toward the encountered sign is giving way or halting with respect to the oncoming car that carries it. Giving way, as taking a direction, belongs essentially to Dasein's being-in-the-world, which is always somehow directed and under way — standing and staying are only limit cases of this directed "under way." The sign addresses itself to a specifically "spatial" being-in-the-world. The sign is precisely not authentically "grasped" when we stare at it and ascertain it as an occurring pointer-thing; even if we follow the arrow's direction with our gaze and look at something present-at-hand within the region into which it points, the sign is not authentically encountered even then. It turns itself toward the circumspection of concernful dealings, so that circumspection, following the sign's directive, brings in such going-along the respective aroundness of the environing world into an explicit "survey" (Übersicht). The circumspective surveying does not grasp the ready-to-hand; it wins, rather, an orientation within the environing world. Another possibility of equipment-experience: the arrow is encountered as equipment belonging to the car, without its specific equipment-character being discovered — what and how it shows may remain wholly indeterminate, and yet what is encountered is no pure thing: thing-experience, over against the nearest coming-upon a manifoldly indeterminate equipment-manifold, requires its own determinateness. Three findings stack up. Sign-uptake is practical response, not reading-off: the arrow is understood in the swerve, not in the stare — even correct gaze-following (looking where it points) misses it, since its showing terminates in comportment, not in an object. Its yield is named exactly: orientation — an explicit survey of the around — which is why signs are preeminent among tools: they thematize the environment that other equipment merely presupposes. And the closing observation completes § 15's inversion: indeterminate equipment, not the bare thing, is the default of experience; thinghood is an achievement requiring its own determinateness.

The ninth unit generalizes the yield across the sign-taxonomy. Signs of the kind described let ready-to-hand beings be encountered — more precisely, let a context of them become accessible in such a way that concernful dealings give themselves and secure an orientation. The sign is not a thing standing in a showing relation to another thing, but an equipment that explicitly raises an equipmental whole into circumspection, so that in one with this the worldly character of the ready-to-hand announces itself. In indication and fore-sign, "what is coming" "shows itself" — not as something merely occurring that gets added to what is already present-at-hand: "what is coming" is that for which we prepare ourselves, or "were not prepared" insofar as we were occupied with something else. In the back-sign, what has come to pass and run its course becomes circumspectively accessible; the mark shows "where" one is at in each case. Signs show primarily and always that "wherein" one lives, where concern dwells, what involvement (Bewandtnis) things have. The definition — sign as the equipment that raises an equipmental whole into explicit circumspection — grounds § 16's finding institutionally: what breakdown does by accident, the sign does by trade; both make the background momentarily foreground. The temporal registers of the taxonomy (the coming, the past, the where-one-stands) all resolve into the same primary showing: the wherein of living — and in the last clause the next section's key word, Bewandtnis, slips in avant la lettre.

The tenth unit confirms the account through sign-institution. The peculiar equipment-character of signs becomes especially clear in "sign-institution" (Zeichenstiftung): it is accomplished in and out of a circumspective foresight that needs the ready-to-hand possibility of letting the particular environing world announce itself, at any time, through something ready-to-hand. Now, to the being of the innerworldly proximally ready-to-hand belongs the described character of self-holding-in, of not-stepping-forth; hence circumspective dealings need ready-to-hand equipment that takes over, in its equipment-character, the "work" of letting the ready-to-hand become conspicuous. The production of such equipment (signs) must therefore be mindful of their conspicuousness — and even as conspicuous they are not left present-at-hand at random, but are "installed" in a determinate way with a view to easy accessibility. The argument closes a beautiful circle with § 16: because inconspicuousness is constitutive for the ready-to-hand (§ 16's positive privatives), circumspection requires a class of equipment professionally exempted from it — signs are engineered conspicuousness, breakdown domesticated and put on retainer.

The eleventh unit deepens institution to discovery. Sign-institution need not proceed by producing an equipment not yet ready-to-hand at all: signs arise also in taking something already ready-to-hand as a sign — and in this mode sign-institution reveals a still more original sense. Showing does not merely procure the circumspectively oriented availability of an equipmental whole and of the environing world in general; sign-instituting can even discover in the first place. What is taken as a sign becomes accessible only through its readiness-to-hand: when, in husbandry, the south wind "counts" as a sign of rain, this "counting" — or the "value adhering" to this being — is no bonus added to something already present-at-hand in itself, an air-current with a determinate geographical direction. As this merely occurring thing, as which it may be meteorologically accessible, the south wind is never proximally present-at-hand, occasionally taking over the function of a fore-sign: rather, the circumspection of husbandry, in the manner of taking-account, first discovers the south wind in its being. The south-wind passage is § 15's value-critique cashed at its strongest test-case: even where the tradition's picture (natural fact plus attached significance) seems irresistible, the order runs the other way — the farmer's rain-sign is what the wind first is; the meteorologist's air-current is the later, de-worlded product. Discovery, not decoration: taking-as-sign is a mode of first access to the being.

The twelfth unit meets the obvious objection. But — one will reply — what gets taken as a sign must surely have become accessible in itself beforehand, grasped prior to the sign-institution. Certainly, it must already be findable in some way; the question is only how, in this antecedent encountering, the being is discovered — whether as a pure occurring thing, or rather as un-understood equipment, as something ready-to-hand with which one hitherto knew "not what to do," which accordingly still veiled itself from circumspection. Here again one must not interpret the equipment-characters not yet circumspectively discovered as mere thinghood, pregiven for a grasping of the merely present-at-hand. The reply refines the ontology of the unfamiliar: prior to its sign-career the wind was not a neutral thing but undetermined equipment — the not-yet-understood is a privative mode of the ready-to-hand, not a specimen of the present-at-hand; § 15's default (indeterminate equipment before determinate things) holds even for what has no use yet.

The thirteenth unit tests the account on the knotted handkerchief. The being-ready-to-hand of signs in everyday dealings, and the conspicuousness — producible with various intents and in various ways — belonging to signs, document not only the inconspicuousness constitutive for the proximally ready-to-hand: the sign itself draws its conspicuousness from the inconspicuousness of the everyday, "self-evident" ready-to-hand equipmental whole — for example, the familiar "knot in the handkerchief" as a memory-sign. What it is to show is in each case something to be attended to in the circumspection of everydayness; and this sign can show many and the most heterogeneous things. To the breadth of what is showable in such a sign corresponds the narrowness of its intelligibility and use: not only is it, as a sign, mostly ready-to-hand only for its "institutor" — it can become inaccessible to him himself, so that a second sign is needed for the possible circumspective usability of the first. The knot, unusable as a sign, thereby does not lose its sign-character; it acquires, rather, the disquieting obtrusiveness of something most closely ready-to-hand. The homely example carries a precise law — showable-breadth inversely proportional to intelligibility (a maximally indeterminate sign is minimally public) — and its punch line is a § 16 breakdown inside § 17: the forgotten knot is the sign's own mode of conspicuous failure, nagging precisely because its showing-function survives its unusability.

The fourteenth unit takes up the anthropological temptation and turns it into a lesson on formal ideas. One might be tempted to illustrate the preeminent role of signs in everyday concern, for the understanding of world itself, by the abundant "sign"-use of primitive Dasein — fetish and magic. Certainly the sign-institution underlying such use is not accomplished with theoretical intent nor by way of theoretical speculation; sign-use here remains wholly within an "immediate" being-in-the-world. But on closer inspection it becomes clear that interpreting fetish and magic along the guiding thread of the idea of sign in general does not suffice to grasp the kind of "being-ready-to-hand" of beings encountered in the primitive world. With regard to the sign-phenomenon one could offer this interpretation: for primitive man the sign coincides with what is shown — the sign itself can stand for the shown not merely in the sense of replacing it, but so that the sign always is the shown. Yet this remarkable coincidence does not lie in the sign-thing's having already undergone a certain "objectification," being experienced as a pure thing and transposed with the shown into the same region of being of the present-at-hand: the "coinciding" is no identification of things previously isolated, but a not-yet-becoming-free of the sign from the signified. Such sign-use is still wholly absorbed in being toward the shown, so that a sign as such cannot yet detach itself at all; the coincidence is grounded not in a first objectification but in the complete absence of one. This means, though: signs are then not discovered as equipment at all — in the end, the innerworldly "ready-to-hand" of the primitive world may not have the mode of being of equipment at all. Perhaps even this ontological guiding thread (readiness-to-hand and equipment) can accomplish nothing for an interpretation of the primitive world — though certainly the ontology of thinghood even less. But if an understanding of being is constitutive for primitive Dasein and the primitive world in general, then it is all the more urgent to work out the "formal" idea of worldhood — of a phenomenon modifiable in such a way that all ontological assertions saying that, in a pregiven phenomenal context, something is not yet or no longer such-and-such receive a positive phenomenal sense from what it is not. The passage is § 11 made concrete and radicalized: the magic-world resists not only thing-ontology but possibly the tool-ontology just built — Heidegger volunteers the limit of his own analysis. The account of the fetish is itself a small phenomenological gem (the sign not yet free of the signified: fusion by absence of objectification, not identification after it), and the conclusion converts the anthropological problem into a methodological demand: worldhood must be formal enough that "not yet equipment" and "no longer equipment" are positive determinations — the privative method (§ 10 on life) given its charter for the theory of world.

The fifteenth unit begins the closing triad: showing, as a possible concretion of the what-for of a serviceability, is founded in the equipment-structure in general, in the in-order-to (reference). The sixteenth adds: the sign's showing belongs, as equipment-character of a ready-to-hand thing, to an equipmental totality, to a reference-context. The two theses bank the seventh and sixth units respectively: reference founds showing (never the reverse); and the sign never shows alone — its showing is emplaced in the totality it serves.

The seventeenth unit states the third relation and re-launches the inquiry. The sign is not only ready-to-hand with other equipment: in its readiness-to-hand the environing world becomes in each case explicitly accessible for circumspection. The sign is something ontically ready-to-hand that, as this determinate equipment, functions at the same time as something that indicates the ontological structure of readiness-to-hand, reference-totality, and worldhood — herein is rooted the preeminence of this ready-to-hand thing within the circumspectively attended environing world. Hence reference itself, if it is to be ontologically the foundation for signs, cannot itself be conceived as a sign: reference is not the ontic determinateness of something ready-to-hand, since it constitutes readiness-to-hand itself. In what sense is reference the ontological "presupposition" of the ready-to-hand, and how far is it, as this ontological foundation, at once a constituent of worldhood in general? The triad's crown explains, at last, the sign's promised preeminence: the sign is the ontic being whose trade is to indicate the ontological — a worldly thing that points at worldhood — which is exactly why the analysis chose it and exactly why it must now be left behind: reference, constituting readiness-to-hand, cannot be one more sign (no semiotic regress), and the question of its own constitution — reference as presupposition of the ready-to-hand and constituent of worldhood — is handed intact to § 18, where involvement and significance will answer it.

###### § 18. Involvement and Significance; the Worldhood of the World

The opening unit gathers the accumulated findings into the section's question. The ready-to-hand is encountered innerworldly; its being, readiness-to-hand, thus stands in some ontological relation to world and worldhood. World is in everything ready-to-hand always already "there"; world is antecedently discovered, though unthematically, with everything encountered, and can also light up in certain ways of environmental dealings. World is that from out of which the ready-to-hand is ready-to-hand. How can world let the ready-to-hand be encountered? The analysis so far showed: what is encountered innerworldly is freed (freigegeben) in its being for concernful circumspection, for taking-account. What does this antecedent freeing mean, and how is it to be understood as an ontological distinction of world? What problems does the question of worldhood pose? The new verb carries the section: Freigabe, freeing or releasing — world does not contain beings but frees them for encounter; § 18's whole business is to say what this liberation is and who accomplishes it.

The second unit clears the last categorial obstacle and coins the master term. The equipment-constitution of the ready-to-hand was indicated as reference. How can world free beings of this mode of being with respect to their being — why are these beings encountered first? As determinate references we named serviceability-for, detrimentality, usability, and the like; the what-for of a serviceability and the wherefore of a usability predelineate in each case the possible concretion of the reference. But the "showing" of the sign, the "hammering" of the hammer are not properties of beings — they are not properties at all, if this title is to designate the ontological structure of a possible determinateness of things. The ready-to-hand has at most suitabilities and unsuitabilities, and its "properties" are still bound up in these, as presence-at-hand, as a possible mode of being of something ready-to-hand, is bound up in readiness-to-hand. Serviceability (reference) as equipment-constitution, however, is no suitability of a being either, but the being-level condition of the possibility of its being determined by suitabilities. What then does reference mean? That the being of the ready-to-hand has the structure of reference means: it has in itself the character of being-referred (Verwiesenheit). Beings are discovered with a view to this — that as the beings they are, they are referred to something: with them, things rest at something, es hat mit ihm bei etwas sein Bewenden. The character of being of the ready-to-hand is involvement (Bewandtnis); in involvement lies: letting something be involved with something at something (bewenden lassen mit etwas bei etwas) — the relation of the "with... at..." is what the term reference indicates. The paragraph makes two moves of rank. First, a strict three-level ontology of the tool: properties (categorial determinateness of things) are bound within suitabilities (the tool's fitness or unfitness for), which are in turn made possible by serviceability (the constitutive reference) — so the tradition's property-ontology stands two derivations away from the tool's being. Second, the baptism of Bewandtnis: an almost untranslatable everyday idiom (what something is involved with, how matters stand with it, what it comes to) chosen precisely because it names being-referred as a way of being — the hammer's being is its being-bound-into the "with... at..." structure, its resting-at hammering.

The third unit unfolds involvement into its famous chain and finds its anchor. Involvement is the being of innerworldly beings, upon which they are in each case already first freed; with beings as beings there is in each case an involvement — and that there is one is the ontological determination of the being of these beings, not an ontic assertion about them. That at which the involvement rests is the what-for of serviceability, the wherefore of usability; and with the what-for there can in turn be an involvement: with this ready-to-hand thing, which we therefore call a hammer, the involvement rests at hammering; with hammering, at making-fast; with making-fast, at protection against bad weather; and this protection "is" for the sake of (um-willen) Dasein's sheltering — that is, for the sake of a possibility of its being. Which involvement a ready-to-hand thing has is in each case predelineated from the involvement-totality: the involvement-totality that constitutes, for instance, the ready-to-hand in a workshop in its readiness-to-hand is "earlier" than the individual equipment — likewise that of a farmstead with all its gear and grounds. But the involvement-totality itself goes back ultimately to a what-for at which there is no further involvement — which is itself not a being of the ready-to-hand's mode of being within a world, but a being whose being is determined as being-in-the-world, to whose constitution worldhood itself belongs. This primary what-for is no for-this, no possible at-which of an involvement: the primary "what-for" is a for-the-sake-of-which (Worum-willen), and the for-the-sake-of always concerns the being of Dasein, for which in its being this being itself is essentially at stake. The indicated connection leading from involvement to Dasein's being as the authentic and sole for-the-sake-of-which shall not yet be pursued further; first, "letting-be-involved" demands clarification enough to bring worldhood into determinateness. This is the structural heart of the chapter, and its two theorems must be held apart. The regress theorem: the chain of for-thises (hammering, fastening, sheltering) cannot run to infinity or terminate in a super-tool — it terminates in a possibility of Dasein's being; the whole workshop hangs from an existentiell "for the sake of dwelling," so instrumentality is anchored in existence, § 4's "es geht um" formula returning as the totality's keystone. The priority theorem: the totality is "earlier" than any item — the ontological a priori of § 15's holism now stated in the language of involvement. Together they entail what § 69 and the doctrine of transcendence will exploit: worldhood and Dasein's being are welded at the Worumwillen.

The fourth unit distinguishes two senses of letting-be. Letting-be-involved means ontically: within factical concern, to let something ready-to-hand be so and so, as it now is and in order that it be so. This ontic sense of "letting be" we grasp in a fundamentally ontological way: we thereby interpret the sense of the antecedent freeing of what is innerworldly first ready-to-hand. Letting "be" antecedently does not mean first bringing something into its being and producing it, but discovering what is in each case already "a being" in its readiness-to-hand and so letting it be encountered as the being of this being. This "a priori" letting-be-involved is the condition of the possibility that the ready-to-hand is encountered at all — so that Dasein, in ontic dealings with beings so encountered, can let matters rest there in the ontic sense. Ontologically understood, letting-be-involved concerns the freeing of everything ready-to-hand as ready-to-hand — whether it is something with which, ontically, one lets matters rest, or rather beings with which one ontically does precisely not let matters rest: beings of concern that we do not "let be" as they are but work over, improve, smash. The distinction rescues the concept from quietism in advance: ontological letting-be is not leaving-alone but dis-covering-as — the prior freeing that makes even demolition possible (one can only smash what has been freed for encounter as smashable). The disclosure that "letting-be" here names an accomplishment of discovery, not an abstention, is the seed of a vocabulary with a long future (Seinlassen in "Vom Wesen der Wahrheit" and the later Gelassenheit both germinate here).

The fifth unit gives the structure its tense. The already-having-let-be-involved that frees toward involvement is an a priori perfect (apriorisches Perfekt), characterizing the mode of being of Dasein itself. Ontologically understood, letting-be-involved is the antecedent freeing of beings toward their inner-environmental readiness-to-hand; from the at-which of letting-be-involved, the with-which of the involvement is freed. Concern encounters it as this ready-to-hand thing: insofar as a being shows itself to concern at all — is discovered in its being — it is always already environmentally ready-to-hand, and precisely not "at first" merely present-at-hand "world-stuff." The grammatical coinage is a discovery about time smuggled into a section on world: the freeing is never an act performed and datable but an always-already-having-happened — a perfect tense with no past present, which § 69(a) will identify as the mark of originary temporality. The closing sentence re-nails § 15's colors to the mast: no neutral world-stuff precedes the workshop; the "merely present-at-hand" is the later product, never the prior material.

The sixth unit ascends from involvement to its pre-discovered whole and legislates terminology. Involvement itself, as the being of the ready-to-hand, is in each case discovered only on the ground of the pre-discoveredness of an involvement-totality: in discovered involvement — in the encountered ready-to-hand — there lies pre-discovered what we called the worldly character of the ready-to-hand. This pre-discovered involvement-totality harbors an ontological relation to world. The letting-be-involved that frees beings toward the involvement-totality must itself already have somehow disclosed that toward-which (woraufhin) it frees. And this — that toward which the environmentally ready-to-hand is freed such that it first becomes accessible as an innerworldly being — cannot itself be conceived as a being of this discovered mode of being: it is essentially not discoverable, if we henceforth hold to discoveredness (Entdecktheit) as the term for a possibility of being of all non-Dasein-like beings. The terminological legislation seals § 16's distinction into the book's permanent grammar: beings are discovered; world (and Dasein) is disclosed — two irreducible modes of unveiledness, whose confusion is precisely the tradition's error (treating world as one more, if larger, discoverable). The argument is transcendental in the strict sense: the freeing presupposes a prior openness of the toward-which; the whither of the release cannot be an item in the released field.

The seventh unit names the prior disclosure. What does it mean that that toward which innerworldly beings are first freed must be antecedently disclosed? To Dasein's being belongs understanding of being; understanding has its being in an understanding (Verstehen).
