The fifteenth unit closes the ledger of the chapter: with the interpretation of being-with and being-a-self in das Man, the question of the who of the everydayness of being-with-one-another is answered; and these considerations have at once yielded a concrete understanding of Dasein's basic constitution — being-in-the-world has become visible in its everydayness and averageness. Bookkeeping, but of rank: the second structural moment of the § 12 program (the who) is discharged, and the promised concreteness of the analytic (§ 9's everydayness-decision) has been redeemed at the who no less than at the world.

The sixteenth unit derives, once more and now completely, the tradition's error from the phenomenon itself. Everyday Dasein draws the pre-ontological interpretation of its being from the nearest mode of being of das Man. The ontological interpretation proximally follows this tendency: it understands Dasein from the world and finds it there as an innerworldly being; not only that — even the sense of being with respect to which these existing "subjects" are understood, the "nearest" ontology of Dasein lets be pregiven from the "world." But because in this absorption in the world the world-phenomenon itself is skipped over, in its place steps the innerworldly present-at-hand: things. The being of the beings that are there-with is conceived as presence-at-hand: thus the exhibition of the positive phenomenon of nearest-everyday being-in-the-world makes possible insight into the root of the ontological missing of this constitution of being. It itself, in its everyday mode of being, is what proximally misses and covers itself. The genealogy of § 5 (Rückstrahlung) and § 21 (Descartes) here receives its final, social premise: the world-reading of the self is not the philosopher's private error but das Man's public interpretation, followed by ontology — and since the skipped world leaves things in its place, the substance-self of § 25 falls out as the necessary product. The closing epigram seals Division One's method: the phenomenon that covers itself is the same phenomenon that, exhibited, explains its own covering — critique and analysis are one act.

The seventeenth unit ends the chapter with the decisive structural theorem and a measured breach. If even the being of everyday being-with-one-another, which seemingly approaches pure presence-at-hand ontologically, is fundamentally different from it, still less can the being of the authentic self be conceived as presence-at-hand: authentic being-a-self rests not on an exceptional condition of the subject detached from das Man, but is an existentiell modification of das Man as an essential existential. But then the selfsameness of the authentically existing self is separated ontologically by a chasm (Kluft) from the identity of the I maintaining itself through the manifold of lived experiences. The modification-theorem is the guard-rail for everything Division Two will say about authenticity: no exit from das Man into a pure subject, no second self behind the they-self — authenticity is a way of being the same structures otherwise (seizing what one is dispersed into), which is why it never annuls being-with, publicness, or the everyday but takes them over. And the closing sentence draws the section's whole arc taut: the self won by such modification is categorially — by a chasm — unlike § 25's identical I of experiences; selfhood as existentiell constancy against selfhood as substrate-identity, the opposition on which § 64 will build. With that, the who is answered, the second moment of being-in-the-world secured, and the analysis can turn to the moment that has silently carried both: being-in as such.

#### Chapter Five: Being-In as Such

##### § 28. The Task of a Thematic Analysis of Being-In

The opening unit re-orients the whole analytic toward its unity. The existential analytic of Dasein has, in its preparatory stage, the basic constitution of this being — being-in-the-world — as its guiding theme; its next goal is the phenomenal raising (Hebung) of the unitary original structure of Dasein's being, from which its possibilities and ways "to be" determine themselves ontologically. Hitherto the phenomenal characterization was directed at the structural moment of world and at answering the who-question; but already in the first delineation of the tasks, an orientation about being-in as such was sent ahead (§ 12) and demonstrated on the concrete mode of knowing the world (§ 13). The word Hebung — a raising, as of ore or of treasure — names the coming operation: not another moment surveyed but the unitary structure lifted; the chapter is expressly a staging toward care.

The second unit recalls why the anticipation was made and names the destination. The anticipation of this carrying structural moment sprang from the intent of encircling the analysis of the individual moments, from the outset, within a sustained preliminary view of the structural whole, and of preventing any bursting and splintering of the unitary phenomenon. Now the interpretation must be led back to the phenomenon of being-in, preserving what was won in the concrete analysis of world and who; and the more penetrating consideration of it is to force the structural totality of being-in-the-world anew and more securely before the phenomenological gaze, and also to pave the way for grasping the original being of Dasein itself: care (Sorge). The anti-splintering rule of the division-preamble is re-invoked at the hinge, and the chapter's double assignment is set: consolidate the whole; open the way to its being — the word Sorge, hitherto only promised, now stands as the announced terminus.

The third unit refuses breadth for the sake of depth — and legislates equiprimordiality. What more can be exhibited in being-in-the-world beyond the essential relations of being-alongside the world (concern), being-with (solicitude), and being-a-self (who)? There remains, at most, the possibility of expanding the analysis in breadth by comparative characterization of the variations of concern and its circumspection, of solicitude and its considerateness, and of setting Dasein off from non-Dasein-like beings by sharpened explication of the being of every possible innerworldly being. Unfinished tasks doubtless lie in that direction; what has been set forth needs manifold supplementation with a view to a closed elaboration of the existential a priori of a philosophical anthropology — but at that the present investigation does not aim: its intent is fundamental-ontological. If we therefore inquire thematically after being-in, we cannot wish to annihilate the phenomenon's originality by derivation from others — by an inappropriate analysis in the sense of a dissolution. But the underivability of something original does not exclude a multiplicity of characters of being constitutive for it: if such show themselves, they are existentially equiprimordial (gleichursprünglich). The phenomenon of the equiprimordiality of constitutive moments has often been disregarded in ontology, owing to a methodically unbridled tendency to demonstrate the provenance of anything and everything from a simple "primal ground" (Urgrund). The paragraph legislates the method of the entire chapter: the Da will be analyzed into disposedness, understanding, discourse — a multiplicity without derivation-order — and the closing polemic names the perennial temptation the rule forbids: the monism of the single origin, philosophy's "unbridled" habit of deriving everything from one Urgrund. Equiprimordiality is the analytic's alternative to both foundationalism and dissolution — a structural pluralism at the origin.

The fourth unit refuses the "between" and diagnoses the demand for circumstantiality. In which direction is one to look for the phenomenal characterization of being-in as such? The answer comes by recalling what was entrusted to the phenomenologically retentive gaze at the phenomenon's first indication: being-in in distinction from the present-at-hand insideness of one present-at-hand thing "in" another; being-in not as a quality of a present-at-hand subject effected or even merely occasioned by the presence-at-hand of "world"; being-in rather as the essential mode of being of this being itself. But what then presents itself with this phenomenon other than the present-at-hand commercium between a present-at-hand subject and a present-at-hand object? This interpretation would come closer to the phenomenal stock if it said: Dasein is the being of this "between." Yet orientation to the "between" would remain misleading: it colludes, unexamined, with the ontologically indeterminate positing of the beings between which this between as such "is" — the between is already conceived as the result of the convenientia of two present-at-hand things. But the antecedent positing of these always already bursts the phenomenon, and it is hopeless ever to reassemble it from the fragments: not only is the "cement" lacking; the "schema" according to which the joining is to happen is burst — or rather was never unveiled. What is ontologically decisive is to prevent the bursting of the phenomenon in advance — to secure its positive phenomenal stock. That this requires far-reaching circumstantiality only expresses the fact that something ontically self-evident was, in the transmitted treatment of the "problem of knowledge," ontologically disguised in manifold ways to the point of invisibility. The critique of the "between" is the subtlest in the book's anti-Cartesian arsenal: even the mediating formula (Dasein as the between of subject and object) is refused, because a between borrows its sense from its termini — accept the relata, and the phenomenon is already in fragments no dialectic can glue. The image is exact: it is not the cement that is missing but the schema; the whole was never a composite. And the apology for laboriousness turns method into diagnosis: the analysis is circumstantial precisely in proportion to the depth of the tradition's disguise.

The fifth unit reads the Da. The being essentially constituted by being-in-the-world is itself in each case its "Da" — its there. By the familiar signification the "da" points to "here" and "there" (dort); the here of an "I-here" understands itself always from a ready-to-hand yonder, in the sense of de-severing-directing-concernful being toward it, and Dasein's existential spatiality, which thus determines its "location," is itself grounded in being-in-the-world: the yonder is the determinateness of something encountered innerworldly. "Here" and "yonder" are possible only in a "Da" — that is, when a being is that, as the being of the "Da," has disclosed spatiality. This being carries, in its ownmost being, the character of unclosedness (Unverschlossenheit): the expression "Da" means this essential disclosedness. Through it, this being (Dasein) is, in one with the being-there (Da-sein) of world, "there" for itself. The book's title-word finally receives its reading, and it is not spatial: the Da is neither here nor yonder but the openness within which here and yonder first are — Dasein means being-the-there, being the disclosedness itself. § 12's promise (the term as pure expression of being) is thus cashed: the entity is its open site, there for itself in one with the being-there of world.

The sixth unit converts the metaphysics of light. The ontically figurative talk of the lumen naturale in man means nothing other than this existential-ontological structure: that this being is in the manner of being its Da. It is "illuminated" means: cleared (gelichtet) in itself as being-in-the-world — not by another being, but in such a way that it is itself the clearing (die Lichtung). Only to a being thus existentially cleared does the present-at-hand become accessible in the light, hidden in the dark. Dasein brings its Da along with it from the start; lacking it, it not only is not factically, but is not at all the being of this essence: Dasein is its disclosedness. The paragraph mints the word on which the later Heidegger's whole thinking will turn — Lichtung, the clearing — here introduced as the de-metaphorized truth of the natural light: the tradition's lumen is not a faculty shining on things but the openness that any light and dark presuppose; Dasein does not have a clearing, it is one. The closing sentence is the chapter's charter in four words: Dasein is its disclosedness — an identity, not an attribute.

The seventh unit converts the identity into the task: the constitution of this being is to be set forth. But since the essence of this being is existence, the existential proposition "Dasein is its disclosedness" says at once: the being about which, in its being, this being is at issue is — to be its "Da." Besides characterizing the primary constitution of the being of disclosedness, the course of the analysis demands an interpretation of the mode of being in which this being everyday is its Da. The § 9 essence-formula bites here: because Dasein is its having-to-be, disclosedness too is a task — Dasein has its there to be — and the double program (constitution of the Da; its everyday mode) yields the chapter's A/B architecture announced next.

The eighth unit divides the chapter: the chapter that undertakes the explication of being-in as such — that is, of the being of the Da — falls into two parts: A, the existential constitution of the Da; B, the everyday being of the Da and the falling (Verfallen) of Dasein. The bipartition executes the seventh unit's double task exactly — constitution, then everyday mode — and quietly names, in "Verfallen," the phenomenon toward which the whole second half runs.

The ninth unit names the constituents: the two equiprimordial constitutive ways of being the Da are seen in disposedness (Befindlichkeit) and understanding (Verstehen); the analysis of each receives its necessary phenomenal confirmation through the interpretation of a concrete mode important for the ensuing problematic; and disposedness and understanding are equiprimordially determined by discourse (Rede). The sentence is the chapter's constitution in miniature, and its third clause repays care: Rede is not a third item after the two but their equiprimordial determinant — co-original articulacy running through attunement and understanding alike — which is why its own section (§ 34) comes last, gathering rather than adding. The verification-rule (each existential confirmed on a concrete mode) explains fear's and, later, anxiety's place in the architecture.

The tenth unit gives part A's table: Da-sein as disposedness (§ 29), fear as a mode of disposedness (§ 30), Da-sein as understanding (§ 31), understanding and interpretation (§ 32), assertion as a derivative mode of interpretation (§ 33), Da-sein, discourse, and language (§ 34). The table's internal logic is a cascade of foundings: from each basic existential to its concretion (fear) or its derivatives (interpretation, then assertion as interpretation's derivative) — the word "abkünftig" in § 33's title already announcing the demotion of the proposition that § 33 will argue.

The eleventh unit fixes the register: the analysis of the being-characters of Da-sein is an existential one — the characters are not properties of something present-at-hand but essentially existential ways to be; hence their mode of being in everydayness must be set forth. The reminder repeats § 9's rule at the chapter most liable to psychological misreading: attunement, understanding, and talk are ways the Da is, not endowments of a subject — and their everydayness is owed analysis, not exemption.

The twelfth unit gives part B's table and its principle: corresponding to the constitutive phenomenon of discourse, to the sight lying in understanding, and to the interpretation belonging to it, there are analyzed, as existential modes of the everyday being of the Da: idle talk (§ 35), curiosity (§ 36), ambiguity (§ 37); in these phenomena a basic kind of the being of the Da becomes visible, which we interpret as falling — a "falling" that shows an existentially distinctive movedness (Bewegtheit) (§ 38). The correspondence is the map's deepest decision: the everyday part is organized as the fallen counterparts of the constitution itself — idle talk to discourse, curiosity to understanding's sight, ambiguity to interpretation — so falling is the everyday enactment of the Da's own structures, not a supervening corruption; and the closing word Bewegtheit promises that falling is a movement, the analytic's first kinetics.

##### A. The Existential Constitution of the Da

###### § 29. Da-sein as Disposedness

The opening unit gives the term its ontic name. What is indicated ontologically by the title disposedness (Befindlichkeit) is ontically the most familiar and most everyday thing: mood (Stimmung), being-attuned. Prior to all psychology of moods — a field which anyway lies wholly fallow — the task is to see this phenomenon as a fundamental existential and to outline its structure. The strategy is signature: the analytic's technical term (Befindlichkeit — how one finds oneself, from the everyday "Wie befinden Sie sich?") names the most ordinary phenomenon, and the ordinary is promoted past psychology to an existential of the Da: mood, of all things, as a fundamental way the there is.

The second unit dignifies the pallid cases and finds being disclosed as burden. The undisturbed equanimity as much as the inhibited ill-humor of everyday concern, the sliding from one into the other and the slipping into out-of-tunedness (Verstimmung), are ontologically not nothing, however unnoticed these phenomena remain as supposedly the most indifferent and fleeting in Dasein. That moods can be spoiled and can shift only says that Dasein is in each case always already attuned. The often persistent, even, pallid un-attunement — not to be confused with ill-humor — is so far from nothing that precisely in it Dasein becomes weary of itself: being has become manifest as a burden (Last). Why, one does not know; and Dasein cannot know such things, because the disclosive possibilities of cognition fall far too short compared with the original disclosing of moods, in which Dasein is brought before its being as Da. And again, elevated mood can relieve of the manifest burden of being — this mood-possibility too discloses, though in relieving, the burden-character of Dasein. Mood makes manifest "how one is and fares"; in this "how one is," being-attuned brings being into its "Da." The analysis inverts every hierarchy of the affects: the flattest states — gray listlessness, the mere absence of mood — are the deepest evidence, for in them being as such weighs; the burden discloses what no cognition can reach (the "why, one does not know" is not ignorance to be remedied but the mark of a disclosure deeper than knowing); and even elation testifies to the burden it lifts. The Last-character, here first sounded, is § 9's Überantwortung felt.

The third unit extracts the disclosure and its evasive form. In attunement, Dasein is always already disclosed, mood-wise, as the being to which Dasein was delivered over in its being — as the being it, existing, has to be. Disclosed does not mean: known as such. And precisely in the most indifferent and harmless everydayness the being of Dasein can break out as the naked "that it is and has to be": the pure "that it is" shows itself — the whence and whither remain in darkness. That Dasein everyday just as much does not "give in" to such moods — does not pursue their disclosing and let itself be brought before what is disclosed — is no proof against the phenomenal fact of the mood-wise disclosedness of the being of the Da in its that, but a testimony for it: Dasein mostly evades, ontically-existentielly, the being disclosed in mood; ontologically-existentially this means: in that to which such mood does not turn, Dasein is unveiled in its being-delivered-over to the Da. In the evading itself, the Da is something disclosed. The argument-form is the section's masterstroke and will bear the whole Angst-analysis (§ 40): evasion is evidence — one can flee only what is disclosed, so everyday indifference to mood's message confirms the message. The naked Daß with darkened whence and whither is the phenomenon awaiting its name in the next unit.

The fourth unit names it. This character of Dasein's being — this "that it is," veiled in its whence and whither yet all the more unveiledly disclosed in itself — we call the thrownness (Geworfenheit) of this being into its Da: in such a way, namely, that it, as being-in-the-world, is the Da. The expression thrownness is meant to indicate the facticity of the being-delivered-over. The "that it is and has to be" disclosed in disposedness is not that "that" which ontologically-categorially expresses the factuality belonging to presence-at-hand — a factuality accessible only in an observing ascertainment. The that disclosed in disposedness must rather be conceived as an existential determinateness of the being that is in the manner of being-in-the-world: facticity is not the factuality of the factum brutum of something present-at-hand, but a character of Dasein's being, taken up into existence though at first thrust aside. The that of facticity is never findable in a beholding. Geworfenheit here receives its coinage, and the definitional care repays attention: thrownness is § 12's facticity given its disclosure-mode — the delivered-over-ness felt in mood — and the double demarcation (against the categorial Tatsächlichkeit of things; against any intuitive access) fixes its logic: the that-I-am is not an observable fact about me but a weight I find myself under, accessible only to disposedness, never to the gaze.

The fifth unit gives disposedness its literal sense and its genesis in flight. A being of Dasein's character is its Da in such a way that, expressly or not, it finds itself (sich befindet) in its thrownness. In disposedness Dasein is always already brought before itself; it has always already found itself — not as a perceiving coming-upon-itself, but as attuned self-finding (gestimmtes Sichbefinden). As a being delivered over to its being, it remains delivered over also to this: that it must always already have found itself — found in a finding that springs not so much from a direct seeking as from a fleeing. Mood does not disclose in the manner of looking at thrownness, but as turning-toward and turning-away (An- und Abkehr); mostly it does not turn toward the burden-character of Dasein manifest in it — least of all as relieved-ness in elevated mood. This turning-away is what it is always in the manner of disposedness. The etymological cash-out (Befindlichkeit from sich befinden: how one finds oneself) yields the deep structure: the self is first found, not sought — and found in fleeing, so that the primary self-relation is aversion; mood's disclosure is constitutively oblique, an An- und Abkehr rather than a beholding. § 25's suspicion about reflective self-givenness is here grounded: prior to any reflection, Dasein has already found itself — in the mode of turning away.

The sixth unit defends mood's evidence on two fronts. One would phenomenally misjudge entirely what mood discloses and how, if one were to collate with the disclosed what attuned Dasein "at the same time" is acquainted with, knows, and believes. Even if Dasein is "secure" in faith about its whither, or supposes itself to know the whence through rational enlightenment, this counts for nothing against the phenomenal fact that mood brings Dasein before the that of its Da, as which it stares at Dasein with unrelenting enigmaticalness. Existentially-ontologically there is not the least right to depress the "evidence" of disposedness by measuring it against the apodictic certainty of a theoretical cognition of the purely present-at-hand; but no less is the falsification that shoves the phenomena off into the refuge of the irrational — irrationalism, as rationalism's counterplay, speaks only with a squint of that toward which rationalism is blind. The double front is drawn with perfect symmetry: against epistemology's measuring-rod (mood's evidence is sui generis, not deficient apodicticity) and against Lebensphilosophie's refuge (the "irrational" is rationalism's own shadow-concept — irrationalism concedes the enemy's map and merely reverses the valuations). The staring enigma — impervious to faith's answers and enlightenment's explanations alike — keeps thrownness beneath every doctrine about whence and whither.

The seventh unit concedes mastery and states the first theorem. That Dasein can, should, and must factically become master of mood with knowledge and will may signify, in certain possibilities of existing, a priority of willing and cognition; only this must not mislead one into ontologically denying mood as the original mode of being of Dasein, in which it is disclosed to itself before all cognition and willing and beyond their range of disclosure. And moreover: we never master a mood free of mood, but always from a counter-mood. As the first ontological essential character of disposedness we thus gain: disposedness discloses Dasein in its thrownness — and proximally and mostly in the manner of evasive turning-away. The concession-plus-limit is exact ethics of the affects: self-mastery is real and, in some existences, ranking — but it is intramural, one mood displacing another; there is no mood-free standpoint, so the primacy of disclosure stays with attunement. The first theorem then formalizes units three through five.

The eighth unit expels the inner state. Already from this it is visible that disposedness is far removed from anything like coming upon a psychic condition; so little has it the character of a grasping that first turns around and back, that all immanent reflection can come upon "lived experiences" only because the Da is already disclosed in disposedness. "Mere mood" discloses the Da more originally — but it also, correspondingly, closes it off more stubbornly than any not-perceiving. The two clauses balance like a scale: reflection is derivative (it finds Erlebnisse only in an already-opened there — the § 13 order, run inward), and mood's power is double-edged — the most original discloser is also the most obstinate concealer, which the next unit shows.

The ninth unit demonstrates it on bad mood, and settles inside/outside. Out-of-tunedness (Verstimmung) shows this: in it Dasein becomes blind to itself, the environing world of concern is veiled, circumspection is misled. Disposedness is so far from being reflected that it assails (überfällt) Dasein precisely in its unreflective abandonment to the "world" of its concern. Mood assails: it comes neither from "outside" nor from "inside," but arises as a way of being-in-the-world out of this itself. Therewith, past a negative demarcation of disposedness against reflective grasping of the "inner," we reach a positive insight into its disclosive character: mood has in each case already disclosed being-in-the-world as a whole and first makes possible a directing-oneself toward... Being-attuned does not relate first to the psychic; it is no inner condition that then, in some enigmatic way, gets outside and rubs off on things and persons. Herewith the second essential character shows itself: disposedness is an existential basic mode of the equiprimordial disclosedness of world, co-Dasein, and existence, because this disclosedness is itself essentially being-in-the-world. The passage abolishes the coloring-theory of the emotions in one stroke: since mood is a mode of being-in-the-world, the inside/outside alternative never applies — attunement discloses the whole (world, others, self) at once, prior to any directedness; the intentional act itself presupposes the tuned openness. The second theorem — mood as whole-disclosure — is the ground of everything §§ 40 and 68(b) will build on Angst and on the temporality of disposedness.

The tenth unit adds the third character: affectability. Beside the two explicated determinations — the disclosing of thrownness and the current disclosing of the whole of being-in-the-world — a third is to be noted, which above all contributes to the more penetrating understanding of the worldhood of the world. Earlier (§ 18) it was said: the antecedently disclosed world lets the innerworldly be encountered. This antecedent disclosedness of world, belonging to being-in, is co-constituted by disposedness. Letting-be-encountered is primarily circumspective, not merely a sensing or a staring; circumspectively concernful letting-be-encountered has — as we now see more sharply from disposedness — the character of being affected (Betroffenwerden). But affectedness by the unserviceability, resistance, threateningness of the ready-to-hand becomes ontologically possible only because being-in as such is existentially determined in advance so that it can be concerned (angegangen) in this way by the innerworldly encountered: this concernability (Angänglichkeit) grounds in disposedness, as which it has disclosed the world, for instance, with regard to threatenability. Only what is in the disposedness of fearing — or of fearlessness — can discover the environmentally ready-to-hand as threatening. The attunedness of disposedness constitutes existentially Dasein's openness to world (Weltoffenheit). The third theorem completes § 16's account of the modes of concern from their condition: things can break in, resist, threaten only for a being antecedently exposed — mattering presupposes attunement. Even fearlessness is listed as a disposedness: the calm in which nothing threatens is itself a tuning of the world, not its absence.

The eleventh unit draws the consequence for the senses and for the primacy of mood. And only because the "senses" belong ontologically to a being that has the mode of being of disposed being-in-the-world can they be "touched" and "have a sense for," so that what touches shows itself in affection. Nothing like affection would come about under the strongest pressure and resistance — resistance would remain essentially undiscovered — if disposed being-in-the-world had not already referred itself to a concernability by innerworldly beings predelineated by moods. In disposedness lies existentially a disclosive referredness upon world, out of which what concerns us can be encountered; and we must in fact, ontologically and in principle, leave the primary discovery of the world to "mere mood." Pure beholding, though it pressed into the innermost veins of the being of something present-at-hand, could never discover anything like the threatening. The argument radicalizes § 21's hardness-analysis to its ground: not only Descartes' kinematics but any pure intuition is constitutionally blind to the threatening — stimulus becomes affection only within an attuned exposure, so the world's primary discovery belongs to mood, and sensation itself is a founded mode of Befindlichkeit. The Cartesian order (sense-data first, significance added) is inverted at the physiology of the senses themselves.

The twelfth unit defends deceivability and finds mood even in theōria. That on the ground of primarily disclosing disposedness everyday circumspection errs and largely succumbs to deception is, measured against the idea of an absolute "world"-cognition, a mē on — a nonbeing; but such ontologically unjustified valuations wholly misjudge the existential positivity of deceivability. Precisely in the unsteady, mood-wise flickering seeing of the "world," the ready-to-hand shows itself in its specific worldhood — which is on no day the same. Theoretical looking-at has always already dimmed the world down to the uniformity of the purely present-at-hand — within which uniformity, to be sure, a new wealth of the discoverable-in-pure-determining is enclosed. But even the purest theōria has not left all mood behind: even to its looking, the merely present-at-hand shows itself in its pure look only when theōria can let it come toward it in tranquil tarrying-alongside, in rhastōnē and diagōgē — Aristotle's leisure and pastime (Metaphysics A 2). And one will not wish to confuse this exhibition of the existential-ontological constitution of cognitive determining in the disposedness of being-in-the-world with an attempt to deliver science, ontically, over to "feeling." The paragraph performs a triple balance: deceivability is dignified (the flickering, never-selfsame world of moods is worldhood showing itself, not a defect against absolute knowledge); theory is honored (its dimming-down opens its own wealth — § 13's positive verdict kept); and the master-stroke — even theōria is a mood: the Greek scientist's calm is an attunement, tranquillity as the tuning in which the pure look is possible, so the exception proves the theorem. The closing guard bars the sentimentalist misreading: grounding cognition in disposedness is ontology, not a plea for feeling in science.

The thirteenth unit opens the historical dossier: within this investigation's problematic the various modes of disposedness and their founding-connections cannot be interpreted. Under the titles of affects and feelings the phenomena are ontically long familiar and have always been considered in philosophy — and it is no accident that the first transmitted, systematically executed interpretation of the affects is not treated within the frame of "psychology": Aristotle investigates the pathē in the second book of his Rhetoric, which must be grasped — against the traditional orientation of the concept of rhetoric to something like a "school subject" — as the first systematic hermeneutic of the everydayness of being-with-one-another. Publicness, as the mode of being of das Man (§ 27), not only has its attunement in general; it needs mood and "makes" it for itself: into it and out of it the orator speaks, needing the understanding of the possibilities of mood in order to arouse and steer it in the right way. The re-reading of the Rhetoric is a small revolution in the history of philosophy, executed in a subordinate clause: Aristotle's treatise on persuasion becomes the first hermeneutics of everyday Mitsein, because the pathē are analyzed there as they function in public life — and § 27's publicness is completed by the observation that das Man manufactures its moods (the sentence in which the modern culture-industries and their political sequels are legible avant la lettre): the orator as the technician of the public attunement.

The fourteenth unit runs the decline: the continuation of the interpretation of the affects in the Stoa, and its transmission through patristic and scholastic theology to modernity, are familiar; what goes unnoticed is that the fundamental ontological interpretation of the affective in general has scarcely advanced a noteworthy step since Aristotle — on the contrary, the affects and feelings fall thematically under the psychic phenomena, functioning mostly as their third class beside representation and will: they sink to accompaniment-phenomena (Begleitphänomene). The verdict has § 6's shape: a Greek beginning, transmitted without renewal, and a modern demotion — the tripartite psychology (representing, willing, feeling) filed as the institutional form of the affects' ontological neglect: mood as the mind's incidental music.

The fifteenth unit credits phenomenology and marks its limit: it is a merit of phenomenological research to have created again a freer view of these phenomena; not only that — Scheler above all, taking up impulses from Augustine and Pascal, directed the problematic to the founding-connections between "representing" and "interest-taking" acts. The folded-in note gives Pascal's text: whereas of human things one says they must be known before they are loved, the saints say of divine things that they must be loved to be known — one enters truth only through charity; with Augustine's non intratur in veritatem, nisi per charitatem behind it. Yet here too the existential-ontological foundations of the act-phenomenon in general remain in the dark. The genealogy Augustine–Pascal–Scheler names the counter-tradition to the tripartite psychology: love as the condition of knowing, interest founding representation — Heidegger's own thesis (disposedness before cognition) given its Christian ancestry — and the criticism is the standing one (§ 10): even Scheler's priority of the affective moves within an unquestioned ontology of acts.

The sixteenth unit gives the darker corollary: disposedness not only discloses Dasein in its thrownness and referredness upon the world already disclosed with its being; it is itself the existential mode of being in which Dasein constantly delivers itself over to the "world" and lets itself be concerned by it in such a way that it in a certain manner evades itself. The existential constitution of this evading will become clear in the phenomenon of falling. The unit ties the section's evasion-motif (units three and five) forward: the turning-away is not an occasional weakness but the standing form of everyday attunement — self-delivery to the world as self-evasion — and § 38 is named as the place where this structure receives its name and its kinetics.

The seventeenth unit converts disposedness into method. Disposedness is an existential basic mode in which Dasein is its Da. It not only characterizes Dasein ontologically; on the ground of its disclosing it is at the same time of fundamental methodological significance for the existential analytic. Like every ontological interpretation, the analytic can only, as it were, listen in on (abhören) previously disclosed beings as to their being; and it will hold itself to the distinctive, most far-reaching possibilities of disclosure of Dasein, in order to receive from them the information about this being. Phenomenological interpretation must give Dasein itself the possibility of original disclosing, and let it, as it were, interpret itself; it only goes along in this disclosing, in order to raise the phenomenal content of the disclosed existentially into the concept. The paragraph is the hermeneutic circle become research-protocol: ontology has no access of its own — it auscultates what Dasein's own disclosedness has opened — so the analytic must seek out the most far-reaching disclosures and follow them. The rule explains, in advance, the architecture of the whole book: why Angst (§ 40), death, and conscience will be elected as the analytic's organs — they are Dasein's own widest self-disclosures, which the interpretation accompanies and conceptualizes but does not replace.

The closing unit makes the first such election: with a view to the later interpretation of an existential-ontologically significant basic disposedness of Dasein — anxiety (§ 40) — the phenomenon of disposedness is to be demonstrated still more concretely on the determinate mode of fear. The transition is doubly motivated: fear verifies the structure just won (the § 28 rule that each existential be confirmed on a concrete mode), and it is chosen as anxiety's foil — the ontic sibling from which the ontological basic mood must later be distinguished.

###### § 30. Fear as a Mode of Disposedness

The opening unit sets the grid — and grounds it. The phenomenon of fear can be considered in three respects: the before-which (Wovor) of fear, fearing itself, and the about-which (Worum) of fear. These possible and connected respects are not accidental: with them the structure of disposedness in general comes to the fore. The analysis is completed by pointing to the possible modifications of fear, each concerning different structural moments. The note refers the whole section to Aristotle's Rhetoric II 5 — the phobos-chapter — making § 30 a silent retrieval of the text § 29 just crowned. The methodological claim is the important one: the triad (before-which, fearing, about-which) is not fear's private anatomy but disposedness's general structure showing through — every mood has its whence of affection, its enactment, and its stake — which is why § 40 can run anxiety through the same grid and let the differences speak.

The second unit anatomizes the fearsome. The before-which of fear, the "fearsome," is in each case something encountered innerworldly, with the mode of being of the ready-to-hand, the present-at-hand, or co-Dasein. The task is not an ontic report on the beings that can be fearsome, but the phenomenal determination of the fearsome in its fearsomeness. What belongs to it? The before-which of fear has the character of threateningness (Bedrohlichkeit), and to this belongs a manifold: what is encountered has the involvement-character of detrimentality (Abträglichkeit) — it shows itself within an involvement-context; this detrimentality aims at a determinate circuit of what it can affect, and comes, thus determined, from a determinate region; the region itself, and what comes from it, is known as such — as that with which things are not "canny" (nicht geheuer); the detrimental, as threatening, is not yet in masterable nearness, but it approaches (naht) — and in such approaching the detrimentality radiates, having therein the character of threatening; this approaching is one within nearness — what may be detrimental in the highest degree, even constantly coming nearer, but far off, remains veiled in its fearsomeness, whereas as an approacher in the near the detrimental threatens: it can strike, and yet in the end may not. In the approaching, this "it can, and yet in the end may not" intensifies — it is fearsome, we say; and this implies: the detrimental, as what nears in the near, carries with it the unveiled possibility of staying away and passing by, which does not diminish or extinguish fearing but forms it (bildet es aus). The six moments are a phenomenology of the threatening executed entirely in the chapter's prior vocabulary — detrimentality as an involvement (§ 18), the region (§ 22), nearness and approach (§ 23) — proving that mood-disclosure inhabits the same world-structures as concern. Two moments carry the philosophical weight: the uncanny region (the whence of threat is known precisely as unhomely — the word ungeheuer planted for § 40's Unheimlichkeit), and the modal flicker at the close: fear feeds not on certainty of harm but on the oscillating "may and may not" — possibility, not actuality, is what threatens; suspense is fear's element, and a guaranteed blow would already be beyond fear.

The third unit analyzes fearing itself. Fearing is the letting-itself-be-concerned that frees (das sich-angehen-lassende Freigeben) the threatening so characterized. It is not that a future evil (malum futurum) is first ascertained and then feared; nor does fearing first register what approaches — it discovers it beforehand in its fearsomeness. And only in fearing can fear then, expressly looking, "clarify" the fearsome to itself. Circumspection sees the fearsome because it is in the disposedness of fear. Fearing, as a slumbering possibility of disposed being-in-the-world — "fearfulness" (Furchtsamkeit) — has already disclosed the world with regard to this, that from it something like the fearsome can approach; and the ability-to-approach itself is freed by the essential existential spatiality of being-in-the-world. The scholastic definition (fear as expectation of future evil — the tradition from Aristotle through the Stoa to the schools) is inverted at its joint: no neutral ascertainment precedes the fearing; the affect is itself the discovery — fear is the organ that first lets anything show as fearsome, and circumspection sees threat only because attunement has opened the world as threatenable (§ 29's third theorem verified). Fearfulness as slumbering possibility gives the disposition its ontological form: a standing readiness of the there, actualized by no inference.

The fourth unit turns to the stake. That about which fear fears is the fearing being itself — Dasein: only a being for which, in its being, this being itself is at issue can fear. Fearing discloses this being in its endangerment, in its abandonment to itself (Überlassenheit an es selbst); fear always unveils Dasein, though in varying explicitness, in the being of its Da. That we fear for house and home is no counter-instance: for Dasein, as being-in-the-world, is in each case concernful being-alongside, and proximally and mostly Dasein is from out of what it attends to — its endangerment is a threatening of being-alongside. Fear discloses Dasein predominantly in a privative manner: it confuses and makes one "lose one's head"; fear at once closes off the endangered being-in, in letting it be seen — so that when fear has withdrawn, Dasein must first find its way about again. The unit fixes the affect's reflexivity on § 9's foundation: only the being whose being is at stake can fear, so every fear is at bottom fear about oneself — and the house-and-home objection is met by § 12: since I am my being-alongside, threats to what I dwell with strike me in my being. The privative clause records fear's peculiar economy: a disclosure that bewilders — showing the endangered being-in precisely by scattering it — everyday attunement's double edge (§ 29, unit eight) at its sharpest.

The fifth unit is the formal résumé: fearing-about, as fearing-before, always discloses — privatively or positively — equiprimordially the innerworldly being in its threateningness and being-in with regard to its being-threatened. Fear is a mode of disposedness. The two-sided disclosure (world as threatening, self as threatened, in one) is § 29's second theorem instantiated: the mood opens the whole relation at once — which is what makes it a mode of Befindlichkeit and not a private state.

The sixth unit analyzes fearing-for-others. Fearing-about can also concern others, and we then speak of fearing for them. This fearing-for does not take the other's fear away from him — which is excluded already because the other, for whom we fear, may not fear at all: we fear for the other most precisely when he does not fear and plunges recklessly at what threatens. Fearing-for is a way of co-disposedness with others, but not necessarily a fearing-along or a fearing-with-one-another: one can fear for... without fearing oneself. Yet looked at closely, fearing-for is after all a fearing-oneself — what is "feared" is the being-with with the other, who could be torn from one. The fearsome does not aim directly at the one who fears along; fearing-for knows itself in a certain way unaffected, and yet is co-affected in the affectedness of the co-Dasein for which it fears. Hence fearing-for is not a weakened fearing-oneself: at issue are not degrees of "feeling-tones" but existential modes; and fearing-for does not forfeit its specific genuineness if it "actually" does not fear for itself. The analysis is a jewel of the Mitsein-chapter's application: the paradox (I fear most for the fearless one) refutes any contagion- or empathy-model of shared affect; the resolution — what is threatened is the Mitsein itself, the with-being that could be torn — locates the stake of altruistic fear in the § 26 structure; and the closing methodological sentence generalizes: existential modes, not intensity-degrees, individuate the affects — a rule against the whole quantitative psychology of feeling.

The closing unit runs the modifications and secures the disposition. The constitutive moments of the full phenomenon of fear can vary, yielding different possibilities of being of fearing. To the encounter-structure of the threatening belongs approach in nearness: insofar as something threatening, in its "not yet, but any moment," itself suddenly breaks into concernful being-in-the-world, fear becomes alarm (Erschrecken) — so in the threatening one must distinguish the nearest approach of what threatens and the manner in which the approach itself is encountered: suddenness. The before-which of alarm is at first something known and familiar; if by contrast the threatening has the character of the wholly and utterly unfamiliar, fear becomes horror (Grauen); and where the threatening is encountered with the character of the horrible and at once with the encounter-character of the alarming — suddenness — fear becomes terror (Entsetzen). Further variations we know as timidity, shyness, apprehensiveness, being-startled. All modifications of fear, as possibilities of self-finding, point to this: that Dasein as being-in-the-world is "fearful" (furchtsam) — a "fearfulness" not to be understood in the ontic sense of a factical, "isolated" predisposition, but as an existential possibility of the essential disposedness of Dasein in general, which of course is not the only one. The combinatorics are elegantly generated from the grid (varying the approach yields alarm; the familiarity, horror; both, terror), showing the analysis productive, not merely descriptive. The closing guard lifts Furchtsamkeit from characterology to constitution — fearfulness as a possibility of the there itself, not a timid temperament — and the last clause, "not the only one," holds the door open through which § 40 will bring anxiety: the disposedness whose before-which is no innerworldly being at all.

###### § 31. Da-sein as Understanding

The opening unit couples the second existential to the first and demotes a famous rival. Disposedness is one of the existential structures in which the being of the Da maintains itself; equiprimordially with it, understanding constitutes this being. Disposedness always has its understanding, if only in keeping it suppressed; understanding is always attuned. If understanding is interpreted as a fundamental existential, the phenomenon is thereby conceived as a basic mode of the being of Dasein; "understanding," by contrast, in the sense of one possible kind of cognition among others — distinguished, say, from "explaining" — must, together with explaining, be interpreted as an existential derivative of the primary understanding that co-constitutes the being of the Da as such. The two opening reciprocities (attunement understands; understanding is attuned) enforce § 28's equiprimordiality against any ranking of feeling and thought; and the aside dispatches the era's dearest methodological dichotomy: Dilthey's Verstehen/Erklären, banner of the human sciences, is demoted at a stroke — both explaining and understanding-as-method are late derivatives of the existential understanding that every Dasein is.

The second unit shows that understanding was already on the table. The investigation has in fact already struck this original understanding without letting it move expressly into the theme. That Dasein, existing, is its Da means: world is "there" — its being-there is being-in — and this is likewise "there," as that for the sake of which Dasein is. In the for-the-sake-of-which, existing being-in-the-world as such is disclosed, and this disclosedness was called understanding (§ 18); in understanding the for-the-sake-of-which, the significance grounded in it is co-disclosed. The disclosedness of understanding concerns, as that of for-the-sake-of-which and significance equiprimordially, the whole of being-in-the-world; significance is that toward which world as such is disclosed. That for-the-sake-of-which and significance are disclosed in Dasein means: Dasein is a being for which, as being-in-the-world, its own being is at issue. The recapitulation binds § 18's world-derivation into the new frame: what there did the disclosing — the self-referral from the Worumwillen through significance — now has its name and its ontological place as the second constitutive way of being the Da.

The third unit derives understanding from ability and installs possibility at the summit. We sometimes use, in ontic speech, the expression "to understand something" in the sense of "being able to manage a thing," "being up to it," "being capable of something" (etwas können). What is "able" in understanding as an existential is no what, but being as existing: in understanding lies, existentially, Dasein's mode of being as potentiality-of-being (Seinkönnen). Dasein is not something present-at-hand that possesses, as an addition, the capacity for something; it is primarily being-possible (Möglichsein). Dasein is in each case what it can be, and how it is its possibility. Its essential being-possible concerns the characterized ways of attending to the "world," of solicitude for others, and, in all this and always already, the potentiality-of-being toward itself, for its own sake. This being-possible, which Dasein in each case existentially is, differs as much from empty logical possibility as from the contingency of something present-at-hand, insofar as with the latter this or that can "come to pass": as a modal category of presence-at-hand, possibility means the not yet actual and not ever necessary — the merely possible, ontologically lower than actuality and necessity. Possibility as an existential, by contrast, is the most original and last positive ontological determinateness of Dasein; at first, like existentiality in general, it can only be prepared as a problem — the phenomenal soil for seeing it at all is offered by understanding as disclosive potentiality-of-being. The paragraph performs one of the book's great transvaluations. The vernacular verb (können — to be able, to know how) supplies the phenomenon: understanding is competence in being, not apprehension of content — I understand my existence the way a craftsman understands his trade. And the modal revolution follows: against the tradition's scale (actuality above possibility, possibility as the not-yet and never-must), possibility is crowned the highest and last determination of Dasein — the § 7 maxim ("higher than actuality stands possibility") receiving its ontological ground, and the whole analytic of death (being toward a possibility, § 53) its license.

The fourth unit binds possibility to thrownness. Possibility as an existential does not mean a free-floating potentiality-of-being in the sense of the "indifference of choice" (libertas indifferentiae). Dasein, as essentially disposed, has in each case already gotten into determinate possibilities; as the potentiality-of-being that it is, it has let such possibilities pass by, constantly waives possibilities of its being, seizes them and mis-seizes itself. But this means: Dasein is being-possible delivered over to itself — thrown possibility through and through. Dasein is the possibility of being-free for its ownmost potentiality-of-being; and its being-possible is transparent to it in various possible ways and degrees. The unit blocks the reading Sartre would make canonical before it could arise: possibility here is not indifferent liberty hovering over options but thrown possibility — always already in determinate possibilities, always waiving, seizing, mis-seizing — so freedom is finite from the root; the formula "possibility of being-free for the ownmost potentiality" makes even freedom something Dasein can be free for, a possibility to be won.

The fifth unit fixes understanding's peculiar "knowing" and its constitutive errancy. Understanding is the being of such potentiality-of-being — one that is never still outstanding as something not yet present-at-hand, but that, as essentially never present-at-hand, "is" with the being of Dasein in the sense of existence. Dasein is in such a way that it has in each case understood, or not understood, to be thus or thus; as such understanding it "knows" what it is at with itself — with its potentiality-of-being. This "knowing" has not first grown from an immanent self-perception; it belongs to the being of the Da, which is essentially understanding. And only because Dasein, understanding, is its Da, can it lose its way and mistake itself; and since understanding is disposed, and as disposed existentially delivered over to thrownness, Dasein has in each case already lost its way and mistaken itself: in its potentiality-of-being it is therefore delivered over to the possibility of first finding itself again in its possibilities. The pre-reflective self-"knowing" (what one is at with oneself — woran es mit ihm selbst ist) completes § 29's account of self-finding from the understanding side; and the derivation of errancy is the deeper stroke: only an understander can go astray, and a thrown understander always already has — self-mistaking is not an accident befalling Dasein but a structural consequence, so that self-finding is essentially re-finding, recovery. § 27's "must first find itself" here receives its transcendental deduction.

The sixth unit is a hinge: understanding is the existential being of Dasein's own potentiality-of-being, in such a way that this being discloses in itself what its being is at with itself; the structure of this existential must be grasped still more sharply. The compressed formula (being that discloses at itself its own whereat) is banked; the sharpening follows as projection.

The seventh unit extends understanding over everything disclosable — and catches Kant in the act. As disclosing, understanding always concerns the whole basic constitution of being-in-the-world: as potentiality-of-being, being-in is in each case potentiality-of-being-in-the-world. World is not only disclosed, qua world, as possible significance; the freeing of the innerworldly itself frees these beings toward their possibilities — the ready-to-hand is discovered as such in its serviceability, usability, detrimentality, and the involvement-totality unveils itself as the categorial whole of a possibility of the connection of the ready-to-hand. Even the "unity" of the manifold present-at-hand, nature, is discoverable only on the ground of the disclosedness of a possibility of it. Is it an accident that the question of the being of nature aims at the "conditions of its possibility"? Wherein does such questioning ground? Facing it, this question cannot be omitted: why is non-Dasein-like being understood in its being when it is disclosed with regard to the conditions of its possibility? Kant presupposes such a thing, perhaps rightly — but this presupposition itself can least of all remain undemonstrated in its right. The claim is sweeping and precise at once: everything disclosed — tool, totality, nature — is disclosed in and as possibility; hence the transcendental method itself (Kant's question of conditions of possibility) is a symptom to be explained, not a foundation: transcendental philosophy silently exploits the possibility-structure of understanding, and fundamental ontology must exhibit what critique presupposes.

The eighth unit gives the structure its name. Why does understanding, in all essential dimensions of what is disclosable in it, always press into possibilities? Because understanding has in itself the existential structure we call projection (Entwurf): it projects the being of Dasein upon its for-the-sake-of-which as originally as upon significance as the worldhood of its current world. The projection-character of understanding constitutes being-in-the-world with regard to the disclosedness of its Da as the Da of a potentiality-of-being; projection is the existential constitution of being of the leeway (Spielraum) of factical potentiality-of-being. And, as thrown, Dasein is thrown into the mode of being of projecting. Projecting has nothing to do with comporting oneself toward a thought-out plan according to which Dasein arranges its being; rather, as Dasein it has always already projected itself, and is, as long as it is, projecting. Dasein always already understands itself, and always still, as long as it is, from possibilities. The projection-character means further that understanding does not thematically grasp that upon which it projects — the possibilities: such grasping deprives the projected of precisely its possibility-character, drags it down to a given, intended stock; whereas projection, in throwing, throws possibility before itself as possibility and lets it be as such. Understanding is, as projecting, the mode of being of Dasein in which it is its possibilities as possibilities. Every clause of the coinage guards against a misreading. Entwurf is not a plan (no design precedes it — Dasein is projecting, not a planner); it is thrown (geworfener Entwurf — the throw is always already underway, from a facticity not chosen); and it is non-thematic (to grasp one's possibility as an object is to lose it as possibility — the profound point that self-knowledge in the survey-mode destroys what it surveys). The Spielraum-sentence quietly re-grounds § 23: the leeway within which anything near or far can matter is projection's clearing.

The ninth unit draws the paradoxes of the projective self. On the ground of the mode of being constituted by the existential of projection, Dasein is constantly "more" than it factually is, if one wished and were able to register it, as something present-at-hand, in its stock of being. But it is never more than it factically is, because potentiality-of-being belongs essentially to its facticity; and, as being-possible, it is also never less: what, in its potentiality-of-being, it is not yet, it is existentially. And only because the being of the Da receives its constitution through understanding and its projection-character — because it is what it becomes, or does not become — can it, understanding, say to itself: "become what you are!" The tatsächlich/faktisch distinction resolves the seeming contradiction: measured as an occurrent stock, Dasein always exceeds the inventory (its possibilities are not listed among its properties); measured factically, the possibilities are it — it is its not-yet. Pindar's imperative, quoted at the close, is thereby rescued from paradox: only a being that is what it becomes can be commanded to become what it is; the sentence is the seed of § 62's anticipatory resoluteness and of the whole existential reading of selfhood as task.

The tenth unit differentiates the projection into the book's great fork. Projection always concerns the full disclosedness of being-in-the-world; understanding has, as potentiality-of-being, itself possibilities, predelineated by the circuit of what is essentially disclosable in it. Understanding can place itself primarily in the disclosedness of the world — Dasein can, proximally and mostly, understand itself from its world; or understanding throws itself primarily into the for-the-sake-of-which — Dasein exists as itself. Understanding is either authentic, springing from the own self as such, or inauthentic. The "in-" does not mean that Dasein cuts itself off from its self and understands "only" the world: world belongs to its selfhood as being-in-the-world. Authentic as well as inauthentic understanding can in turn be genuine or ungenuine (echt oder unecht). Understanding is, as potentiality-of-being, thoroughly shot through with possibility; but placing oneself into one of these basic possibilities does not lay the other aside — rather, because understanding in each case concerns the full disclosedness of Dasein as being-in-the-world, the self-placement of understanding is an existential modification of the projection as a whole: in understanding world, being-in is always co-understood; understanding of existence as such is always an understanding of world. The fork (self-understanding from world versus from the Worumwillen) gives authenticity and inauthenticity their precise structural definition — a difference in the primary direction of one projection, not two faculties — and the double guard is essential: inauthenticity does not sever the self (world belongs to selfhood), authenticity does not shed the world (existence-understanding is world-understanding); the authentic/genuine cross-division adds a second axis the reception mostly forgets — there is ungenuine authenticity (posturing ownness) and genuine inauthenticity (honest absorption).

The eleventh unit is a single sentence banking the everyday case: as factical, Dasein has in each case already displaced its potentiality-of-being into a possibility of understanding. The brevity is the point — the fork is never faced from neutral ground; one always finds oneself already on a branch.

The twelfth unit gathers the sights and defines transparency. Understanding constitutes, in its projection-character, existentially what we call Dasein's sight (Sicht). With the disclosedness of the Da, this sight is existentially, equiprimordially according to the characterized basic ways of its being: as circumspection of concern, considerateness of solicitude, and as the sight upon being as such, for the sake of which Dasein in each case is as it is. The sight that relates primarily and in the whole to existence we call transparency (Durchsichtigkeit) — the term chosen to designate well-understood "self-knowledge," to indicate that at issue is not the perceptual tracking-down and beholding of a self-point, but an understanding seizing of the full disclosedness of being-in-the-world through its essential constitutive moments. Existing beings sight "themselves" only insofar as they have become transparent to themselves equiprimordially in their being alongside the world and in being-with others, as the constitutive moments of their existence. The § 15 and § 26 sights are now derived from their common root (all sight is projected understanding), and self-knowledge is re-founded: transparency is not introspection of an inner point but seeing oneself through world and others — I know myself in my workshop and my friendships or not at all; the Delphic imperative routed through being-in-the-world.

The thirteenth unit adds the sober corollary: conversely, Dasein's opacity (Undurchsichtigkeit) is rooted not solely and primarily in "egocentric" self-deceptions, but just as much in ignorance of the world. The one-sentence inversion is a quiet demolition of the moral psychology of self-deception: since selfhood runs through world, world-ignorance blinds one to oneself as surely as vanity does — a thesis with consequences for every therapeutic and confessional tradition that seeks the self only within.

The fourteenth unit guards the ocular vocabulary. The expression "sight" must be preserved from a misunderstanding: it corresponds to the clearedness (Gelichtetheit) as which the disclosedness of the Da was characterized. "Seeing" means not only not perceiving with the bodily eyes, but also not the pure non-sensuous apprehending of something present-at-hand in its presence-at-hand; only this peculiarity of seeing is claimed for the existential signification of sight — that it lets the beings accessible to it be encountered unconcealed in themselves. This, of course, every "sense" accomplishes within its genuine region of discovery; but the tradition of philosophy is from the outset oriented primarily to "seeing" as the mode of access to beings and to being, and to preserve the connection with it, sight and seeing may be formalized so far as to yield a universal term characterizing every access to beings and to being as access in general. The guard cuts both ways: against literal ocularity and against the noetic intuition the tradition refined out of it — "sight" keeps only the formal trait of letting-be-encountered-unconcealed; the concession to tradition (retaining the visual term) is booked as strategy, and the later Heidegger's critique of the ocular paradigm is here already licensed from within.

The fifteenth unit dethrones intuition by derivation. By showing that all sight grounds primarily in understanding — the circumspection of concern is understanding as common sense (Verständigkeit) — pure intuition (Anschauen) is deprived of its priority, which corresponds noetically to the traditional ontological priority of the present-at-hand. "Intuition" and "thinking" are both already distant derivatives of understanding; even the phenomenological "intuition of essences" (Wesensschau) grounds in existential understanding — a decision about this kind of seeing can be made only once the explicit concepts of being and being-structure are won, as which alone phenomena in the phenomenological sense can function. The genealogy is the noetic twin of § 6's ontological one: as presence-at-hand dominated the concept of being, so intuition dominated the concept of access — the two priorities stand and fall together; and the last sentence quietly subordinates Husserl's supreme court, the Wesensschau, to the existential understanding it presupposes — the master's method filed as a founded mode, its final assessment deferred to the clarified concept of being.

The sixteenth unit closes part one of the section by grounding the Introduction's Faktum. The disclosedness of the Da in understanding is itself a mode of Dasein's potentiality-of-being: in the projectedness of its being upon the for-the-sake-of-which, in one with that upon significance (world), lies disclosedness of being in general. In projecting upon possibilities, understanding of being is already anticipated; being is understood in projection, not ontologically conceived. A being with the mode of being of the essential projection of being-in-the-world has, as a constituent of its being, the understanding of being. What was earlier posited dogmatically (§ 4) now receives its demonstration from the constitution of the being in which Dasein, as understanding, is its Da; and a clarification of the existential sense of this understanding of being, satisfying within the limits of the whole investigation, can be achieved only on the ground of the temporal interpretation of being. The paragraph is architecturally decisive: the Seinsverständnis on which the whole Introduction traded is finally exhibited — it is the anticipation of being in every projection — with the strict register kept (understood, not conceived: pre-ontological, not ontology), and the promissory note signed once more to the temporal interpretation, i.e., to the book's unwritten third division.

The seventeenth unit binds the two existentials into the thrown projection and lets the enigma stand. Disposedness and understanding characterize, as existentials, the original disclosedness of being-in-the-world: in the manner of attunement Dasein "sees" possibilities from out of which it is; in the projecting disclosing of such possibilities it is in each case already attuned. The projection of its ownmost potentiality-of-being is delivered over to the factum of thrownness into the Da. Does the being of Dasein not become more enigmatic with the explication of the existential constitution of the being of the Da as thrown projection (geworfener Entwurf)? Indeed: we must first let the full enigmaticalness of this being emerge, if only to be able to founder on its "solution" in a genuine way and to pose anew the question of the being of thrown-projecting being-in-the-world. The formula geworfener Entwurf — the throw that is thrown — is the section's yield, welding §§ 29 and 31 into one structure; and the closing sentences are a rare methodological confession: the analysis has deepened the riddle, deliberately — genuine foundering on the enigma, not premature solution, is the way the question of this being's unity (care, § 41; temporality, § 65) can be forced open.

The closing unit sets the next task: in order to bring even the everyday mode of being of disposed understanding — of the full disclosedness of the Da — phenomenally and sufficiently into view, a concrete working-out of these existentials is needed. The transition licenses § 32: understanding must be followed into its own development — interpretation.

###### § 32. Understanding and Interpretation

The opening unit derives interpretation and fixes its rank. Dasein, as understanding, projects its being upon possibilities; this understanding being-toward-possibilities is itself, through the striking-back (Rückschlag) of these possibilities, as disclosed, into Dasein, a potentiality-of-being. The projecting of understanding has its own possibility of developing itself (sich auszubilden); this development of understanding we call interpretation (Auslegung). In it, understanding appropriates understandingly what it has understood; in interpretation understanding does not become something else, but itself. Interpretation grounds existentially in understanding, and understanding does not arise through interpretation: interpretation is not the taking-notice of the understood, but the working-out of the possibilities projected in understanding. In keeping with these preparatory analyses of everyday Dasein, we pursue the phenomenon of interpretation in the understanding of the world — in inauthentic understanding, and indeed in the mode of its genuineness. Every sentence legislates. The Rückschlag names the feedback that makes existence self-transforming (disclosed possibilities recoil into the discloser); the founding order is fixed against the whole hermeneutic tradition's temptation — interpretation develops understanding, never produces it; and the object-choice is flagged with the § 31 cross-division: everyday circumspective interpretation, inauthentic but genuine — the honest workshop, not the posturing seminar.

The second unit finds the as-structure in the workshop. From the significance disclosed in the understanding of world, concernful being-alongside the ready-to-hand gives itself to understand what involvement it can in each case have with what is encountered. Circumspection discovers — this means: the "world" already understood is interpreted; the ready-to-hand comes expressly into the understanding sight. All preparing, arranging, repairing, improving, supplementing accomplishes itself in this way: the circumspectively ready-to-hand is laid apart (auseinandergelegt) in its in-order-to, and attended to according to the laid-apartness that has become sighted. What is circumspectively laid apart with regard to its in-order-to as such — the expressly understood — has the structure of something as something: to the circumspective question what this determinate ready-to-hand thing is, the circumspectively interpreting answer runs: it is for... (es ist zum...). Stating the what-for is not simply naming something; what is named is understood as that as which the thing in question is to be taken. What is disclosed in understanding — the understood — is always already accessible in such a way that its "as what" can be expressly lifted out of it. The "as" constitutes the structure of the expressness of something understood: it constitutes interpretation. The circumspectively-interpreting dealing with the environmentally ready-to-hand, which "sees" this as a table, a door, a carriage, a bridge, need not necessarily also lay apart the circumspectively interpreted in a determining assertion. All pre-predicative simple seeing of the ready-to-hand is in itself already understanding-interpreting. But does not the absence of this "as" constitute the simplicity of a pure perceiving of something? The seeing of this sight is in each case already understanding-interpreting: it harbors in itself the expressness of the reference-relations (of the in-order-to) belonging to the involvement-totality from which what is simply encountered is understood. The articulation of the understood, in the interpreting bringing-near of beings along the guiding thread of "something as something," lies before the thematic assertion about it: in the assertion the "as" does not first emerge; it is only first expressed — which is possible only because it lies there as expressible. That in simple looking the expressness of an asserting can be lacking does not entitle one to deny to this simple seeing every articulating interpretation, and hence the as-structure. The simple seeing of the nearest things in having-to-do-with... carries the interpretation-structure so originally in itself that precisely an as-free grasping of something requires a certain readjustment (Umstellung): the merely-having-before-oneself of something is present in pure staring as no-longer-understanding. This as-free grasping is a privation of the simply understanding seeing — not more original than it, but derived from it. The ontic unexpressedness of the "as" must not seduce one into overlooking it as the a priori existential constitution of understanding. The paragraph is the hermeneutic revolution executed in a single sweep, and its steps must be counted. The as-structure is won from repair and arrangement, not from predication — "it is for..." as the primordial answer to "what is it?"; the pre-predicative field is claimed entire (all simple seeing already interprets — the "as" operates below assertion, which merely expresses it); and the burden of proof is reversed at the close: the bare, as-free datum — sense-data theory's foundation — is exposed as a derivative privation, an achieved staring that requires readjustment and equals no-longer-understanding. Perception's atoms are late artifacts; the interpreted whole is first.

The third unit turns the objection about meanings on its head. But if every perceiving of ready-to-hand equipment is already understanding-interpreting, letting something be encountered circumspectively as something — does this not just say: at first a pure present-at-hand thing is experienced, which is then apprehended as a door, as a house? That would be a misunderstanding of the specific disclosure-function of interpretation: it does not, as it were, throw a "signification" over the naked present-at-hand, nor paste a value onto it; rather, with the innerworldly encountered as such, there is in each case already an involvement, disclosed in the understanding of world, which interpretation lays out (herauslegt). The verb-play carries the doctrine: Auslegung as Heraus-legung — a laying-out of what lies in, not a laying-over of what is added — and the twin metaphors refused (thrown signification, pasted value) are exactly § 15's and § 21's targets: the meaning-conferring act and the value-predicate, both convicted of presupposing the naked thing the phenomena never give.

The fourth unit uncovers the fore-structure. The ready-to-hand is always already understood from the involvement-totality — which need not be explicitly grasped by a thematic interpretation; even if it has passed through such interpretation, it recedes again into unlifted understanding, and precisely in this mode it is the essential foundation of everyday, circumspective interpretation. This grounds in each case in a fore-having (Vorhabe): as appropriation of understanding, interpretation moves in understanding being toward an already understood involvement-totality. The appropriation of the understood-but-still-veiled accomplishes its unveiling always under the guidance of a respect (Hinsicht) that fixes that with regard to which the understood is to be interpreted: interpretation grounds in each case in a fore-sight (Vorsicht), which "cuts into" (anschneidet) what is taken in fore-having with a view to a determinate interpretability.
