Therewith an investigation is introduced that seeks to uncover the origin of the scientific exploration of beings and their being from this mode of being of Dasein: this Greek interpretation of the existential genesis of science is not accidental; in it comes to explicit understanding what is predelineated in Parmenides' sentence, to gar auto noein estin te kai einai — being is what shows itself in pure intuiting perceiving, and only this seeing discovers being. Original and genuine truth lies in pure intuition. This thesis remains henceforth the foundation of Western philosophy: in it the Hegelian dialectic has its motive, and only on its ground is it possible. The double reading of the Metaphysics' first sentence is a destruction in one stroke: Aristotle's "all men by nature desire to know" is rendered as "the care of seeing lies in man's being" — the origin of science located in an existential tendency (§ 3's crisis-doctrine given its ancient warrant) — and then the whole lineage is drawn taut: from Parmenides' identity of noein and einai, through the primacy of intuition, to Hegel — one thesis, one foundation, § 33's noetic genealogy now anchored at both ends.

The third unit lets Augustine testify — at length and in Latin. The remarkable priority of "seeing" was noticed above all by Augustine, in connection with his interpretation of concupiscentia (Confessions X, 35): seeing belongs properly to the eyes, but we use this word "see" for the other senses too when we bend them to knowing. We do not say: hear how it glimmers, or smell how it gleams, or taste how it shines, or feel how it glows; of all these we say: see — we say all this is seen. And we say not only "see how it shines," which the eyes alone can perceive, but also "see how it sounds," "see how it smells," "see how it tastes," "see how hard it is." Hence sense-experience in general is called "the lust of the eyes," because the other senses, by a certain likeness, appropriate to themselves the accomplishment of seeing when it is a matter of cognition, in which accomplishment the eyes have priority. The long citation is doing double duty: philologically it proves the ocular hegemony inside ordinary language itself (every sense borrows the grammar of vision when knowledge is at stake); genealogically it plants curiosity in Augustine's soil — concupiscentia oculorum, the second of the triple lust — so that the coming analysis silently secularizes a theological phenomenology Heidegger had lectured on in 1921: the existential structure retained, the sin-frame suspended (per § 38's coming disclaimer).

The fourth unit poses the question in two lines: what is it about this tendency toward mere perceiving? Which existential constitution of Dasein becomes intelligible in the phenomenon of curiosity? The brevity marks the pivot from testimony to analysis.

The fifth unit derives curiosity from rest. Being-in-the-world is at first absorbed in the world of concern; concern is guided by circumspection, which discovers the ready-to-hand and preserves it in its discoveredness — circumspection gives all procuring and performing its route of procedure, its means of execution, the right occasion, the fitting moment. Concern can come to rest, in the sense of the reposing interruption of performance or as completion. In rest, concern does not vanish; but circumspection becomes free — no longer bound to the work-world. In reposing, care settles into the freed circumspection. The circumspective discovering of the work-world has the being-character of de-severing; the freed circumspection has nothing ready-to-hand left whose bringing-near it must attend to, and, as essentially de-severant, it procures itself new possibilities of de-severing: it tends away from the nearest ready-to-hand into the far and strange world. Care becomes attending to the possibilities of seeing the "world" merely in its look (Aussehen), reposing and tarrying: Dasein seeks the far only to bring it near to itself in its look; it lets itself be carried along solely by the look of the world — a mode of being in which it attends to becoming rid of itself as being-in-the-world, rid of being alongside the nearest everyday ready-to-hand. The derivation is a small marvel of economy: curiosity is unemployed circumspection — de-severance idling — § 23's essential tendency toward nearness running on without a work-world to serve, so that the far is fetched only as look. Note the exactness of the target: not theōria (which § 29 showed to require tranquil tarrying) but its restless double; and the last clause names the stake — a mode of concern whose business is to be rid of oneself: falling's self-flight, visible in the sightseeing eye.

The sixth unit gives the three characters. Freed curiosity attends to seeing not in order to understand the seen — to come into a being toward it — but only in order to see; it seeks the new only to spring from it anew to the new. The care of this seeing is not concerned with grasping, and with being knowingly in the truth, but with possibilities of abandoning itself to the world. Hence curiosity is characterized by a specific not-tarrying (Unverweilen) with the nearest; it seeks therefore not the leisure of contemplative tarrying but restlessness and excitement through the ever-new and the change of what is encountered. In its not-tarrying, curiosity attends to the constant possibility of distraction (Zerstreuung). Curiosity has nothing to do with the wondering contemplation of beings, with thaumazein; it has no interest in being brought, by wonder, into not-understanding — it attends to a knowing, but merely in order to have known. The two constitutive moments — not-tarrying with the attended environing world and distraction into new possibilities — found the third essential character, which we call never-dwelling-anywhere (Aufenthaltslosigkeit): curiosity is everywhere and nowhere. This mode of being-in-the-world reveals a new mode of being of everyday Dasein, in which it constantly uproots itself. The triad (not-tarrying, distraction, dwelling-nowhere) is a phenomenology of restlessness with three barbs set into it: against Platonic wonder (curiosity flees the not-understanding thaumazein seeks — it wants no perplexity, § 1's lost Verlegenheit refused once more); against knowledge (its perfect tense — to have known, ticked off — versus being in the truth); and toward Division Two: Zerstreuung and Unverweilen will return in § 68's temporal analysis as the making-present that springs away (Gegenwart als Entspringen), curiosity being the existential portrait of leaping time.

The seventh unit couples the two phenomena: idle talk governs also the ways of curiosity — it says what one must have read and seen; the being-everywhere-and-nowhere of curiosity is delivered over to idle talk. These two everyday modes of being of discourse and sight are, in their uprooting tendency, not merely co-present; one way to be drags the other with it. Curiosity, to which nothing is closed, and idle talk, to which nothing remains ununderstood, give themselves — that is, give the Dasein that is in this way — the guarantee of a supposedly genuine "living life." With this supposedness, however, a third phenomenon shows itself, which characterizes the disclosedness of everyday Dasein. The interlocking is the section's structural yield: das Man's cultural agenda ("what one must have seen") steers the roving eye — talk drags sight, sight feeds talk — and their joint counterfeit is named with the era's own slogan: "lebendiges Leben," the vitalist cult of lived life, exposed as the self-certificate of uprootedness. The third phenomenon is thereby motivated from within: where everything is open and understood, the genuine and the counterfeit become indistinguishable — ambiguity.

###### § 37. Ambiguity

The opening unit defines the phenomenon by its scope. When, in everyday being-with-one-another, the kind of thing is encountered that is accessible to everyone and about which anyone can say anything, it soon becomes undecidable what is disclosed in genuine understanding and what is not. This ambiguity (Zweideutigkeit) extends not only to the world, but just as much to being-with-one-another as such, and even to Dasein's being toward itself. The definition is epistemic in form and ontological in force: ambiguity is the undecidability of genuine and ungenuine that universal accessibility itself produces — § 31's echt/unecht axis rendered publicly inoperable — and its scope-clause (world, others, self) announces the section's plan.

The second unit locates ambiguity in the projection of possibilities. Everything looks as if genuinely understood, grasped, and spoken, and at bottom is not; or does not so look, and at bottom is. Ambiguity concerns not only the disposing over and dealing with what is accessible in use and enjoyment: it has already established itself in understanding as potentiality-of-being — in the manner of the projection and pre-giving of Dasein's possibilities. Not only does everyone know and discuss what is present and occurs; everyone also already knows how to talk about what is yet to happen, what is not yet present but "really" ought to be done. Everyone has always already surmised and sensed in advance what others also surmise and sense; and this being-on-the-scent — from hearsay, for whoever is genuinely "on the scent" of a matter does not talk about it — is the most insidious way in which ambiguity pre-gives possibilities of Dasein, in order to smother them already in their force. The double-look formula (seems genuine and is not; seems not and is) states the phenomenon's perfect symmetry — ambiguity cuts both ways, hiding the genuine as effectively as it gilds the hollow — and the analysis then moves where it hurts: into the future. Public surmising colonizes the possible itself; and the parenthetical dagger (the genuine tracker keeps silent — § 34's reticence) marks the criterion ambiguity effaces: talk about the scent is the sign of not being on it. Possibilities pre-given by hearsay are strangled as possibilities — § 31's warning that thematic grasping robs the possible of its character, here executed socially.

The third unit narrates the revenge. Suppose what one surmised and sensed is one day actually translated into deed: then ambiguity has already seen to it that interest in the realized matter immediately dies off. This interest subsists only in the manner of curiosity and idle talk, as long as the possibility of a noncommittal merely-surmising-along is given; being-in-on-it, when and so long as one is on the scent, refuses allegiance once the carrying-out of the surmised begins — for with this, Dasein is in each case forced back upon itself. Idle talk and curiosity lose their power; and they take their revenge. Faced with the carrying-out of what was surmised-along, idle talk is quick with the observation: that, one could have done too — one did, after all, surmise it as well. Idle talk is in the end even indignant that what it surmised and constantly demanded now actually happens — for therewith the opportunity to keep surmising is snatched from it. The narrative is a comedy of the public sphere written as ontology: commitment expels the crowd (execution forces each back on himself — the anti-ambiguous act is individuating), and the two-step revenge — retrospective deflation ("anyone could have") and indignation at fulfillment — is observed with a moralist's eye and booked as structure: idle talk's element is the noncommittal possible, and actuality is its expropriation.

The fourth unit adds the two times. Insofar as the time of the Dasein that sets itself to work is — in the reticence of carrying-through and of genuine foundering — a different time, publicly seen an essentially slower one, than that of idle talk, which "lives faster," this idle talk has long since arrived at something else, the currently newest: what was earlier surmised and finally carried out has come too late with respect to the newest. Idle talk and curiosity, in their ambiguity, see to it that what is genuinely and newly created is, at its emergence, obsolete for the public; it can become free in its positive possibilities only when the covering idle talk has become ineffective and the "common" interest has died off. This is the book's philosophy of intellectual history in one paragraph — two temporalities, the slow time of work (with genuine foundering expressly included in it) and the fast time of talk — with a law of reception as corollary: the created arrives publicly obsolete, and is freed only posthumously to the chatter. Written in 1926, the passage reads as the author's advance directive for his own book's fate; systematically, it plants the theme of § 65 ff.: modes of being differ as temporalizations.

The fifth unit draws the inversion: the ambiguity of public interpretedness passes off the talking-in-advance and curious surmising as the authentic happening, and stamps carrying-out and action as something subsequent and inconsequential. The understanding of Dasein in das Man thus constantly mistakes itself (versieht sich) in its projections regarding the genuine possibilities of being. Ambiguously, Dasein is always "there" — in the public disclosedness of being-with-one-another, where the loudest idle talk and the most ingenious curiosity keep the "business" (Betrieb) going — there, where everyday everything and at bottom nothing happens. The inversion is total: anticipation counts as the event, the deed as its footnote — and the closing epigram (everything happens and nothing happens) names the Betrieb, the hum of busy-ness that § 38 will re-encounter, as the everyday form of history-less happening.

The sixth unit is a hinge in two lines: this ambiguity always plays to curiosity what it seeks, and gives idle talk the semblance of having everything decided in it. The three phenomena lock: ambiguity is the medium in which the other two thrive — supply for the roving eye, the air of verdict for the talk.

The seventh unit extends ambiguity into being-with itself. This mode of being of the disclosedness of being-in-the-world pervades also being-with-one-another as such: the other is at first "there" from out of what one has heard of him, what one says and knows about him — into original being-with-one-another, idle talk first insinuates itself. Everyone watches the other first and foremost: how he will comport himself, what he will say to something. Being-with-one-another in das Man is not at all a sealed-off, indifferent side-by-side, but a tense, ambiguous watching-one-another, a secret mutual listening-in (Sich-gegenseitig-abhören): under the mask of the for-one-another, an against-one-another plays. The portrait corrects a possible misreading of § 27: the public mode of being-with is not bland juxtaposition but surveillance — reputation preceding encounter (the other "there" from hearsay first), mutual monitoring under the mask of solicitude. The sentence about mask and counter-play is as dark as the book gets about everyday sociality, and it is offered, per the preamble, without moral verdict: this is the structure of publicly mediated Mitsein, not an indictment of individuals.

The closing unit secures the phenomenon's origin and status: it must be noted that ambiguity does not first spring from an express intent to disguise and distort, nor is it first evoked by the individual Dasein — it lies already in being-with-one-another as thrown being-with-one-another in a world. But publicly it is precisely hidden, and one will always resist the suggestion that this interpretation of the mode of being of das Man's interpretedness is apt. It would be a misunderstanding if the explication of these phenomena were to seek confirmation in the assent of das Man. The three closing moves complete the section's logic: no conspirator (ambiguity is thrown, structural — the § 35 pattern of guiltless concealment again); self-concealing (the phenomenon hides itself publicly, so resistance to the analysis is predicted by the analysis); and the methodological corollary, cut off mid-sentence by the section-break but complete in sense: the account of das Man cannot be verified by das Man's agreement — public assent would be Gerede about Gerede, and the analysis must appeal past its object to the phenomena.

###### § 38. Falling and Thrownness

The opening unit gathers and names. The phenomena of idle talk, curiosity, and ambiguity were set forth in such a way that among them a connection of being already indicates itself; the mode of being of this connection is now to be grasped existentially-ontologically. The basic kind of the being of everydayness is to be understood within the horizon of the structures of Dasein's being won so far. The section's task is stated as a demand for unity: three phenomena, one movement — the chapter's threefold everyday (talk, sight, interpretation in their fallen modes) awaits its single name.

The second unit gives it: idle talk, curiosity, and ambiguity characterize the way in which Dasein everyday is its "Da" — the disclosedness of being-in-the-world. As existential determinations these characters are not present-at-hand at Dasein; they co-constitute its being. In them and in their connection of being, a basic kind of the being of everydayness reveals itself, which we call the falling (Verfallen) of Dasein. The naming-sentence keeps the strict register (existentials, not properties), and the term arrives with its dangerous connotations — which the next four units, in one of the book's most careful sequences of guards, will disarm one by one.

The third unit issues the first guard and defines. The title, which expresses no negative valuation, is to signify: Dasein is proximally and mostly alongside the attended "world." This absorption in... has mostly the character of being-lost in the publicness of das Man. Dasein has, as authentic potentiality-of-being-a-self, proximally always already fallen away from itself and fallen upon the "world" (an die »Welt« verfallen). Fallenness upon the "world" means absorption in being-with-one-another, insofar as this is led by idle talk, curiosity, and ambiguity. What we called the inauthenticity of Dasein (§ 9) now receives, through the interpretation of falling, a sharper determination. But "in-" and "not-authentic" by no means signify "really not," as though Dasein with this mode of being lost its being altogether: inauthenticity so little means anything like no-longer-being-in-the-world that it constitutes precisely a distinctive being-in-the-world — one wholly taken in by the "world" and the co-Dasein of others in das Man. Not-being-itself functions as a positive possibility of the being that, essentially attending, is absorbed in a world; this not-being must be conceived as the nearest mode of being of Dasein, in which it mostly maintains itself. The double definition (away from itself, upon the world — Abfall and Verfall in one motion) fixes falling's vector, and the guard is the strongest yet: inauthenticity is a distinctive, positive being-in-the-world — the "not" of not-being-oneself is a mode, not a lack (§ 9's promise honored with interest). Falling is where Dasein mostly lives, not where it occasionally sins.

The fourth unit bars the theological reading: Dasein's fallenness must therefore not be conceived as a "fall" from a purer and higher "primal state" — of that we have not only, ontically, no experience, but also, ontologically, no possibilities and no guiding threads of interpretation. The Adamic frame is refused on both registers at once: no ontic memory of Eden, no ontological warrant for postulating one — the analysis will not borrow the status integritatis even as a foil (the closing units return to seal this).

The fifth unit bars the causal-external reading: from itself, as factical being-in-the-world, Dasein as falling has already fallen away; and it has fallen not upon some being it first collides with in the course of its being — or does not — but upon the world that itself belongs to its being. Falling is an existential determination of Dasein itself and says nothing about it as present-at-hand — nothing about present-at-hand relations to beings from which it "descends" or with which it has subsequently come into a commercium. The precision is structural: the "whither" of the fall is the world that Dasein is (being-in-the-world falling into its own worldly moment) — no external seducer, no genealogical descent, no acquired bad company; falling is self-relation, which is why no change of circumstances cures it.

The sixth unit bars the progressivist reading: the ontological-existential structure of falling would likewise be misunderstood if one wished to attach to it the sense of a bad and deplorable ontic property, perhaps removable in advanced stages of human culture. The third guard completes the triangle: neither theology's fall, nor causality's contamination, nor the Enlightenment's remediable defect — falling is constitution, so no cultural progress retires it; the barb reaches every perfectionism, religious or secular.

The seventh unit repositions the whole prior analytic. At the first indication of being-in-the-world as Dasein's basic constitution, as in the characterization of its constitutive structural moments, the mode of being of this constitution remained phenomenally unattended behind the analysis of the constitution itself. The possible basic kinds of being-in, concern and solicitude, were described; but the question of the everyday mode of being of these ways to be remained undiscussed. Being-in also showed itself to be anything but a merely contemplating or acting confrontation — a co-presence-at-hand of a subject and an object; nevertheless the semblance had to remain that being-in-the-world functions as a rigid framework (Gerüst) within which Dasein's possible comportments toward its world run their course, without the "framework" itself being touched in its being. But this supposed framework itself co-constitutes the mode of being of Dasein: an existential mode of being-in-the-world documents itself in the phenomenon of falling. The self-correction is architectural: everything since § 12 described the constitution; falling is the discovery that the constitution has a how — being-in-the-world is not a stage but itself happens, and the everydayness elected in § 9 now shows itself as a mode of being of the basic constitution itself, in motion.

The eighth unit re-runs the triad as disclosure-in-closure: idle talk discloses to Dasein the understanding being toward its world, toward others, and toward itself — but so that this being-toward has the mode of a groundless floating; curiosity discloses each and every thing — but so that being-in is everywhere and nowhere; ambiguity conceals nothing from Dasein's understanding — but only in order to suppress being-in-the-world in the uprooted everywhere-and-nowhere. The three formulas share one syntax — discloses, but so that — which is the precise ontology of falling: not blindness but a disclosedness whose mode defeats it; the Da fully lit, and lost.

The ninth unit poses the kinetic question: only with the ontological clarification of the mode of being of everyday being-in-the-world glimpsed in these phenomena do we gain the existentially sufficient determination of Dasein's basic constitution. Which structure does the "movedness" (Bewegtheit) of falling show? The scare-quoted Bewegtheit announces a new register — the analytic's first dynamics — with the term carefully held apart from physical motion (an aside Heidegger's Aristotle-lectures make explicit: kinēsis rethought existentially).

The tenth unit locates the tempter. Idle talk, and the public interpretedness enclosed in it, constitutes itself in being-with-one-another: it is not present-at-hand as a detached product of it, standing for itself within the world; and just as little can it be volatilized into a "universal" that, since it belongs essentially to nobody, is "really" nothing and occurs "really" only in the individual speaking Dasein. Idle talk is the mode of being of being-with-one-another itself, and does not first arise through certain circumstances working on Dasein "from outside." But if Dasein itself, in idle talk and public interpretedness, pre-gives to itself the possibility of losing itself in das Man, of falling into groundlessness, this says: Dasein prepares for itself the constant temptation (Versuchung) to fall. Being-in-the-world is in itself tempting (versucherisch). The ontological placement repeats § 27's double refusal (neither detached product nor nominalist fiction) and then draws the momentous conclusion: the temptation is home-made — Dasein tempts itself; no serpent enters the analysis, because being-in-the-world, harboring its own public interpretedness, is the tempter. Augustine's tentatio (the 1921 lectures' central category) is thereby de-theologized into structure: the first of four moments of the movement.

The eleventh unit gives the second: having thus already become a temptation to itself, public interpretedness holds Dasein fast in its fallenness. Idle talk and ambiguity, the having-seen-everything and having-understood-everything, develop the supposedness that the disclosedness of Dasein so available and dominant could guarantee to it the security, genuineness, and fullness of all possibilities of its being. The self-certainty and decidedness of das Man spreads a growing needlessness (Unbedürftigkeit) of authentic disposed understanding; the supposedness of das Man — that it nourishes and leads the full and genuine "life" — brings a tranquilization (Beruhigung) into Dasein, for which everything is "in the best order" and all doors stand open. Falling being-in-the-world, tempting itself, is at the same time tranquilizing. The second moment names the anesthetic: not deception about facts but the manufactured needlessness of questioning — all doors open, nothing required — § 35's insurance against foundering generalized into a metaphysical complacency; and the "vollen und echten Lebens" repeats § 36's vitalist counterfeit as the tranquilizer's label.

The twelfth unit corrects the image of rest: this tranquilization in inauthentic being does not, however, seduce to standstill and inactivity, but drives into the unrestraint of "business" (Betrieb). Being-fallen upon the "world" does not now somehow come to rest: tempting tranquilization intensifies the falling. With special regard to the interpretation of Dasein, the opinion can now arise that understanding the most foreign cultures, and the "synthesis" of these with one's own, leads to the complete and first genuine enlightenment of Dasein about itself: versatile curiosity and restless knowing-it-all masquerade as universal understanding of Dasein. But at bottom it remains indeterminate and unasked what is really to be understood; it remains ununderstood that understanding itself is a potentiality-of-being that must become free solely in one's ownmost Dasein. In this tranquilized, all-"understanding" comparing of itself with everything, Dasein drives toward an alienation (Entfremdung) in which its ownmost potentiality-of-being conceals itself from it. Falling being-in-the-world is, as tempting-tranquilizing, at the same time alienating. The paradox is exact — a sedative that accelerates: tranquility discharges as busyness, the Betrieb of § 37 — and the polemical instance is chosen from philosophy's own house: the era's comparative culture-synthesis (§ 6's and § 11's typology-critique returning) as falling's highbrow form, its error stated in one clause — understanding mistaken for a stock of contents rather than a Seinkönnen to be freed in one's own existence. The third moment, Entfremdung, thus means estrangement from one's potentiality, not from an essence.

The thirteenth unit sharpens alienation into the fourth moment. This alienation cannot in turn mean that Dasein is factically torn away from itself: on the contrary, it drives Dasein into a mode of being bent on the most exaggerated "self-dissection," which essays every possibility of interpretation, so that the "characterologies" and "typologies" it displays have themselves already become innumerable. This alienation, which closes off to Dasein its authenticity and possibility — even if only as the possibility of a genuine foundering — nevertheless does not deliver it over to beings that it itself is not, but forces it into its inauthenticity, into a possible mode of being of itself. The tempting-tranquilizing alienation of falling leads, in its own movedness, to Dasein's becoming entangled (sich verfängt) in itself. The correction is essential and subtle: alienation is not self-loss into the alien but hyper-preoccupation with oneself — the boom of characterology and typology (Klages, Spranger, the psycho-graphic industry of the 1920s) diagnosed as falling's introspective form: endless self-dissection as the perfect way to miss the self, since the self is a Seinkönnen, not a specimen. Even the closed-off authenticity is measured generously — "if only as genuine foundering": authenticity's possibility includes failing authentically, a clause of great weight for Division Two. The fourth moment: das Verfängnis, entanglement — Dasein snared in itself.

The fourteenth unit names the movement: the exhibited phenomena of temptation, tranquilization, alienation, and self-entanglement (entanglement) characterize the specific mode of being of falling. We call this "movedness" of Dasein in its own being the plunge (Absturz): Dasein plunges out of itself into itself — into the groundlessness and nullity of inauthentic everydayness. But this plunge remains hidden from it by the public interpretedness, so much so that it is interpreted as "ascent" and "concrete life." The kinetics culminate in a fall without an outside: aus ihm selbst in es selbst — origin and terminus the same being, the plunge a self-relation (no height lost toward any below but its own groundless everydayness) — and the concealment is built in: the fall reads, publicly, as rising; decadence as vitality. "Nullity" (Nichtigkeit) sounds here for the first time in this register, a word § 58 will make load-bearing.

The fifteenth unit adds the vortex: the movement-kind of the plunge into and within the groundlessness of inauthentic being in das Man constantly tears understanding away from the projecting of authentic possibilities, and tears it into the tranquilized supposedness of possessing or attaining everything. This constant tearing-away from authenticity, together with the constant simulation of it, in one with the tearing-into das Man, characterizes the movedness of falling as vortex (Wirbel). The second kinetic figure completes the first: the plunge has spin — a double tearing (away from the authentic, into the one) plus permanent counterfeit of what it removes — turbulence as the everyday's mode of motion, against every static picture of inauthenticity as mere torpor.

The sixteenth unit closes the circuit with thrownness. Falling determines not only being-in-the-world existentially: the vortex reveals at the same time the throw- and movedness-character of thrownness, which, in Dasein's disposedness, can force itself upon Dasein itself. Thrownness is not only not a "finished fact"; it is also not a closed-off factum: to its facticity belongs that Dasein, as long as it is what it is, remains in the throw (im Wurf) and is whirled into the inauthenticity of das Man. Thrownness, in which facticity lets itself be seen phenomenally, belongs to Dasein, for which, in its being, this being itself is at issue: Dasein exists factically. The section-title's conjunction is here cashed: falling is thrownness in motion — the throw not a past event (neither finished nor closed) but ongoing; one remains in the throw, whirled — so § 29's Geworfenheit receives the "existential concretion" the preamble promised: everyday whirling is how being-thrown feels and works. The closing four words (Dasein existiert faktisch) compress the chapter: facticity and existence, throw and project, one being.

The seventeenth unit meets the deepest objection and converts it into proof. But is not, with this exhibition of falling, a phenomenon set forth that speaks directly against the determination with which the formal idea of existence was indicated? Can Dasein be conceived as the being whose being is concerned with potentiality-of-being, if precisely in its everydayness this being has lost itself and, in falling, "lives" away from itself? Falling upon the world is a phenomenal "proof" against Dasein's existentiality only if Dasein is posited as an isolated I-subject, a self-point from which it moves away — then the world is an object, and falling upon it gets ontologically reinterpreted as presence-at-hand in the manner of an innerworldly being. But if we hold fast to Dasein's being in the exhibited constitution of being-in-the-world, it becomes manifest that falling, as the mode of being of this being-in, furnishes rather the most elementary proof for Dasein's existentiality: in falling, nothing else is at issue than the potentiality-of-being-in-the-world, though in the mode of inauthenticity. Dasein can fall only because it is concerned with understanding-disposed being-in-the-world; conversely, authentic existence is nothing that floats above falling everydayness — existentially it is only a modified seizing of this. The dialectic is the chapter's crown: the objection (a self-losing being cannot be the being whose being is at issue) is traced to the self-point ontology and inverted — only a being at issue for itself can flee itself; falling presupposes care (§ 39 will build on exactly this: even in flight, Dasein pursues its being). And the counter-guard lands with equal weight: authenticity does not hover above the everyday but is its modified seizure — § 27's modification-theorem repeated at the chapter's exit, barring the two-world reading of the book forever.

The eighteenth unit refuses the "night-view": the phenomenon of falling gives nothing like a "night view" of Dasein, an ontically occurring property that might serve to complete its harmless aspect. Falling reveals an essential ontological structure of Dasein itself, which so little determines its night-side that it constitutes all its days in their everydayness. The Schopenhauerian idiom (the pessimist's Nachtansicht) is dismissed with a fine inversion: falling is not the dark supplement to a daylight nature — it constitutes the days themselves; everydayness through and through, neither shadow nor exception.

The nineteenth unit settles accounts with theology. The existential-ontological interpretation therefore also makes no ontic assertion about the "corruption of human nature" — not because the necessary means of proof are lacking, but because its problematic lies before every assertion about corruption and incorruption. Falling is an ontological concept of movement. Ontically it is not decided whether man is "drowned in sin," in the status corruptionis, whether he walks in the status integritatis, or finds himself in an intermediate stage, the status gratiae. But faith and "worldview," insofar as they assert this or that, and insofar as they assert about Dasein as being-in-the-world, will have to come back to the existential structures set forth — provided their assertions at the same time raise a claim to conceptual understanding. The paragraph fixes the relation of the analytic to theology with juridical care: neutrality by priority, not by agnosticism — the existential concept of falling lies before the alternatives of sin and integrity (Luther's drowning-in-sin quoted from Heidegger's own theological formation), and the closing conditional is the quiet imperialism of fundamental ontology: any faith that speaks conceptually of man-in-the-world must route its concepts through these structures — § 3's theology-crisis and the 1927 "Phenomenology and Theology" program, restated as a demand.

The twentieth unit tallies the chapter: the guiding question concerned the being of the Da; the theme became the ontological constitution of the disclosedness essentially belonging to Dasein, whose being constitutes itself in disposedness, understanding, and discourse. The everyday mode of being of disclosedness is characterized by idle talk, curiosity, and ambiguity; and these themselves show the movedness of falling, with the essential characters of temptation, tranquilization, alienation, and entanglement. The summary is the chapter's table of contents recited as result — constitution (three existentials), everyday mode (three counterfeits), movement (four moments) — the symmetry of § 28's plan closed.

The closing unit hands the whole to Chapter Six: with this analysis, the whole of Dasein's existential constitution has been laid free in its main features, and the phenomenal soil won for the "summarizing" interpretation of Dasein's being as care. The scare-quotes around "summarizing" are a warning the next chapter will justify: care is not the sum of the moments but their original unity — and the question of how a thrown, projecting, falling, discursive being can be one at all is exactly where § 39 begins.

#### Chapter Six: Care as the Being of Dasein

##### § 39. The Question of the Original Totality of Dasein's Structural Whole

The opening unit takes stock and names the danger. Being-in-the-world is an originally and constantly whole structure; in the preceding chapters it was phenomenally clarified as a whole and, always on this ground, in its constitutive moments. The preview of the whole phenomenon given at the outset (§ 12) has now lost the emptiness of its first general predelineation. But the phenomenal manifoldness of the constitution of the structural whole, and of its everyday mode of being, can now easily obstruct (verstellen) the unified phenomenological view of the whole as such — and this view must be kept all the freer and held ready all the more securely as we now pose the question toward which the preparatory fundamental analysis of Dasein has all along been striving: how is the totality of the exhibited structural whole to be determined existentially-ontologically? The paradox is stated candidly: the analysis's very success — its wealth of moments — threatens the unity it began from; the division-preamble's whole-first rule now returns as the chapter's task, no longer as a precaution but as the question itself.

The second unit assembles the full formula of everydayness. Dasein exists factically; asked for is the ontological unity of existentiality and facticity — the essential belonging of the latter to the former. On the ground of the disposedness essentially belonging to it, Dasein has a mode of being in which it is brought before itself and disclosed to itself in its thrownness; but thrownness is the mode of being of a being that in each case is its possibilities themselves, in such a way that it understands itself in and from them (projects itself upon them). Being-in-the-world — to which being alongside the ready-to-hand belongs as originally as being-with others — is in each case for the sake of itself; but the self is proximally and mostly inauthentic, the they-self, and being-in-the-world is always already fallen. Average everydayness can accordingly be determined as: falling-disclosed, thrown-projecting being-in-the-world, which, in its being alongside the "world" and in being-with with others, is concerned with its ownmost potentiality-of-being itself. The sentence is Division One compressed to a single clause — every chapter contributes a participle — and its very length poses the problem: the formula concatenates; the phenomenon must unify. The question of care is the question whether this grammatical monster names one being.

The third unit poses the triple question: can this structural whole of Dasein's everydayness be grasped in its totality? Can Dasein's being be lifted out unitarily, so that from it the essential equiprimordiality of the exhibited structures becomes intelligible, together with the belonging existential possibilities of modification? Is there a way to win this being phenomenally on the soil of the present approach of the existential analytic? The three demands calibrate success in advance: totality, equiprimordiality made intelligible (not abolished — § 28's rule holds), and the modifications (authentic/inauthentic) derivable — care must ground the moments and their modes at once.

The fourth unit legislates negatively and screens the candidates. Negatively it stands beyond question: the totality of the structural whole is not to be reached phenomenally by assembling the elements — that would require a building-plan. The being of Dasein, which ontologically bears the structural whole as such, becomes accessible in a full look through this whole toward an originally unitary phenomenon that already lies in the whole, so that it ontologically founds every structural moment in its structural possibility. The "summarizing" interpretation can therefore be no collecting combination of what has been won. The question of Dasein's existential basic character is essentially different from the question of the being of something present-at-hand: everyday environmental experience, directed ontically and ontologically at innerworldly beings, cannot pregive Dasein ontically-originally for the ontological analysis; likewise, the immanent perception of lived experiences lacks an ontologically sufficient guiding thread; nor, on the other hand, is Dasein's being to be deduced from an idea of man. Can it be gathered from the interpretation of Dasein so far which ontic-ontological access to itself it demands, from itself, as the sole appropriate one? The building-plan argument repeats § 28's schema-critique at the level of the whole (assembly presupposes the unity it fakes), and the triple screening eliminates the classical accesses by name: outer experience (reads Dasein worldly — § 5's Rückstrahlung), inner perception (reads it as Erlebnis-stream — § 25's trap), and deduction from an idea of man (§ 10's anthropology). What remains is the book's signature move: let the being itself nominate its access.

The fifth unit finds the criterion in three lines: to Dasein's ontological structure belongs understanding of being — being, it is disclosed to itself in its being; disposedness and understanding constitute the mode of being of this disclosedness. Is there an understanding disposedness in Dasein, in which it is disclosed to itself in a distinguished way? The question operationalizes § 29's methodological theorem (the analytic listens in on Dasein's own disclosures): sought is a mood that understands — a disposedness whose disclosure reaches the whole.

The sixth unit states the requirements: if the existential analytic is to retain fundamental clarity about its fundamental-ontological function, then for mastering its provisional task — the exhibition of Dasein's being — it must seek one of the most far-reaching and most original possibilities of disclosure lying in Dasein itself. The manner of disclosing in which Dasein brings itself before itself must be such that in it Dasein becomes accessible in a certain way simplified; with what is disclosed in it, the structural totality of the sought being must then come elementarily to light. Two criteria — simplification and totality — define the method: the mood must strip the camouflage (the innerworldly clutter to which Dasein clings) and expose the whole in elemental form; the analytic, unable to construct unity, must catch Dasein in the act of being disclosed to itself as one.

The seventh unit nominates anxiety and maps the chapter. As a disposedness satisfying such methodical requirements, the phenomenon of anxiety (Angst) is laid at the basis of the analysis. The working-out of this basic disposedness, and the ontological characterization of what is disclosed in it as such, takes its departure from the phenomenon of falling, and demarcates anxiety against the previously analyzed kindred phenomenon of fear. Anxiety, as a possibility of being of Dasein, together with the Dasein itself disclosed in it, gives the phenomenal soil for the explicit grasping of Dasein's original totality of being: its being unveils itself as care (Sorge). The ontological working-out of this existential basic phenomenon demands demarcation against phenomena that might at first be identified with care: will, wish, propensity, urge — care cannot be derived from them, because they are themselves founded in it. The nomination is flagged as such (the next section opens by admitting it is "at first an assertion"), and the anti-derivation rule is posted in advance: the conative family (Wille, Wunsch, Hang, Drang) — psychology's candidates for the root of striving — will be shown to presuppose care, per § 28's ban on the Urgrund-derivation in reverse: care is not a super-drive.

The eighth unit anticipates the estrangement and promises attestation. The ontological interpretation of Dasein as care lies — like every ontological analysis with what it wins — far from what remains accessible to the pre-ontological understanding of being, let alone to ontic acquaintance with beings; that common understanding finds the ontologically known strange, measured against the only thing it knows ontically, cannot surprise. Nonetheless even the ontic approach of the attempted interpretation of Dasein qua care may appear contrived and theoretically excogitated — to say nothing of the violence one might see in the exclusion of the transmitted and confirmed definition of man. Hence a pre-ontological attestation (Bewährung) of the existential interpretation of Dasein as care is needed: it lies in the demonstration that Dasein, early on, when it spoke itself out about itself, interpreted itself as care (cura) — though only pre-ontologically. The paragraph is a rare piece of rhetorical self-consciousness: Heidegger concedes his result will look artificial and violent (animal rationale "excluded" — § 10's asceticism owned as scandal), and answers with a novel evidentiary form — the pre-ontological document, § 42's Cura-fable, in which Dasein's own ancient self-interpretation is called as witness for the ontology; § 4's pre-ontological understanding converted into a court of appeal.

The ninth unit widens the chapter beyond anthropology. The analytic that presses forward to the phenomenon of care is to prepare the fundamental-ontological problematic — the question of the meaning of being in general. To direct the view expressly toward this from what has been won, beyond the special task of an existential-a-priori anthropology, the phenomena standing in closest connection with the guiding question of being must be grasped retrospectively and more penetratingly: the modes of being explicated so far, readiness-to-hand and presence-at-hand, which determine innerworldly beings of non-Dasein-like character. Because the ontological problematic hitherto understood being primarily in the sense of presence-at-hand ("reality," "world"-actuality), while Dasein's being remained ontologically undetermined, a discussion is needed of the ontological connection of care, worldhood, readiness-to-hand, and presence-at-hand (reality) — leading to a sharper determination of the concept of reality, in the context of a discussion of the epistemological questions of realism and idealism oriented to this idea. The unit motivates § 43 from the book's deepest stratum: the analytic is not anthropology (the standing disclaimer, § 5), so its yield must be turned back onto the being-question — and since the tradition's name for being was "reality," care must now confront reality, realism, and idealism.

The tenth unit states, in advance, the theses of § 43 and § 44. Beings are independent of the experience, acquaintance, and grasping through which they are disclosed, discovered, and determined; but being "is" only in the understanding of that being to whose being something like an understanding of being belongs. Being can therefore be unconceptualized, but it is never completely un-understood. In the ontological problematic, being and truth have from of old been brought together, if not identified: therein is documented — though perhaps hidden in its original grounds — the necessary connection of being and understanding. For the sufficient preparation of the question of being, the ontological clarification of the phenomenon of truth is therefore needed; it is accomplished first on the soil of what the preceding interpretation has won with the phenomena of disclosedness and discoveredness, interpretation and assertion. The first two sentences are among the book's most quoted and most disputed, and their balance is everything: realism about beings (independent of all access), the understanding-condition for being — a distinction the entire idealism/realism quarrel of § 43 will turn on, and which only the ontological difference makes stateable. The second pair (being and truth ancient companions) motivates § 44 with a destructive observation: the tradition's own equation of on and alēthes testifies, without understanding itself, to the bond of being and disclosedness.

The closing unit gives the chapter's table: the conclusion of the preparatory fundamental analysis has as its theme: the basic disposedness of anxiety as a distinguished disclosedness of Dasein (§ 40); the being of Dasein as care (§ 41); the attestation of the existential interpretation of Dasein as care from Dasein's pre-ontological self-interpretation (§ 42); Dasein, worldhood, and reality (§ 43); Dasein, disclosedness, and truth (§ 44). The map confirms the chapter's double character: two sections of construction (anxiety, care), one of attestation, two of confrontation with the tradition's master-concepts (reality, truth) — Division One to close by measuring its yield against the two oldest names for what is.

##### § 40. The Basic Disposedness of Anxiety as a Distinguished Disclosedness of Dasein

The opening unit poses the methodological question: a possibility of being of Dasein is to give ontic "information" about Dasein itself as a being — information possible only in the disclosedness belonging to Dasein, which grounds in disposedness and understanding. In what way is anxiety a distinguished disposedness? How is Dasein, in it, brought before itself by its own being, so that phenomenologically the being disclosed in anxiety can be determined in its being as such — or this determination sufficiently prepared? The double question fixes the section's burden of proof: anxiety must be shown distinguished (against all other moods) and shown to bring Dasein before itself (against § 29's rule that moods mostly turn away).

The second unit chooses the unlikely starting point. Intending to press forward to the being of the totality of the structural whole, we take our departure from the concrete analyses of falling just carried through. Absorption in das Man and in the attended "world" manifests something like a flight (Flucht) of Dasein before itself as authentic potentiality-of-being-a-self. But this phenomenon — Dasein's flight before itself and its authenticity — seems least of all suited to serve as phenomenal soil for the following investigation: in this flight Dasein precisely does not bring itself before itself; the turning-away, in keeping with falling's ownmost trait, leads away from Dasein. Yet with such phenomena the investigation must guard against conflating the ontic-existentiell characterization with the ontological-existential interpretation — against overlooking the positive phenomenal foundations the former contains for the latter. The objection is raised in full strength (how learn about the self from the movement that abandons it?) so that the answer, the section's methodological jewel, can be earned rather than assumed.

The third unit delivers it. Existentielly, in falling, the authenticity of being-a-self is closed off and thrust aside — but this closedness is only the privation of a disclosedness, which manifests itself phenomenally in this: that Dasein's flight is flight before itself. In the before-which of flight, Dasein comes precisely "after" itself. Only insofar as Dasein is, by its ontological essence, brought before itself at all through the disclosedness belonging to it, can it flee before itself; in this falling turning-away the before-which of the flight is indeed not grasped, not even experienced in a turning-toward — but it is, in the turning-away from it, disclosed as "there." The existentiell-ontic turning-away, on the ground of its disclosedness-character, gives phenomenally the possibility of grasping the before-which of the flight existentially-ontologically as such: within the ontic "away from" lying in the turning-away, the before-which can be understood and brought to concept in a phenomenologically interpreting "turning-toward." The argument turns § 29's evasion-theorem into an instrument: flight is negative testimony — one flees only what is disclosed, so the fugitive carries the map of what he flees; the interpreter has only to reverse the vector (the ontic away-from read as the ontological toward-which). Closedness as privation of disclosure: § 7 A's founding of semblance on showing, now working at the analytic's most delicate joint.

The fourth unit generalizes the method and posts the claim: orienting the analysis by the phenomenon of falling is thus not in principle condemned to hopelessness of learning something ontological about the Dasein disclosed in it — on the contrary, precisely here the interpretation is least delivered over to an artificial self-apprehension of Dasein; it merely carries out the explication of what Dasein itself ontically discloses. The possibility of pressing forward to Dasein's being, by interpretively going-along-with and going-after within a disposed understanding, increases the more original the phenomenon that functions methodically as disclosing disposedness. That anxiety accomplishes this is at first an assertion. The paragraph completes § 29's hermeneutic protocol: interpretation as accompaniment (Mit- und Nachgehen) of Dasein's own disclosure, its yield indexed to the originality of the mood employed — and the candid last sentence ("at first an assertion") is the book's method at its most honest: the claim will be cashed phenomenally or not at all.

The fifth unit clears the terminological ground: for the analysis of anxiety we are not wholly unprepared, though it remains dark how it hangs together ontologically with fear. Manifestly there is a phenomenal kinship, whose sign is the fact that the two phenomena mostly remain undistinguished: what is fear gets designated anxiety, and what has the character of anxiety gets called fear. We attempt to press forward to the phenomenon step by step. The everyday lexical confusion is itself made evidence of kinship — and the section's care with the pair (Angst/Furcht) sets the terminological standard the whole later literature, from theology to psychoanalysis, would inherit.

The sixth unit runs the differential through fear's own grid. Dasein's falling upon das Man and the attended "world" we called a "flight" before itself. But not every shrinking-back before..., not every turning-away from... is necessarily flight: the shrinking-back founded in fear, before what fear discloses — the threatening — has the character of flight. The interpretation of fear as disposedness showed: the before-which of fear is in each case an innerworldly being, approaching from a determinate region, in nearness, detrimental, and able to stay away. In falling, Dasein turns away from itself; the before-which of this shrinking-back must in general have the character of threatening, yet it is a being of the same mode of being as the one shrinking back — Dasein itself. This before-which cannot be grasped as something "fearsome," for the fearsome is always encountered as an innerworldly being; the threat that alone can be "fearsome," and that is discovered in fear, always comes from innerworldly beings. The § 30 grid pays its dividend: falling's turning-away fits fear's form (threat) but breaks its material condition (innerworldly provenance) — the threatening here is the shrinking being itself, so a mood other than fear must be in play; the differential diagnosis is complete before anxiety is even named.

The seventh unit draws the founding-order: the turning-away of falling is therefore no fleeing founded on fear of innerworldly beings — a flight-character so grounded belongs to it least of all, since this turning-away precisely turns toward innerworldly beings, as absorption in them. The turning-away of falling grounds rather in anxiety, which in its turn first makes fear possible. The inversion is double and decisive: falling flees into the innerworldly (so no innerworldly item is its motor), and fear is demoted to founded status — the § 30 phenomenon, analyzed first, turns out to be anxiety fallen upon the world (the closing units will say it verbatim). The ontic order of familiarity (fear common, anxiety rare) is the reverse of the ontological order of founding.

The eighth unit names the before-which. To understand talk of Dasein's falling flight before itself, being-in-the-world as this being's basic constitution must be recalled: the before-which of anxiety is being-in-the-world as such. How does what anxiety is anxious before differ phenomenally from what fear fears? The before-which of anxiety is no innerworldly being — hence it can essentially have no involvement. The threat has not the character of a determinate detrimentality striking the threatened in a determinate respect regarding a particular factical potentiality-of-being: the before-which of anxiety is completely indeterminate. This indeterminacy not only leaves factually undecided which innerworldly being threatens; it says that innerworldly beings are not "relevant" at all. Nothing of what is ready-to-hand and present-at-hand within the world functions as that before which anxiety is anxious; the innerworldly discovered involvement-totality of the ready-to-hand and present-at-hand is as such altogether without import — it collapses into itself (sinkt in sich zusammen). The world has the character of complete insignificance (Unbedeutsamkeit). In anxiety there is encountered nothing that, as threatening, could have an involvement. The definition proceeds by strict negation of § 30's six moments — no entity, no involvement, no determinate detrimentality, no region — and its positive content is precisely the negative event: the collapse of the involvement-totality, significance switched off entire. Where § 16's breakdown suspended one reference and let world flash, anxiety suspends the whole web: the mood is worldhood's total eclipse-experiment, performed by Dasein's own being.

The ninth unit adds the nowhere and the suffocating nearness. Hence anxiety also does not "see" a determinate "here" and "yonder" from which the threatening approaches: that the threatening is nowhere characterizes anxiety's before-which. Anxiety "knows not" what it is anxious before; but "nowhere" does not mean nothing — in it lies region in general, disclosedness of world in general for essentially spatial being-in. The threatening therefore also cannot approach from a determinate direction within nearness: it is already "there" — and yet nowhere; so near that it oppresses and takes one's breath away — and yet nowhere. The paragraph turns § 22's spatiality inside out: the nowhere is not privation of place but the naked region-structure itself, exposed when no direction carries a threat; and the phenomenology of the closing clause — the unlocalizable pressure at the throat — earns the word Angst its etymology (angustiae, Enge: the strait, the narrows) without ever citing it.

The tenth unit converts the double negation into the positive finding. In anxiety's before-which, the "it is nothing and nowhere" becomes manifest; and the obstinacy of the innerworldly nothing-and-nowhere says phenomenally: anxiety's before-which is the world as such. The complete insignificance announcing itself in the nothing and nowhere does not mean world-absence, but says that innerworldly beings are in themselves so completely without import that, on the ground of this insignificance of the innerworldly, the world in its worldhood alone still obtrudes. The inference is the section's crux, and its logic is § 16's writ large: when every being recedes, what remains is not vacancy but the condition of beings — the world as such, which ordinarily hides behind its contents (§ 16's twelfth unit: world silent so that things may be), forced into salience by their collapse. Anxiety is the phenomenological reduction performed by a mood.

The eleventh unit certifies the finding from everyday speech. What oppresses is not this or that, but also not everything present-at-hand together as a sum — rather the possibility of the ready-to-hand in general, that is, the world itself. When anxiety has subsided, everyday discourse is wont to say: "it was really nothing." This speech in fact hits ontically what it was: everyday discourse aims at attending to and discussing the ready-to-hand, and what anxiety is anxious before is nothing of the innerworldly ready-to-hand. But this nothing-of-the-ready-to-hand, which everyday circumspective discourse alone understands, is no total nothing: the nothing of readiness-to-hand grounds in the most original "something" — the world; and the world belongs ontologically essentially to Dasein's being as being-in-the-world. If, accordingly, the nothing — that is, the world as such — presents itself as anxiety's before-which, this says: that before which anxiety is anxious is being-in-the-world itself. The exegesis of "it was really nothing" is destruction applied to a sigh of relief: the everyday verdict is ontically exact (no thing threatened) and ontologically eloquent despite itself — its "nothing" names the world; the most dismissive sentence in the language testifies to the deepest phenomenon. The chain then closes: world belongs to Dasein's being, so the before-which is being-in-the-world itself — the flight before oneself and the anxiety before the world are one.

The twelfth unit fixes the disclosure's originality: being-anxious discloses, originally and directly, the world as world. It is not that first, by reflection, one abstracts from innerworldly beings and thinks only the world, before which anxiety then arises; rather anxiety, as a mode of disposedness, first discloses the world as world. This does not mean, however, that in anxiety the worldhood of the world is conceived. The guard cuts both ways: against intellectualism (no meditation manufactures the mood — the ontological order runs from anxiety to any thought of world) and against over-claiming (the mood discloses worldhood, it does not conceptualize it — that labor remains philosophy's, per § 29's protocol: the analytic conceptualizes what the mood opens).

The thirteenth unit turns to the about-which and finds individuation. Anxiety is not only anxiety before...; as disposedness it is at the same time anxiety about... That about which anxiety is anxious is not a determinate mode of being and possibility of Dasein — the threat is itself indeterminate and hence cannot penetrate threateningly to this or that factically concrete potentiality-of-being. That about which anxiety is anxious is being-in-the-world itself. In anxiety, the environmentally ready-to-hand — innerworldly beings in general — sinks away; the "world" can offer nothing more, and just as little the co-Dasein of others. Anxiety thus takes from Dasein the possibility of understanding itself, falling, from the "world" and the public interpretedness; it throws Dasein back upon that about which it is anxious — its authentic potentiality-for-being-in-the-world. Anxiety individualizes (vereinzelt) Dasein upon its ownmost being-in-the-world, which, as understanding, projects itself essentially upon possibilities; with the about-which of being-anxious, anxiety thus discloses Dasein as being-possible — as that which it can be solely from itself, as individualized in individuation. The mechanism of individuation is exact, not rhetorical: the public sources of self-understanding (world's offers, others' interpretedness) are cut by the same collapse of significance — nothing left to understand oneself from except one's own naked potentiality; so anxiety strips Dasein to what § 31 said it is, Möglichsein, and returns it to itself as possibility. The § 39 criteria are met in one stroke: simplification (everything inessential fallen away) and totality (world and self disclosed together).

The fourteenth unit names what individuation frees. Anxiety manifests in Dasein the being toward its ownmost potentiality-of-being — that is, being-free for the freedom of choosing and seizing itself. Anxiety brings Dasein before its being-free for... (propensio in...) the authenticity of its being as the possibility it always already is; and this being is at the same time that to which Dasein, as being-in-the-world, is delivered over. The paragraph is the book's doctrine of freedom in three lines: freedom appears as what one is brought before, not what one exercises — being-free for the freedom of self-choice, a possibility always already been and simultaneously a deliverance (überantwortet — § 9's word): thrown freedom. The Augustinian propensio in the parenthesis quietly signs the lineage.

The fifteenth unit closes the circle and coins the scandal-phrase. That about which anxiety is anxious unveils itself as that before which it is anxious: being-in-the-world. This selfsameness of anxiety's before-which and its about-which extends even to being-anxious itself, for this, as disposedness, is a basic mode of being-in-the-world. The existential selfsameness of the disclosing with the disclosed — such that in the disclosed the world is disclosed as world, being-in as individualized, pure, thrown potentiality-of-being — makes clear that with anxiety a distinguished disposedness has become the theme. Anxiety individualizes and so discloses Dasein as "solus ipse"; but this existential "solipsism" so little transposes an isolated subject-thing into the harmless emptiness of a worldless occurring that it brings Dasein precisely, in an extreme sense, before its world as world, and thereby itself before itself as being-in-the-world. The triple identity (before-which = about-which = the anxious being itself, all being-in-the-world) is the formal proof of the mood's distinction: discloser and disclosed coincide — Dasein brought before itself by itself, § 40's opening demand met to the letter. And the scare-quoted solipsism is a preemptive strike at the individualism-reading: the solus ipse of anxiety is maximally worldly — alone before the world, not without it; individuation intensifies being-in-the-world rather than escaping it.

The sixteenth unit calls everyday language as witness once more, and translates. That anxiety as basic disposedness discloses in this way — for that, everyday interpretation and speech are again the most unbiased evidence. Disposedness, it was said, makes manifest "how one is": in anxiety one feels "unheimlich" — uncanny, not-at-home. In this there first comes to expression the peculiar indeterminacy of that alongside which Dasein finds itself in anxiety: the nothing and nowhere. But Unheimlichkeit means at the same time not-being-at-home (Nicht-zuhause-sein). When being-in was first indicated, and distinguished from the categorial "insideness," it was determined as dwelling-alongside, being-familiar-with (§ 12); this character was then made concretely visible through the everyday publicness of das Man, which brings tranquilized self-assurance — the self-evident "being-at-home" — into Dasein's average everydayness (§ 27). Anxiety, by contrast, fetches Dasein back out of its falling absorption in the "world": everyday familiarity collapses in itself. Dasein is individualized, but as being-in-the-world; being-in enters the existential "mode" of the not-at-home (Un-zuhause). Nothing else is meant by talk of "Unheimlichkeit." The etymological cash-out is the section's second summit: the idiom "es ist einem unheimlich" is split into its components — un-heimlich as un-homely — so that the mood's own name says the finding: the dwelling of § 12 (being-in as inhabiting familiarity) can suspend, and anxiety is that suspension; the at-home of everydayness shows itself as a mode, not the ground.

The seventeenth unit identifies, at last, what falling flees. Now it becomes phenomenally visible before what falling, as flight, flees: not before innerworldly beings, but precisely toward them, as the beings alongside which concern, lost in das Man, can dwell in tranquilized familiarity. The falling flight into the at-home of publicness is flight before the not-at-home — before the uncanniness that lies in Dasein as thrown being-in-the-world, delivered over to itself in its being. This uncanniness pursues Dasein constantly and threatens, though inexpressly, its everyday lostness in das Man; the threat can factically go together with complete security and needlessness of everyday concern. Anxiety can arise in the most harmless situations; nor is darkness needed, in which things more commonly become uncanny for one — in the dark there is, in an emphatic way, "nothing" to see, though the world is still, and more obtrusively, "there." The flight's direction is finally corrected: not away from things but into them — publicness as asylum from the uncanny — and § 35's closing chord (the interpretedness hiding the Unheimlichkeit of the floating) is redeemed: das Man is the institutionalized flight from not-being-at-home. The two closing observations are phenomenological gold: anxiety needs no occasion (harmlessness is no protection — the threat is structural, not situational), and the darkness-remark reverses the psychology textbook: the dark is uncanny not because something may be there but because, with nothing to see, the world itself obtrudes.

The eighteenth unit ranks the two modes. If we interpret Dasein's uncanniness existentially-ontologically as the threat that reaches Dasein from itself, this does not assert that in factical anxiety the uncanniness is always already understood in this sense: the everyday way Dasein understands uncanniness is the falling turning-away that "dims down" the not-at-home. But the everydayness of this fleeing shows phenomenally: to the essential constitution of being-in-the-world — which, as existential, is never present-at-hand but always itself in a mode of factical Dasein, that is, in a disposedness — belongs anxiety as basic disposedness. Tranquilized-familiar being-in-the-world is a mode of Dasein's uncanniness, not the reverse: the not-at-home must be conceived existentially-ontologically as the more original phenomenon. This is the section's most radical sentence, and it must be given its full weight: homelessness is the ground, homeyness the derivative mode — the everyday at-home is a covering achievement over an uncanniness that is constitutional. The inversion completes a series (in-itself grounded in world, § 16; presence-at-hand in readiness-to-hand's modification, § 33) and out-bids them all: even familiarity, being-in's very definition at § 12, is now a mode of its opposite. The later Heidegger's meditations on the unhomely (the Ister-lectures' deinon) grow from this root.

The nineteenth unit derives fear, closing the § 30 account: and only because anxiety latently determines being-in-the-world always already, can being-in-the-world, as attending-disposed being alongside the "world," fear. Fear is anxiety fallen upon the "world," inauthentic, and, as such, hidden from itself. The definition is a masterpiece of compression: fear = anxiety in worldly disguise — the indeterminate threat contracted onto an innerworldly stand-in, the mood thereby made manageable (one can flee a thing) and self-concealing (as anxiety). The founding promised at the seventh unit is executed: § 30's rich phenomenon is care's uncanny ground-mood, mundanized.

The twentieth unit takes up the physiological objection. Factically, the mood of uncanniness mostly remains existentielly ununderstood; "authentic" anxiety, given the predominance of falling and publicness, is moreover rare. Often anxiety is "physiologically" conditioned — but this fact is, in its facticity, an ontological problem, not only as to its ontic causation and course: physiological triggering of anxiety is possible only because Dasein, in the ground of its being, is anxious. The reply to naturalism is transcendental in a single line: the body can occasion the mood only in a being whose being admits of it — physiology explains the release, never the possibility; the somatic fact itself testifies to the existential ground. Rarity, meanwhile, is conceded and set aside — with its interpretation deferred one unit.

The twenty-first unit converts rarity into credential. Rarer still than the existentiell fact of authentic anxiety are attempts to interpret the phenomenon in its fundamental existential-ontological constitution and function; the grounds lie partly in the neglect of the existential analytic in general, especially in the misjudgment of the phenomenon of disposedness. But the factual rarity of the anxiety-phenomenon cannot deprive it of its aptness to take over a fundamental methodical function for the existential analytic — on the contrary: the phenomenon's rarity is an index that Dasein, which mostly remains covered up in its authenticity by das Man's public interpretedness, becomes disclosable in this basic disposedness in an original sense. The argument inverts the statistical objection: precisely because publicness suppresses it, anxiety's rareness measures its depth — frequency indexes conformity to the covering, rarity the breach of it; the methodological privilege of the exceptional mood is thereby grounded, not asserted.

The twenty-second unit states the distinction formally — and, in the folded-in note, files the phenomenon's theological dossier. To the essence of every disposedness it belongs to disclose, in each case, full being-in-the-world according to all its constitutive moments (world, being-in, self); but in anxiety lies the possibility of a distinguished disclosing, because anxiety individualizes. This individuation fetches Dasein back from its falling and makes authenticity and inauthenticity manifest to it as possibilities of its being: these basic possibilities of Dasein, which is in each case mine, show themselves in anxiety as in themselves, undisguised by innerworldly beings to which Dasein proximally and mostly clings. The appended note records that it is no accident that the phenomena of anxiety and fear, which remain everywhere undistinguished, came ontically — and, within very narrow limits, ontologically — into the purview of Christian theology, always when the anthropological problem of man's being toward God won priority and phenomena like faith, sin, love, and remorse guided the questioning: Augustine's doctrine of timor castus and servilis, discussed throughout his exegetical writings and letters, and the quaestiones on fear in De diversis quaestionibus; Luther's treatment of the fear-problem in the traditional context of poenitentia and contritio and in his Genesis commentary — there least conceptually, but all the more penetratingly as edification; and furthest of all Kierkegaard, who pressed into the analysis of the anxiety-phenomenon — again in the theological context of a "psychological" exposition of the problem of hereditary sin: The Concept of Anxiety, 1844. Text and note together perform a double acknowledgment. The formal statement completes the § 39 requirements — every mood discloses the whole; anxiety alone discloses it individualized and undisguised, the two basic possibilities (authentic/inauthentic) showing as such. And the note is the section's honest genealogy: the phenomenon's discoverers were theologians — chaste versus servile fear (Augustine's distinction shadowing Angst versus Furcht), Luther's contrition, and above all Kierkegaard's anxiety-book, the section's nearest ancestor — with Heidegger's standing verdict encoded in the qualifiers: ontically penetrating, ontologically narrow; the existential analytic claims to give these discoveries the conceptual ground their theological frame could not.

The closing unit hands the yield to § 41 as a question: to what extent has this existential interpretation of anxiety won a phenomenal soil for answering the guiding question of the being of the totality of Dasein's structural whole? The interrogative form is discipline, not modesty — the mood has been exhibited; whether it carries the structural whole (thrownness, projection, falling in one) is exactly what the care-analysis must now demonstrate.

##### § 41. The Being of Dasein as Care

The opening unit inventories anxiety's yield and poses the unity-question. Intending to grasp the totality of the structural whole ontologically, we must first ask: can the phenomenon of anxiety, and what is disclosed in it, give the whole of Dasein phenomenally in such equiprimordial fashion that the searching view of totality can fulfill itself at this givenness? The total stock of what lies in anxiety can be registered in formal enumeration: being-anxious is, as disposedness, a way of being-in-the-world; the before-which of anxiety is thrown being-in-the-world; the about-which of anxiety is potentiality-for-being-in-the-world. The full phenomenon of anxiety thus shows Dasein as factically existing being-in-the-world; the fundamental ontological characters of this being are existentiality, facticity, and being-fallen. These existential determinations do not belong, as pieces, to a composite from which one could at times be missing: in them weaves an original connection, which constitutes the sought totality of the structural whole. In the unity of these determinations of being, Dasein's being becomes ontologically graspable as such. How is this unity itself to be characterized? The enumeration is the proof § 39 demanded: anxiety's three moments (enactment, before-which, about-which) map exactly onto the three ontological characters (falling-disposedness, facticity, existentiality) — one mood carrying the whole, per the simplification-and-totality criteria — and the anti-composite clause repeats § 39's building-plan ban at the moment of assembly: the weave (webt) precedes the strands.

The second unit derives the first structural moment. Dasein is the being for which, in its being, that being itself is at issue: the "it is at issue" (es geht um...) has clarified itself in the constitution of understanding as self-projecting being toward the ownmost potentiality-of-being. This potentiality is that for the sake of which Dasein in each case is as it is; Dasein has in each case already put itself together (sich zusammengestellt) with a possibility of itself. Being-free for the ownmost potentiality-of-being — and therewith for the possibility of authenticity and inauthenticity — shows itself in original, elemental concretion in anxiety.
