The paragraph is the book's social ethics in four sentences: § 26's positive solicitude (vorspringend-befreiend) finds here its condition — only the self-possessed can free others into their possibilities — and the strongest sentence gives Fürsorge its maximum: to become the conscience of the other, calling him toward his Seinkönnen as one's own conscience called oneself. The closing antithesis (authentic Miteinander from resoluteness, not from the jealous pacts and voluble brotherhoods of das Man) is aimed at every collectivism of the day, left and right: community founded on owned selves, or counterfeit.

The tenth unit refuses the ethics of prescription. Resoluteness is, by its ontological essence, in each case that of a respective factical Dasein; the essence of this being is its existence. Resoluteness "exists" only as understanding-self-projecting resolution (Entschluß). But upon what does Dasein disclose itself in resoluteness — to what is it to resolve? The answer only the resolution itself can give. It would be a complete misunderstanding of the phenomenon to suppose it a mere receptive seizing of presented and recommended possibilities: the resolution is precisely first the disclosive projecting and determining of the current factical possibility. To resoluteness necessarily belongs the indeterminacy that characterizes every factically thrown potentiality-of-being of Dasein; resoluteness is certain of itself only as resolution. But the existentiell indeterminacy of resoluteness — determining itself in each case only in the resolution — has nevertheless its existential determinateness. The paragraph is § 59's sixteenth unit converted to positive doctrine: no catalogue of resolvable contents exists — the answer belongs to the resolution alone, because resolving is the disclosing of the possibility, not its selection from a menu; hence the structural indeterminacy (no ontology can say what to do) paired with existential determinateness (ontology can say the structure of the doing) — the pair the next units unfold as the situation.

The eleventh unit gives the whither its structure and appropriates untruth. The whereto of resoluteness is ontologically predelineated in the existentiality of Dasein in general, as potentiality-of-being in the manner of concernful solicitude. As care, however, Dasein is determined by facticity and falling: disclosed in its "Da," it holds itself equiprimordially in truth and untruth. This holds "authentically" precisely of resoluteness as authentic truth: resoluteness appropriates untruth authentically. Dasein is in each case already, and perhaps soon again, in irresoluteness (Unentschlossenheit). This title expresses only the phenomenon interpreted as being-delivered-over to the dominant interpretedness of das Man: Dasein, as they-self, is "lived" by the common-sense ambiguity of publicness, in which nobody resolves and which yet has always already decided. Resoluteness means letting-oneself-be-summoned out of the lostness in das Man. The irresoluteness of das Man remains nevertheless in dominion — only it cannot assail resolute existence. Irresoluteness, as counter-concept to existentially understood resoluteness, does not mean an ontic-psychic constitution in the sense of being burdened with inhibitions. Even the resolution remains dependent upon das Man and its world; understanding this belongs to what it discloses, insofar as resoluteness first gives Dasein its authentic transparency. In resoluteness Dasein is concerned with its ownmost potentiality-of-being, which, as thrown, can project itself only upon determinate factical possibilities. Resolution does not withdraw from "actuality," but first discovers the factically possible — seizing it in the way in which it, as ownmost potentiality, is possible in das Man. The paragraph is the chapter's most sober, and its clauses guard against every heroic misreading in turn. Resoluteness appropriates untruth (§ 44(b)'s equiprimordiality holding at the summit: the resolute one is not delivered from concealment but owns it); irresoluteness is not weakness of will (the psychological reading barred — it names delivery to the public interpretedness, where nobody resolves and everything is decided); the resolute one may fall back (the "perhaps soon again" — resoluteness no permanent estate); das Man's dominion continues, merely unable to assail; and the resolution stays dependent on das Man and its world — no exit, only owned inhabitation: the possible seized as it is possible in das Man. The epigram at the center — nobody resolves, yet it has always already decided — is § 27's whole analysis in nine words.

The twelfth unit coins the situation. The existential determinateness of the in-each-case possible resolute Dasein embraces the constitutive moments of the existential phenomenon, hitherto passed over, that we call the situation. In the term situation (Lage — "being in a position") a spatial signification resonates; we shall not attempt to expunge it from the existential concept, for it lies also in the "Da" of Dasein. To being-in-the-world belongs an own spatiality, characterized by the phenomena of de-severance and directionality; Dasein "makes room" insofar as it factically exists. But Dasein-like spatiality — on whose ground existence in each case determines its "place" — grounds in the constitution of being-in-the-world, whose primary constitutive is disclosedness: as the spatiality of the Da grounds in disclosedness, so the situation has its foundations in resoluteness. The situation is the Da, in each case disclosed in resoluteness, as which the existing being is there. The situation is not a present-at-hand frame in which Dasein occurs, or into which it might even only bring itself: far removed from a present-at-hand mixture of encountering circumstances and accidents, the situation is only through and in resoluteness. Resolved for the Da, as which the self existing has to be, the current factical involvement-character of the circumstances first discloses itself to it. Only to resoluteness can that be-fall (zu-fallen) from the with-world and environing-world which we call accidents (Zufälle). The coinage completes the chapter's yield: the situation as resoluteness's correlate — not the objective circumstances (that is the frame-picture, refused) but the Da as disclosed in the resolution; circumstance becomes situation only for the resolved. The etymological close is the finest stroke: Zufall read as Zu-fall — the accident as what falls to one — so that even chance is indexed to resoluteness: only a disclosed Da has luck; das Man, the next unit says, has only occurrences it miscounts as deeds.

The thirteenth unit gives das Man its counter-concept: to das Man, by contrast, the situation is essentially closed. It knows only the "general position" (allgemeine Lage), loses itself to the nearest "opportunities," and defrays its Dasein from the reckoning-up of "accidents" which it — misrecognizing them — takes and passes off as its own achievement. The three-term portrait (the general position, the opportunities, the accidents booked as merit) is das Man's practical life complete: where the resolute has a situation, the irresolute has a market — and the last clause adds the vanity: chance re-audited as accomplishment.

The fourteenth unit closes the argument of the chapter: resoluteness brings the being of the Da into the existence of its situation. Resoluteness delimits the existential structure of the authentic potentiality-of-being attested in conscience — wanting-to-have-a-conscience. In it we recognized the appropriate understanding of the appeal. From this it becomes fully clear that the call of conscience, when it summons to the potentiality-of-being, holds up no empty ideal of existence, but calls forth into the situation. This existential positivity of the rightly understood call makes intelligible at the same time how far the restriction of the call-tendency to occurred and intended indebtednesses misrecognizes the disclosure-character of conscience and only apparently conveys the concrete understanding of its voice. The existential interpretation of understanding the appeal as resoluteness unveils conscience as the mode of being, enclosed in the ground of Dasein, in which it — attesting its ownmost potentiality-of-being — makes its factical existence possible for itself. The unit discharges § 59's remaining debt with the situation-concept in hand: the call is concrete after all — more concrete than the deed-ledger, for it calls into the situation, the maximally determinate; the vulgar reproach of emptiness inverted one last time. And the closing formula seals the attestation: conscience as Dasein's self-enabling — the being that, calling itself, makes its own factical existence possible.

The fifteenth unit refuses two last confusions. The phenomenon set forth under the title resoluteness can hardly be conflated with an empty "habitus" or an indeterminate "velleity." Resoluteness does not first represent a situation to itself, taking cognizance; it has already placed itself into it: resolved, Dasein already acts. We avoid the term "action" (Handeln) deliberately: for one thing, it would have to be taken so broadly that activity also embraces the passivity of resistance; for another, it suggests the Dasein-ontological misunderstanding that resoluteness is a special comportment of the practical faculty over against a theoretical. Care, however, as concernful solicitude, embraces Dasein's being so originally and wholly that it must in each case already be presupposed, as a whole, in the division of theoretical and practical comportment, and cannot first be built together from these faculties by means of a dialectic necessarily groundless because existentially ungrounded. The double refusal completes the concept's fencing: against the virtue-reading (no habitus, no velleity — resoluteness is enacted or nothing: schon handelt) and, subtly, against the praxis-reading its own vocabulary invites — "action" avoided because it would re-import the theory/practice split that § 41 dissolved, and because resistance's passivity belongs to resolve as much as deed: the resolute endurance no less than the resolute act. Hegel's mediation of the faculties dismissed in a subordinate clause as groundless dialectic.

The sixteenth unit draws the disciplinary boundary: to present the factical existentiell possibilities in their chief traits and connections, and to interpret them according to their existential structure, falls within the task-circle of thematic existential anthropology; for the fundamental-ontological intent of the present investigation, the existential delimitation of the authentic potentiality-of-being attested in conscience, from Dasein itself for it itself, suffices. The § 10 boundary re-drawn at the harvest: the content of resolute lives — the typology of vocations and commitments — belongs to an anthropology this book does not write; ontology stops at the structure, deliberately.

The closing unit hands Chapter Three its problem. With the working-out of resoluteness as the reticent, anxiety-ready self-projection upon the ownmost being-guilty, the investigation is enabled to delimit the ontological sense of the sought authentic potentiality-of-being-whole of Dasein. Authenticity of Dasein is now neither an empty title nor an invented idea. But even so, the existentially deduced authentic being toward death, as authentic potentiality-of-being-whole, remains a purely existential projection lacking the Dasein-like attestation; only when this is found does the investigation satisfy the required exhibition of an existentially confirmed and clarified authentic potentiality-of-being-whole. For only when this being has become phenomenally accessible in its authenticity and wholeness does the question of the meaning of the being of this being — to whose existence understanding of being belongs — come onto tenable soil. The chapter closes with its books balanced and one entry open: authenticity attested (resoluteness — no longer empty or invented), wholeness projected (anticipation — still unattested), and the two not yet shown to be one. Chapter One gave the whole without the witness; Chapter Two the witness without the whole; § 62's task is written by the remainder: whether resoluteness, thought to its own end, is anticipation.

#### Chapter Three: Dasein's Authentic Potentiality-of-Being-Whole, and Temporality as the Ontological Sense of Care

##### § 61. Predelineation of the Methodical Step from the Delimitation of Authentic Dasein-like Being-Whole to the Phenomenal Laying-Free of Temporality

The opening unit states the standoff — and the note salutes Jaspers. Existentially projected was an authentic potentiality-of-being-whole of Dasein: the laying-apart of the phenomenon unveiled authentic being toward death as anticipation. In its existentiell attestation, Dasein's authentic potentiality-of-being was exhibited as resoluteness, and at the same time interpreted existentially. The folded-in note records that in the direction of this problematic Karl Jaspers first expressly grasped and carried through the task of a doctrine of worldviews: his Psychology of Worldviews asks after and determines "what man is" from what he essentially can be — whence the fundamental existential-ontological significance of the "limit-situations" becomes clear; the philosophical tendency of the work is wholly misjudged if one merely "uses" it as a reference-work for "types of worldview." The two results are laid side by side with their provenance marked: anticipation from projection (Chapter One), resoluteness from attestation (Chapter Two) — the division's two halves facing each other; and the Jaspers-note, placed at this hinge, is the book's fullest bow to a contemporary: the man-from-his-possibility approach and the Grenzsituationen credited as genuinely existential-ontological in significance, with the defense against the typology-readers repeating § 49's compliment — fundamentality above classification.

The second unit lets the incompatibility speak: how are the two phenomena to be brought together? Did the ontological projection of the authentic potentiality-of-being-whole not lead into a dimension of Dasein lying far from the phenomenon of resoluteness? What is death supposed to have in common with the "concrete situation" of acting? Does the attempt to force resoluteness and anticipation together not seduce into an intolerable, wholly unphenomenological construction — one that may no longer even claim the character of a phenomenally grounded ontological projection? The objection is given its sharpest form — death and the situation, the uttermost and the concrete, mortality and action — and the stakes named: a forced synthesis would forfeit phenomenology itself.

The third unit finds the only path. An external binding-together of the two phenomena forbids itself of itself. There remains, as the methodically sole possible way: to depart from the phenomenon of resoluteness, attested in its existentiell possibility, and to ask — does resoluteness, in its ownmost existentiell tendency-of-being, itself point forward to anticipatory resoluteness (vorlaufende Entschlossenheit) as its ownmost authentic possibility? What if resoluteness, by its own sense, had brought itself into its authenticity only when it projects itself not upon arbitrary and merely nearest possibilities, but upon the uttermost one — the possibility lying before all factical potentiality-of-being of Dasein and, as such, standing more or less undisguised into every factically seized potentiality? What if resoluteness, as Dasein's authentic truth, reached only in anticipation toward death the authentic certainty belonging to it? What if in anticipation toward death all factical "provisionality" of resolving were first authentically understood — that is, existentielly overtaken? The paragraph fixes the method that saves the chapter from construction: no welding — instead, let resoluteness itself testify; the three "what if" clauses sketch the demonstration § 62 will execute (the uttermost possibility as what stands into every resolution; certainty completed only anticipatorily; the resolve's provisionality caught up only in the running-ahead), each conditional a promissory note drawn on the phenomenon's own tendency. The term of the entire division — vorlaufende Entschlossenheit — is minted here, as a question.

The fourth unit generalizes the rule: so long as the existential interpretation does not forget that its pregiven thematic being has Dasein's mode of being and cannot be pieced together, from present-at-hand pieces, into something present-at-hand, all its steps must let themselves be guided by the idea of existence. For the question of the possible connection between anticipation and resoluteness, this means nothing less than the demand to project these existential phenomena upon the existentiell possibilities predelineated in them, and to "think these through to the end" existentially. Thereby the working-out of anticipatory resoluteness, as an existentielly possible authentic potentiality-of-being-whole, loses the character of an arbitrary construction: it becomes the interpretive liberation of Dasein for its uttermost possibility of existence. The methodological coinage — existential Zu-Ende-denken, thinking a phenomenon through to the end of its own tendency — names the procedure that distinguishes projection from construction; and the closing re-description is the division's self-understanding at its noblest: the analysis as befreiende Interpretation — interpretation that frees Dasein for its uttermost possibility, hermeneutics as liberation.

The fifth unit pauses for method, on principle: with this step the existential interpretation makes known at once its ownmost methodical character. Hitherto, express methodical discussions were deferred (occasional necessary remarks apart); it was necessary first to "advance" toward the phenomena. But before laying free the sense of the being of the being unveiled in its phenomenal basic stock, the course of the investigation needs a halt — not for the purposes of "rest," but to give the investigation its sharpened impetus. The pause is itself methodical doctrine: phenomena first, methodology after — reflection earns its place only on won ground (§ 7's order kept); and the halt announced is § 63, the division's great methodological reckoning.

The sixth unit states the principle of genuine method: genuine method grounds in the appropriate fore-view of the basic constitution of the "object" to be disclosed, or of the object-region. Genuine methodical reflection — to be well distinguished from empty discussions of technique — therefore gives at the same time information about the mode of being of the thematic being. The clarification of the methodical possibilities, requirements, and limits of the existential analytic in general first secures the necessary transparency for its ground-laying step: the unveiling of the sense of the being of care. But the interpretation of the ontological sense of care must accomplish itself on the ground of the full and constant phenomenological presentification of Dasein's existential constitution as set forth hitherto. The principle inverts methodologism: method is answerable to the matter (fore-view of the constitution, not a toolkit) — so methodological reflection is itself ontology, disclosing the theme's mode of being; technique-talk dismissed as empty in a parenthesis. § 32's fore-structure doctrine, applied to the book's own next step.

The seventh unit re-fixes the theme against substance: Dasein is ontologically in principle different from everything present-at-hand and real; its "subsistence" grounds not in the substantiality of a substance but in the "self-standingness" (Selbständigkeit) of the existing self, whose being was conceived as care. The phenomenon of the self, co-enclosed in care, needs an original and authentic existential delimitation over against the preparatory exhibition of the inauthentic they-self; therewith goes a fixing of the possible ontological questions to be directed at the "self" at all, if it is neither substance nor subject. The unit assigns § 64 its office and coins its key: Selbständigkeit heard literally — self-standing-ness, the constancy of the self re-thought from existence rather than from substrate — the Kant-confrontation (the paralogisms) already implicit in "neither substance nor subject."

The eighth unit names the destination and its law. The phenomenon of care, thus first sufficiently clarified, we then interrogate as to its ontological sense; the determination of this sense becomes the laying-free of temporality (Zeitlichkeit). This exhibition leads not into remote, separated districts of Dasein, but only conceives the whole phenomenal stock of Dasein's existential basic constitution in the ultimate foundations of its own ontological intelligibility. Temporality is experienced phenomenally originally at Dasein's authentic being-whole — at the phenomenon of anticipatory resoluteness; if temporality makes itself known originally therein, then presumably the temporality of anticipatory resoluteness is a distinguished mode of temporality itself. Temporality can temporalize itself (sich zeitigen) in various possibilities and in various ways: the basic possibilities of existence, authenticity and inauthenticity of Dasein, ground ontologically in possible temporalizations of temporality. The paragraph is the division's second half in outline, and two decisions carry it. The site of the phenomenon: temporality is to be read off anticipatory resoluteness — the authentic whole as temporality's original showing (whence § 65's derivation) — with the immediate corollary that this showing is one distinguished mode among possible ones. And the verb: sich zeitigen — temporality temporalizes itself, ripens, brings itself forth (the word carrying § 48's fruit within it) — modality returned to time itself: authenticity and inauthenticity re-grounded, in advance, as ways time times.

The closing unit posts the warning and gives the map. If the ontological character of its own being already lies far from Dasein under the predominance of the falling understanding of being (being as presence-at-hand), then still more the original foundations of this being. Hence it must not astonish if, at first glance, temporality does not correspond to what is accessible to the vulgar understanding as "time." The time-concept of vulgar time-experience, and the problematic growing from it, cannot therefore function unexamined as criteria of the appropriateness of an interpretation of time: the investigation must beforehand make itself familiar with the original phenomenon of temporality, in order from it first to illuminate the necessity and the manner of the origin of the vulgar understanding of time, and equally the ground of its dominion. The securing of the original phenomenon accomplishes itself through the demonstration that all the fundamental structures of Dasein set forth hitherto are, with regard to their possible wholeness, unity, and unfolding, at bottom "temporal," and to be conceived as modes of the temporalizing of temporality. Thus there grows for the existential analytic, from the laying-free of temporality, the task of repeating the accomplished analysis of Dasein in the sense of an interpretation of the essential structures upon their temporality; the basic directions of the analyses thereby demanded are predelineated by temporality itself. The chapter accordingly receives the following division: Dasein's existentielly authentic potentiality-of-being-whole as anticipatory resoluteness (§ 62); the hermeneutical situation won for an interpretation of the sense of the being of care, and the methodical character of the existential analytic in general (§ 63); care and selfhood (§ 64); temporality as the ontological sense of care (§ 65); Dasein's temporality and the tasks, springing from it, of an original repetition of the existential analysis (§ 66). The warning repeats the book's constant clause at its highest stake: vulgar time — the clock's and the tradition's — is disqualified in advance as criterion, its own origin and dominion to be derived instead (Chapter Six's office); and the verification-principle is stated as the second half's law: temporality proves itself by re-generating every structure won so far as one of its modes — the Wiederholung (§ 45's announced repetition) now scheduled, with § 62 as the gate.

##### § 62. Dasein's Existentielly Authentic Potentiality-of-Being-Whole as Anticipatory Resoluteness

The opening unit poses the section's question in its exact form: how far does resoluteness, "thought through to the end" in accordance with its ownmost tendency-of-being, lead to authentic being toward death? How is the connection between wanting-to-have-a-conscience and the existentially projected authentic potentiality-of-being-whole to be conceived? Does the welding-together of the two yield a new phenomenon — or does it remain with resoluteness, attested in its existentiell possibility, in such a way that it can undergo, through being toward death, an existentiell modalization? And what does it mean to "think the phenomenon of resoluteness existentially to its end"? The alternatives are posed with care: no new phenomenon is to be manufactured — the question is whether resoluteness modalizes itself toward anticipation; § 61's method (Zu-Ende-denken) is itself put in question at the threshold of its use.

The second unit runs the first argument: from constancy. Resoluteness was characterized as the reticent self-projection, exacting anxiety of itself, upon the ownmost being-guilty. This belongs to Dasein's being and means: being the null ground of a nullity. The "guilty" belonging to Dasein's being admits of neither increase nor diminution — it lies before every quantification, if such has any sense at all; nor is Dasein essentially guilty at times and then again not guilty. Wanting-to-have-a-conscience resolves itself for this being-guilty; in resoluteness's own sense lies the projecting of itself upon this being-guilty as which Dasein is, as long as it is. The existentiell taking-over of this "guilt" in resoluteness is therefore authentically accomplished only when resoluteness has become so transparent to itself in its disclosing of Dasein that it understands the being-guilty as constant. But this understanding makes itself possible only in such a way that Dasein discloses to itself its potentiality-of-being "unto its end." Dasein's being-at-an-end, however, means existentially: being toward the end. Resoluteness authentically becomes what it can be as understanding being toward the end — that is, as anticipation into death. Resoluteness does not merely "have" a connection with anticipation as something other than itself: it harbors authentic being toward death in itself, as the possible existentiell modality of its own authenticity. The argument is a jewel of internal derivation: guilt is constant (before quantification — § 58's yield), so its authentic taking-over must understand it as constant; constancy is understood only when the Seinkönnen is disclosed to its end; being-at-the-end is being-toward-the-end (§ 48); therefore resoluteness completes itself as Vorlaufen. No welding — the connection is discovered inside resoluteness as its own demand: anticipation as resoluteness's harbored modality.

The third unit runs the second argument: from possibility. Resoluteness means: letting oneself be called forth to the ownmost being-guilty. Being-guilty belongs to Dasein's being itself, which we determined primarily as potentiality-of-being. That Dasein "is" constantly guilty can only mean that it holds itself in this being, in each case, as authentic or inauthentic existing: being-guilty is not a merely persisting property of a constantly present-at-hand thing, but the existentiell possibility of being guilty authentically or inauthentically; the "guilty" is in each case only in the current factical potentiality-of-being. Being-guilty must therefore, as belonging to Dasein's being, be conceived as ability-to-be-guilty (Schuldigseinkönnen). Resoluteness projects itself upon this potentiality — understands itself in it. This understanding holds itself accordingly in an original possibility of Dasein; it holds itself in it authentically when resoluteness is originally what it tends to be. But Dasein's original being toward its potentiality-of-being we unveiled as being toward death — toward the characterized distinguished possibility; anticipation discloses this possibility as possibility. Resoluteness therefore becomes, only as anticipatory, an original being toward Dasein's ownmost potentiality-of-being: the "can" of the ability-to-be-guilty resoluteness understands only when it "qualifies" itself as being toward death. The second derivation runs through modality itself: guilt, being of Dasein, is a Können — and the being that discloses possibility as possibility is anticipation (§ 53's making-possible); so the resolve that would understand its own "can" originally must anticipate. The two arguments interlock: constancy demands the end; possibility demands the running-ahead that frees the possible.

The fourth unit runs the third argument: from nullity — and the note draws the theological boundary. Resolved, Dasein authentically takes over, in its existence, that it is the null ground of its nullity. Death we conceived existentially as the characterized possibility of the impossibility of existence — as the absolute nullity of Dasein. Death is not pieced onto Dasein at its "end"; rather, as care, Dasein is the thrown (that is, null) ground of its death. The nullity originally ruling through Dasein's being unveils itself to it in authentic being toward death: anticipation first makes being-guilty manifest from the ground of the whole being of Dasein. Care harbors death and guilt equiprimordially in itself; anticipatory resoluteness first understands the ability-to-be-guilty authentically and wholly — that is, originally. The folded-in note distinguishes: the being-guilty originally belonging to Dasein's constitution is well to be distinguished from the theologically understood status corruptionis; theology can find in the existentially determined being-guilty an ontological condition of its factical possibility. The guilt enclosed in the idea of that status is a factical indebtedness of a wholly own kind, with its own attestation, which remains in principle closed to every philosophical experience. The existential analysis of being-guilty proves nothing for or against the possibility of sin; strictly taken, one cannot even say that the ontology of Dasein of itself leaves this possibility open, since, as philosophical questioning, it fundamentally "knows" nothing of sin. The third argument is the deepest: the two nullities meet at the ground — death as the absolute nullity, Dasein as thrown null ground of its death — so care holds Tod und Schuld gleichursprünglich, and only their joint disclosure (anticipatory resoluteness) reads either originally. The note is the § 38/§ 49 theology-settlement at its most scrupulous: sin's guilt has its own attestation (faith's, closed to philosophy in principle); the analysis proves nothing either way — and the final refinement out-Kants Kant: philosophy cannot even certify the possibility as open, for it knows nothing of sin at all; neutrality radicalized into ignorance de jure.

The fifth unit is the compact eigenste-clause: understanding the call of conscience unveils the lostness in das Man; resoluteness fetches Dasein back to its ownmost potentiality-of-being-a-self. One's own potentiality becomes authentic and wholly transparent in understanding being toward death as the ownmost possibility. The predicate-run of § 53 now replays with conscience supplying the entry: ownness recovered by the call, completed by the running-ahead.

The sixth unit runs the non-relational: the call of conscience passes over, in its appeal, all "worldly" prestige and ability of Dasein; unrelentingly it individualizes Dasein upon its ability-to-be-guilty, which it exacts of it to be authentically. The unbroken sharpness of the essential individualization upon the ownmost potentiality-of-being discloses anticipation into death as the non-relational possibility: anticipatory resoluteness lets the ability-to-be-guilty, as ownmost and non-relational, strike wholly into the conscience (ganz ins Gewissen schlagen). The convergence is structural: § 56's Übergehen (the call's disregard of worldly standing) and § 53's individualization are one movement seen from two sides — and the idiom at the close (etwas schlägt einem ins Gewissen) is re-literalized: the guilt strikes home entire only anticipatorily.

The seventh unit runs the unoutstrippable: wanting-to-have-a-conscience means readiness for the appeal to the ownmost being-guilty, which has in each case already determined factical Dasein before every factical indebtedness and after its discharge. This prior and constant being-guilty shows itself undisguised in its priority only when this priority is placed into the possibility that is for Dasein absolutely not to be outstripped. When resoluteness, anticipating, has caught up (eingeholt) the possibility of death into its potentiality-of-being, Dasein's authentic existence can no longer be outstripped by anything. The argument turns on the two priorities matching: guilt's beforeness (prior to every deed) shows as such only against death's finality (beyond every possibility) — the a priori of guilt legible only in the light of the ultimum; and the closing sentence banks the chapter's prize: the anticipatorily resolved existence is unüberholbar — nothing can overtake it, because it has itself overtaken its end.

The eighth unit runs the certain — and derives the retraction-clause. With the phenomenon of resoluteness we were led before the original truth of existence: resolved, Dasein is unveiled to itself in its current factical potentiality-of-being, and in such a way that it itself is this unveiling and being-unveiled. To truth belongs a corresponding holding-for-true; the express appropriation of the disclosed is being-certain. The original truth of existence demands an equiprimordial being-certain as holding-oneself in what resoluteness discloses. Resoluteness gives itself the current factical situation and brings itself into it; the situation cannot be pre-calculated and pre-given like something present-at-hand awaiting apprehension — it is disclosed only in a free resolving, beforehand undetermined but open to determinability. What, then, does the certainty belonging to such resoluteness mean? It is to hold itself in what the resolution discloses. But this means: it precisely cannot rigidify upon the situation, but must understand that the resolution, by its own disclosure-sense, must be held free and open for the current factical possibility. The certainty of the resolution means: keeping oneself free for its possible and in each case factically necessary retraction (Zurücknahme). Such holding-for-true of resoluteness (as truth of existence) by no means lets one fall back into irresoluteness: on the contrary, this holding-for-true, as resolute keeping-oneself-free for retraction, is the authentic resoluteness toward the repetition of itself (zur Wiederholung ihrer selbst). Therewith the lostness in irresoluteness is precisely existentielly undermined. The holding-for-true belonging to resoluteness tends, by its sense, to keep itself constantly free — that is, for the whole potentiality-of-being of Dasein. This constant certainty is guaranteed to resoluteness only in such a way that it comports itself toward the possibility of which it can be absolutely certain: in its death, Dasein must absolutely "take itself back." Constantly certain of this — that is, anticipating — resoluteness gains its authentic and whole certainty. This paragraph is the section's profoundest, and its logic must be walked slowly. Existential certainty cannot be rigidity (the situation is not a fact to grip but a disclosure to inhabit), so certainty = freedom-for-retraction — the resolve held revisable by its own truth-character; yet revisability is not relapse: keeping-free-for-retraction is resoluteness's self-repetition (Wiederholung entering the book here in its existentiell sense: the resolve renewed, not merely retained). And the totalization: constancy of this freedom across the whole Seinkönnen is available only from the one absolutely certain possibility — death, the retraction absolute, in which Dasein must take itself back entirely. Anticipation is thus certainty's own completion: the resolve certain of its revisability because certain of the final revocation. The structure of every authentic commitment — held fast and held open at once — is here given its ontological deduction.

The ninth unit runs the indeterminate — and appropriates untruth once more. Dasein, however, is equiprimordially in untruth: anticipatory resoluteness gives it at the same time the original certainty of its closedness. Anticipatorily resolved, Dasein holds itself open for the constant lostness — possible from the ground of its own being — into the irresoluteness of das Man: irresoluteness, as constant possibility of Dasein, is co-certain. Resoluteness transparent to itself understands that the indeterminacy of the potentiality-of-being determines itself in each case only in the resolution upon the current situation; it knows about the indeterminacy that rules through a being that exists. But this knowing must, if it is to correspond to authentic resoluteness, itself spring from an authentic disclosing. The indeterminacy of one's own potentiality — though become certain in each resolution — manifests itself wholly, however, only in being toward death. Anticipation brings Dasein before a possibility constantly certain and yet every moment indeterminate as to when the possibility becomes impossibility: it makes manifest that this being is thrown into the indeterminacy of its "limit-situation," resolved toward which Dasein gains its authentic potentiality-of-being-whole. The indeterminacy of death discloses itself originally in anxiety; this original anxiety resoluteness seeks to exact of itself (sich zuzumuten). It clears away every covering of Dasein's abandonment to itself. The nothing before which anxiety brings unveils the nullity that determines Dasein in its ground — which ground itself is as thrownness into death. The fifth predicate completes the run with its two yields: certainty of one's own possible relapse (the resolute one certain, too, of the irresoluteness that stalks him — sobriety built into the structure) and the indeterminacy of the when, whole only anticipatorily, endured only in the anxiety resoluteness demands of itself. Jaspers' word — Grenzsituation — is set in quotation marks into the argument at its exact fit, § 61's note redeemed; and the closing chain (nothing, nullity, ground as thrownness-into-death) knots §§ 40, 58, and 50 into one clause.

The tenth unit declares the first direction proven: the analysis unveiled, in sequence, the moments of modalization growing from authentic being toward death as the ownmost, non-relational, not-to-be-outstripped, certain and yet indeterminate possibility — moments toward which resoluteness tends from itself. Resoluteness is authentically and wholly what it can be only as anticipatory resoluteness. The verdict banks the five-predicate run: each mark of death was found demanded by resoluteness's own tendency — the modalization internal, the welding-charge dead.

The eleventh unit reverses the direction: conversely, only the interpretation of the "connection" between resoluteness and anticipation reached the full existential understanding of anticipation itself. Hitherto it could count only as ontological projection; now it has shown itself: anticipation is no fictioned possibility forced upon Dasein, but the mode of an existentiell potentiality-of-being attested in Dasein — one Dasein exacts of itself, if indeed it understands itself authentically as resolved. Anticipation "is" not as a free-floating comportment, but must be conceived as the possibility — hidden in the existentielly attested resoluteness, and therewith co-attested — of its authenticity. The authentic "thinking of death" is the wanting-to-have-a-conscience that has become existentielly transparent to itself. The reversal pays Chapter One's outstanding debt (§ 53's "fantastic exaction"): anticipation, unattestable directly, is co-attested — hidden in resoluteness as its own authenticity, so conscience's testimony covers it; and the closing sentence quietly rehabilitates the phrase § 53 refused: the authentic Denken an den Tod is not brooding but transparent conscience — the memento mori re-founded.

The twelfth unit converts the question's genre: if resoluteness, as authentic, tends toward the mode delimited by anticipation, while anticipation constitutes Dasein's authentic potentiality-of-being-whole, then in the existentielly attested resoluteness an authentic potentiality-of-being-whole of Dasein is co-attested. The question of the potentiality-of-being-whole is a factical-existentiell one; Dasein answers it as resolved. The question has now wholly stripped off the character it showed at the beginning — as if it were merely a theoretical, methodical question of the analytic, sprung from the effort for a complete "givenness" of the whole Dasein; the initially only ontologically-methodically discussed question of Dasein's wholeness had its right, but only because its ground goes back to an ontic possibility of Dasein. The paragraph is the division's self-transformation made explicit: § 45's methodological demand (the whole in the fore-having) unmasks itself as grounded in an existentiell possibility — the wholeness-question answered not by the analyst but by the resolute existence; theory's right derived from life's possibility, § 63's whole problematic seeded.

The thirteenth unit fixes the status and posts the guard: the illumination of the "connection" between anticipation and resoluteness, in the sense of the possible modalization of the latter by the former, became the phenomenal exhibition of an authentic potentiality-of-being-whole of Dasein. If with this phenomenon a mode of being of Dasein is reached in which it brings itself to and before itself, then it must remain, ontically and ontologically, unintelligible to the everyday common-sense interpretation of das Man. It would be misunderstanding to shove this existentiell possibility aside as "unproven," or to want to "prove" it theoretically; nevertheless the phenomenon needs protection against the crudest perversions. The status-clause repeats § 54's factuality-doctrine at the summit (neither provable nor refutable — the vorhanden-tribunal has no jurisdiction), and predicts its own reception: unintelligibility to das Man is entailed, not regretted.

The fourteenth unit provides the protection — and lets joy be named. Anticipatory resoluteness is no way out, invented to "overcome" death; it is the understanding, following the call of conscience, that frees for death the possibility of becoming powerful over Dasein's existence (der Existenz mächtig zu werden) and of dispersing at the ground every fugitive self-covering. Wanting-to-have-a-conscience, determined as being toward death, means no world-fleeing seclusion either: it brings, without illusion, into the resoluteness of "acting." Nor does anticipatory resoluteness spring from an "idealistic" exaction soaring above existence and its possibilities: it springs from the sober understanding of factical basic possibilities of Dasein. With the sober anxiety that brings before the individualized potentiality-of-being goes the armored joy (die gerüstete Freude) in this possibility. In it Dasein becomes free from the "contingencies" of being-entertained that busy curiosity procures for itself primarily from world-events. The analysis of these basic moods, however, exceeds the limits drawn for the present interpretation by its fundamental-ontological aim. The three perversions are barred by name: no conquest of death (the inverse — death empowered over existence, every fugitive covering dispersed: anticipation as surrender of the last illusion, not victory over the end); no monkish flight (illusionless into action — § 60's situation kept); no idealist exaction (sober, factical). And then the section's one unguarded moment: nüchterne Angst paired with gerüstete Freude — sober anxiety and armored joy together — the sole mention of joy in the book's account of authenticity, freeing from curiosity's entertainment-contingencies; and at once the door is closed: the analysis of these basic moods exceeds the book's limits — three words of eudaimonia, then discipline.

The closing unit makes the confession that founds § 63: but does not a determinate ontic conception of authentic existence — a factical ideal of Dasein — underlie the accomplished ontological interpretation of Dasein's existence? That is indeed so. This factum must not only not be denied or conceded under compulsion; it must be conceived in its positive necessity, from the thematic object of the investigation. Philosophy will never want to deny its "presuppositions," but neither may it merely admit them: it conceives the presuppositions and brings them, together with that for which they are presuppositions, to more penetrating unfolding. This function the now-required methodical reflection has. The admission is the book's most famous methodological candor: a factical ideal underlies the analysis — yes (das ist in der Tat so) — and the response is neither denial nor shrug but the third way: presuppositions conceived, not confessed; the fore-structure owned and worked (§ 32's imperative applied to the book itself). § 63 is thereby commissioned as the audit of the author's own hermeneutical situation.

##### § 63. The Hermeneutical Situation Won for an Interpretation of the Sense of the Being of Care, and the Methodical Character of the Existential Analytic in General

The opening unit certifies the situation. With anticipatory resoluteness, Dasein has been made phenomenally visible with regard to its possible authenticity and wholeness. The hermeneutical situation, previously insufficient for the exegesis of the sense of the being of care, has received the demanded originality: Dasein is placed into the fore-having originally — with regard to its authentic potentiality-of-being-whole; the guiding fore-sight, the idea of existence, has gained its determinateness through the clarification of the ownmost potentiality-of-being; and with the concretely worked-out structure of Dasein's being, its ontological peculiarity over against everything present-at-hand has become so distinct that the fore-grasp upon Dasein's existentiality possesses sufficient articulation to guide securely the conceptual elaboration of the existentials. The certification runs the § 45 audit in reverse: fore-having (now the whole, via anticipation), fore-sight (existence now including authenticity, via resoluteness), fore-grasp (the conceptuality now articulate) — the triple deficit of § 45 discharged item by item; the interpretation of care's sense may proceed.

The second unit demonstrates the opening thesis of the book. The way of the analytic traversed so far became the concrete demonstration of the thesis merely thrown out at the start: the being that we in each case ourselves are is ontologically the farthest. The ground for this lies in care itself: the falling being alongside the nearest-attended of the "world" guides the everyday interpretation of Dasein and covers over, ontically, its authentic being — denying to the ontology directed at this being the appropriate basis. Hence the original phenomenal pre-giving of this being is anything but self-evident, even if ontology at first follows the pull of the everyday interpretation. The laying-free of Dasein's original being must rather be wrested from it in counter-movement (im Gegenzug) to the falling ontic-ontological tendency of interpretation. The unit redeems § 5's paradox (nearest ontically, farthest ontologically) with its now-available ground — care's own falling — and states the analytic's kinetics in one word: Gegenzug, counter-pull; ontology of Dasein as movement against the current of Dasein's own self-interpretation.

The third unit generalizes the evidence: not only the exhibition of the most elementary structures of being-in-the-world, the delimitation of the world-concept, the clarification of the nearest and average who (the they-self), the interpretation of the "Da" — but above all the analyses of care, death, conscience, and guilt show how, in Dasein itself, the concernful common sense has taken power over the potentiality-of-being and its disclosure — that is, closure. The inventory converts the whole book into testimony for the counter-pull: at every station the phenomenon had to be taken from a prior covering; the possessive grammar of the last clause (common sense empowered over disclosure and closure alike) names the occupation the analytic contests.

The fourth unit names the method's violence — and generalizes it. Dasein's mode of being therefore demands of an ontological interpretation that has set itself the goal of the originality of phenomenal exhibition, that it conquer for itself the being of this being against its own covering-tendency. The existential analysis therefore constantly has, for the claims — or the complacency and tranquilized self-evidence — of the everyday interpretation, the character of a violence (Gewaltsamkeit). This character distinguishes the ontology of Dasein especially, but it belongs to every interpretation, because the understanding that develops itself in interpretation has the structure of projecting. But is there not, for this, in each case an own guidance and regulation? Whence are the ontological projections to take the evidence of phenomenal appropriateness for their "findings"? Ontological interpretation projects pregiven beings upon the being proper to them, in order to bring them to concept with regard to their structure. Where are the signposts for the direction of the projection, so that it strikes upon being at all? And what if the being that becomes thematic for the existential analytic conceals, in its way of being, the being belonging to it? The paragraph owns the reproach the reader has long harbored — the analysis is violent — and re-values it: violence not the analytic's vice but interpretation's essence (all understanding projects; every reading does violence to the complacent surface), intensified here because the theme itself hides. The questions that close are the genuine ones: projection needs direction and warrant — whence? The remainder of the section is their answer.

The fifth unit gives the first ground: Dasein interprets itself. To Dasein's being belongs self-interpretation. In the circumspect-concernful discovering of the "world," concern is co-sighted; Dasein always already understands itself factically in determinate existentiell possibilities, even if the projections stem only from das Man's common sense. Existence is, expressly or not, appropriately or not, somehow co-understood; every ontic understanding has its — even if only pre-ontological, not theoretically-thematically conceived — "inclusions." Every ontologically express question about Dasein's being is already prepared by Dasein's mode of being. The first signpost: the projection is not into the void — the theme has always already projected itself; ontology elaborates inclusions that ontic existence carries (§ 4's pre-ontological understanding as the analytic's raw material and warrant at once).

The sixth unit lets the relativism-objection form at full strength. Nevertheless — from what is one to gather what constitutes Dasein's "authentic" existence? Without an existentiell understanding, all analysis of existentiality remains groundless. Does not an ontic conception of existence underlie the accomplished interpretation of Dasein's authenticity and wholeness — one that may be possible, but need not be binding for everyone? The existential interpretation will never want to assume authority to decree (einen Machtspruch) over existentiell possibilities and obligations. But must it not justify itself with regard to the existentiell possibilities with which it gives the ontological interpretation its ontic ground? If Dasein's being is essentially potentiality-of-being and being-free for its ownmost possibilities, and if it in each case exists only in freedom for them or unfreedom against them, can the ontological interpretation do other than lay ontic possibilities (ways of the potentiality-of-being) at the ground, and project these upon their ontological possibility? And if Dasein mostly interprets itself from lostness in the concern of the "world," is not the determination of the ontic-existentiell possibilities won in counter-pull to that, and the existential analysis grounded on it, the mode of disclosure appropriate to such a being? Then does not the violence of the projection become the freeing (Freigabe) of Dasein's undisguised phenomenal stock? The objection (a possible ideal, binding for no one) is met not by denial but by structure: an ontology of a free being can only proceed from ontic possibilities (no neutral ground exists — the alternative to some existentiell footing is not objectivity but vacancy); the disclaimer of the Machtspruch is entered in the record (no existentiell legislation); and the counter-pull argument converts the violence one last time: against a self-covering being, violence is release — the forcing open of what closes itself is fidelity, not distortion.

The seventh unit narrows the arbitrariness: the "violent" pre-giving of possibilities of existence may be methodically demanded — but can it be withdrawn from free discretion? If the analytic lays at its ground, as existentielly authentic potentiality, anticipatory resoluteness — a possibility to which Dasein itself calls itself, and indeed from the ground of its existence — is this possibility then arbitrary? Is the way of being according to which Dasein's potentiality comports itself toward its distinguished possibility, death, contingently seized upon? Has being-in-the-world a higher court of its potentiality-of-being than its death? The three rhetorical questions carry the whole justification: the chosen ideal was chosen by the phenomenon — conscience calls to it (attestation), death stands into every Seinkönnen (structure) — and the last question is the argument's summit: what higher instance could adjudicate a being-in-the-world's possibilities than the possibility of its impossibility? The ideal is factical, yes; arbitrary, no.

The eighth unit presses to the deeper circle: the ontic-ontological projection of Dasein upon an authentic potentiality-of-being-whole may even be non-arbitrary — is the existential interpretation performed on this phenomenon thereby already justified? Whence does it take its guiding thread, if not from a "presupposed" idea of existence in general? What regulated the steps of the analysis of inauthentic everydayness, if not the posited concept of existence? And when we say Dasein "falls," and that therefore the authenticity of the potentiality-of-being must be wrested from it against this tendency of being — from what point of view is this spoken? Is not everything already — though duskily — illuminated by the light of the "presupposed" idea of existence? Whence does it take its right? Was the first projection indicating it without guidance? By no means. The self-cross-examination reaches the book's own first page: even "falling" is a verdict from somewhere — the whole analysis lit, however dimly, by the presupposed Existenzidee; and the abrupt Keineswegs pivots to the vindication.

The ninth unit vindicates the idea of existence from the Faktum. The formal indication of the idea of existence was guided by the understanding of being lying in Dasein itself. Without any ontological transparency, it nevertheless unveils: the being that we call Dasein I am in each case myself, and indeed as potentiality-of-being for which it is at issue to be this being. Dasein understands itself — though without sufficient ontological determinateness — as being-in-the-world; so being, it encounters beings of the mode of the ready-to-hand and present-at-hand. However far the distinction of existence and reality may be from an ontological concept — even if Dasein at first understands existence as reality — it is not merely present-at-hand but has, in whatever mythical and magical interpretation, in each case already understood itself: for otherwise it would not "live" in a myth and would not, in rite and cult, attend to its magic. The posited idea of existence is the existentielly non-binding predelineation of the formal structure of the understanding of Dasein in general. The vindication grounds the guiding idea where § 4 grounded the whole enterprise: in the Faktum of self-understanding — and the anthropological aside is a small marvel: myth and magic themselves witness the Seinsverständnis (only a self-understanding being lives in a myth, attends a cult) — even the "primitive" interpretation, however reality-bound, proves the structure the formal indication merely lifts. The idea presupposed is thus nothing but the form of what every Dasein already does.

The tenth unit traces the idea's career: under the guidance of this idea the preparatory analysis of nearest everydayness proceeded to the first conceptual delimitation of care; this phenomenon made possible the sharpened grasp of existence and its relations to facticity and falling; and the delimitation of the care-structure gave the basis for a first ontological distinction of existence and reality — leading to the thesis: the substance of man is existence. The genealogy shows the circle productive, not vicious: the formal idea guided; the analysis fattened it (care, facticity, falling); the fattened idea yielded the § 43 distinction and the § 25 thesis — presupposition and result mutually deepening, exactly the spiral § 32 legitimated.

The eleventh unit takes the last step down: but even this formal, existentielly non-binding idea of existence harbors in itself an already determinate, though unlifted, ontological "content," which — like the idea of reality demarcated against it — "presupposes" an idea of being in general. Only in its horizon can the distinction between existence and reality be accomplished: both, after all, mean being. The regress reaches bottom: beneath existence and reality, the idea of being itself — the two regional ideas distinguishable only within its horizon; the book's presupposition-structure fully exposed at the very point (§ 63) where it must be, since § 65 is about to project care upon its sense.

The twelfth unit lets the circle-objection sound at the fundamental level: but is not the ontologically clarified idea of being in general to be won only through the working-out of the understanding of being belonging to Dasein? This, however, lets itself be originally grasped only on the ground of an original interpretation of Dasein along the guiding thread of the idea of existence. Does it not then become fully manifest that the unrolled fundamental-ontological problem moves in a "circle"? The objection is granted its complete form: being from Dasein's understanding, Dasein's interpretation from the existence-idea, the existence-idea from an idea of being — the ring closed and named.

The thirteenth unit dissolves "presupposing" and re-founds the procedure. We showed already, in the analysis of the structure of understanding in general, that what is faulted with the inappropriate expression "circle" belongs to the essence and distinction of understanding itself. Nevertheless the investigation must now, with regard to the clarification of the hermeneutical situation of the fundamental-ontological problematic, expressly come back to the "circle-argument." The "circle-objection" against the existential interpretation means: the idea of existence and of being in general is "presupposed," and "according to it" Dasein is interpreted, in order to win from this the idea of being. But what does "presupposing" mean? Is a proposition posited with the idea of existence, from which, according to the formal rules of consequence, we deduce further propositions about Dasein's being? Or has this pre-supposing the character of understanding projecting — such that the interpretation developing this understanding lets what is to be interpreted first itself come to word, so that it may of itself decide whether it, as this being, yields the constitution of being upon which it was disclosed in the projection, formally-indicatively? Can beings come to word at all, with regard to their being, in any other way? In the existential analytic a "circle" in the proof cannot even be "avoided," because it does not prove at all according to the rules of "consequence-logic." What common sense — supposing thereby to satisfy the highest rigor of scientific investigation — wishes to eliminate with the avoidance of the "circle" is nothing less than the basic structure of care. Originally constituted by care, Dasein is in each case already ahead of itself; being, it has always already projected itself upon determinate possibilities of its existence, and in such existentiell projections it has, pre-ontologically, co-projected something like existence and being. Can this projecting, essential to Dasein, then be denied to research — which, like all research, is itself a mode of being of disclosive Dasein and wants to develop and bring to concept the understanding of being belonging to existence? The paragraph is § 32's circle-doctrine raised to the book's own case, and its two moves settle the matter. The disambiguation of Voraussetzen: not an axiom for deduction but a formally indicating projection submitted to the phenomenon's own verdict — the interpreted lets itself come to word and decides (the method's whole honesty in one clause: formal indication as falsifiable projection). And the deep grounding: the circle is care — the ahead-of-itself that has always co-projected being; to demand circle-free research is to demand research by a being that is not care, i.e., by nothing. The reproach dissolves into the constitution.

The fourteenth unit diagnoses the objector: the "circle-objection" itself comes from a mode of being of Dasein. To the common sense of concernful absorption in das Man, anything like projecting — and an ontological one at that — remains necessarily strange, because it "on principle" bars itself against it. Common sense attends, "theoretically" or "practically," only to the circumspectly surveyable; its distinction lies in supposing that it experiences only "factual" beings, so as to be able to rid itself of an understanding of being. It misrecognizes that beings can be "factually" experienced only when being is already understood, though not conceived: common sense misunderstands understanding (Verständigkeit mißversteht das Verstehen). And therefore it must also necessarily pass off as "violent" whatever lies beyond the reach of its understanding, and the going-beyond toward it. The genealogy completes the defense: the objection located in das Man's positivism — the self-image of pure factuality convicted by § 31 (facts only within understood being) — and the four-word epigram seals it; the "violence"-charge, likewise, unmasked as common sense's name for its own horizon's edge.

The fifteenth unit converts the circle into an imperative — and bills the rivals. Talk of the "circle" of understanding is the expression of a double misrecognition: (1) that understanding itself constitutes a basic mode of Dasein's being; (2) that this being is constituted as care. To deny the circle, to conceal it, or even to want to overcome it means to fasten this misrecognition definitively. The effort must rather aim at springing into this "circle" originally and wholly, in order to secure, already in the approach of the analysis of Dasein, the full view of Dasein's circular being. Not too much, but too little is "presupposed" for the ontology of Dasein, if one "departs" from a worldless I in order then to procure for it an object and an ontologically groundless relation to it; too short is the reach of the gaze, if "life" is made the problem and then death is also occasionally taken into account; artificially and dogmatically pruned is the thematic object, if one restricts oneself "at first" to a "theoretical subject" in order then to supplement it "on the practical side" with an appended "ethics." The imperative radicalizes § 32 (there: come into the circle rightly; here: spring into it originally and wholly), and the closing triple audit reverses the ledger with a flourish: the presupposition-charge inverted — the Cartesian (worldless I plus procured object), the Lebensphilosoph (life with death as appendix), and the Kantian (theoretical subject plus appended ethics) each convicted of presupposing too little; the analytic's rich fore-having is its rigor, the rivals' parsimony their dogmatism.

The closing unit certifies and proceeds: this may suffice for clarifying the existential sense of the hermeneutical situation of an original analytic of Dasein. With the setting-forth of anticipatory resoluteness, Dasein is brought into the fore-having with regard to its authentic wholeness; the authenticity of the potentiality-of-being-a-self vouches for the fore-sight upon original existentiality; and this secures the minting of the appropriate existential conceptuality. The section closes on the triple certification with which it opened, now earned: fore-having, fore-sight, fore-grasp aligned on the authentic whole.

The final unit adds the truth-theoretic seal. The analysis of anticipatory resoluteness led at the same time to the phenomenon of original and authentic truth. It was shown earlier how the proximally and mostly dominant understanding of being conceives being in the sense of presence-at-hand and so covers over the original phenomenon of truth. But if being "is given" only insofar as truth "is," and if the understanding of being varies according to the kind of truth, then original and authentic truth must guarantee the understanding of the being of Dasein and of being in general. The ontological "truth" of the existential analysis develops itself on the ground of the original existentiell truth — but the latter does not necessarily need the former. The most original, fundamental existential truth, toward which the fundamental-ontological problematic strives — preparing the question of being in general — is the disclosedness of the sense of the being of care; for the laying-free of this sense, the undiminished holding-ready of the full structural stock of care is needed. The paragraph knots § 44 into the method: since being is indexed to truth, the deepest interpretation requires the deepest truth — anticipatory resoluteness, as authentic disclosedness, is the truth in which alone care's sense can show itself; and the asymmetry-clause is a fine humility: ontology lives from existentiell truth (the analyst must be resolute enough to see), but existentiell truth owes ontology nothing — one can exist authentically without ever philosophizing. With this, the hermeneutical situation is complete, and § 64 (the self) and § 65 (temporality) may lawfully proceed.

##### § 64. Care and Selfhood

The opening unit takes stock and sharpens the unity-question. The unity of the constitutive moments of care — existentiality, facticity, fallenness — made possible the first ontological delimitation of the totality of Dasein's structural whole; the care-structure was brought to the existential formula: ahead-of-itself-already-being-in (a world) as being-alongside (innerworldly encountered beings). The totality of this structure does not first grow from a coupling, yet it is articulated. This ontological result had to be assessed as to how far it satisfies the demands of an original interpretation; the reflection yielded that neither the whole Dasein nor its authentic potentiality-of-being had been made theme. But the attempt to grasp the whole Dasein seemed to founder precisely on the care-structure: the ahead-of-itself presented itself as a not-yet. The ahead-of-itself characterized as an outstanding unveiled itself, however, to the genuinely existential consideration as being toward the end, which every Dasein is in the ground of its being. Likewise we made plain that care, in the call of conscience, summons Dasein to its ownmost potentiality-of-being; the understanding of the appeal revealed itself — originally understood — as anticipatory resoluteness, which encloses in itself an authentic potentiality-of-being-whole of Dasein. The care-structure does not speak against a possible being-whole; it is the condition of the possibility of such an existentiell potentiality. In the course of these analyses it became plain that in the phenomenon of care the existential phenomena of death, conscience, and guilt lie anchored: the articulation of the totality of the structural whole has become still richer, and therewith the existential question of the unity of this totality still more pressing. The recapitulation is the division's ledger balanced: the § 46 antinomy dissolved (the ahead not an outstanding but being-toward-the-end — care the condition of wholeness, not its obstacle), the new anchorings entered (death, conscience, guilt inside care), and the price named: richer articulation, more urgent unity-question — the § 41 closing question returning with compound interest.

The second unit locates the traditional answer and re-poses the who. How are we to conceive this unity? How can Dasein exist unitarily in the named ways and possibilities of its being? Manifestly only in such a way that it itself is this being in its essential possibilities — that in each case I am this being. The "I" seems to "hold together" the totality of the structural whole; the "I" and the "self" have from of old been conceived, in the "ontology" of this being, as the supporting ground (substance or subject). The present analytic already struck, in the preparatory characterization of everydayness, upon the question of Dasein's who: it showed that proximally and mostly Dasein is not itself but lost in the they-self, which is an existentiell modification of the authentic self. The question of the ontological constitution of selfhood remained unanswered; the guiding thread was fixed in principle — if the self belongs to the essential determinations of Dasein, whose "essence" lies in existence, then I-hood and selfhood must be conceived existentially. Negatively it also showed that the ontological characterization of das Man forbids every use of categories of presence-at-hand (substance); and it became fundamentally clear: care is not to be derived ontologically from reality or built up with reality's categories. Care already harbors the phenomenon of the self in itself, if indeed the thesis rightly stands that the expression "care of self," on the analogy of solicitude as care for others, would be a tautology. But then the problem of the ontological determination of Dasein's selfhood sharpens itself into the question of the existential "connection" between care and selfhood. The unit assembles every prior deposit on the self (§ 25's guiding thread, § 27's modification, § 41's tautology-argument, § 43's ban on reality-categories) and re-frames the tradition's instinct: the I as the "holder-together" — substance or subject as the answer to the unity-question — is exactly what the section must audit; the unity sought may not be a bearer at all.

The third unit opens the phenomenal dossier: the I-saying. The clarification of the existentiality of the self takes its "natural" departure from Dasein's everyday self-interpretation, which speaks itself out about "itself" in saying-I — vocalization not being necessary. With "I" this being means itself; the content of the expression counts as absolutely simple: it means in each case only me and nothing further. As this simple thing, the "I" is also no determination of other things — not itself predicate, but the absolute "subject." What is spoken out and addressed in saying-I is always encountered as the same self-maintaining thing. The characters of "simplicity," "substantiality," and "personality," which Kant, for example, lays at the ground of his doctrine of the paralogisms of pure reason, spring from a genuine pre-phenomenological experience; the question remains whether what is ontically so experienced may be interpreted ontologically with the help of the named "categories." The move is the book's constant one, applied to grammar's proudest word: the phenomenal datum honored (the I said as simple, subject, selfsame — a genuine experience) and its categorial interpretation suspended; Kant's three paralogism-predicates are granted their phenomenal source precisely so that the analysis can ask whether the source licenses the ontology.

The fourth unit fixes Kant's double position. Kant does show, in strict fit to the phenomenal stock given in saying-I, that the ontic theses about the soul-substance inferred from those characters are without right; but thereby only an ontic mis-explanation of the I is rejected — the ontological interpretation of selfhood is by no means won, or even secured and positively prepared. Although Kant tries more rigorously than his predecessors to hold fast the phenomenal content of saying-I, he slides back again into the same inappropriate ontology of the substantial whose ontic foundations he has theoretically denied to the I. This is to be shown more exactly, in order thereby to fix the ontological sense of the approach to the analysis of selfhood in saying-I; the Kantian analysis of the "I think" is to be adduced only so far as required for clarifying this problematic. The verdict-form is § 6's Kant-clause executed: the paralogisms honored (the greatest critique of soul-substance) and re-arraigned — refuting rational psychology's inferences is not yet an ontology of the self; the negative victory left the categorial horizon standing, into which Kant then slid back.

The fifth unit reports the doctrine: the "I" is a mere consciousness that accompanies all concepts; with it "nothing further is represented than a transcendental subject of thoughts"; "consciousness in itself is not so much a representation... as a form of representation in general"; the "I think" is "the form of apperception, which attaches to every experience and precedes it." The three citations fix the textual base: the I as form, not content — Kant's deepest anti-substantialist stratum, quoted so that the coming critique cannot be accused of fighting a straw Kant.

The sixth unit gives the doctrine its best reading. Kant rightly grasps the phenomenal content of the "I" in the expression "I think" — or, if the inclusion of the "practical person" in "intelligence" is co-attended, "I act." Saying-I must, in Kant's sense, be grasped as saying-I-think. Kant seeks to fix the phenomenal content of the I as res cogitans. If he calls this I "logical subject," this does not mean the I is a concept won merely by logical means: the I is rather the subject of logical comportment, of binding. "I think" means "I bind"; all binding is "I bind." In every taking-together and relating, the I always already lies at the ground — hypokeimenon. Hence the subjectum is "consciousness in itself," not a representation but rather its "form": the I-think is nothing represented, but the formal structure of representing as such, whereby anything like a represented first becomes possible. Form of representation means neither a frame nor a universal concept, but that which, as eidos, makes every represented and representing what it is. The I, understood as form of representation, means the same as: it is "logical subject." The exegesis is generous to a fault and precisely thereby devastating in preparation: "logical subject" is saved from the psychologistic misreading (not a logically derived concept but the subject of the logical act) — and in the same breath the Greek words are planted like charges: hypokeimenon, eidos — Kant's most critical formula translated back into the ontology of the underlying and the look; the form of apperception exposed as substance-thinking in its subtlest costume.

The seventh unit weighs the yield — and the note points to the Kantbuch. The positive in the Kantian analysis is double: first, Kant sees the impossibility of the ontic reduction of the I to a substance; second, he holds fast the I as "I think." Nevertheless he grasps this I again as subject, and therewith in an ontologically inappropriate sense: for the ontological concept of the subject characterizes not the selfhood of the I qua self, but the selfsameness and constancy of something always already present-at-hand. To determine the I ontologically as subject means to posit it as something always already present-at-hand; the being of the I is understood as reality of the res cogitans. The note refers, for the analysis of transcendental apperception, to the author's Kant and the Problem of Metaphysics. The verdict lands on the exact word: subject — even the form-doctrine, once the I is called subjectum, imports the ontology of standing presence (Selbigkeit und Beständigkeit eines immer schon Vorhandenen); the distinction that carries the whole section is minted in passing: Selbstheit versus Selbigkeit — selfhood versus mere selfsameness — the self's way of being versus a thing's identity through time.

The eighth unit asks why the relapse was necessary — and the long note carries the Heimsoeth debate. Whence comes it that Kant cannot ontologically exploit the genuine phenomenal approach in the "I think," and must fall back on the "subject" — the substantial? The I is not only "I think" but "I think something"; and does Kant not himself repeatedly stress that the I remains related to its representations and is nothing without them? The appended note engages Heimsoeth's essay on personality-consciousness and the thing-in-itself: Heimsoeth urges that the close interworking of theoretical and practical reason in Kant is too little heeded — that the categories retain validity under the primacy of practical reason and find a new, de-naturalized application (substance in "person" and personal immortality, causality as "causality from freedom," community in the "community of rational beings"), serving as conceptual means of fixing an approach to the unconditioned without rationalizing object-cognition. But here — Heidegger replies — the authentic ontological problem is leapt over: the question cannot be avoided whether these "categories" can retain original validity and merely need different application, or whether they do not pervert from the ground up the ontological problematic of Dasein. Even if theoretical reason is built into practical, the existential-ontological problem of the self remains not only unsolved but unposed.
