On what ontological soil is the "interworking" of theoretical and practical reason to be accomplished? Does theoretical comportment determine the person's mode of being, or practical, or neither — and which then? Do the paralogisms, despite their fundamental significance, not reveal the ontological groundlessness of the problematic of the self from Descartes' res cogitans to Hegel's concept of spirit? One need not think "naturalistically" or "rationalistically," and can yet stand in a only more fateful — because seemingly self-evident — subservience to the ontology of the "substantial." The note also refers to Heimsoeth's companion essay on the metaphysical motives of critical idealism, and to Scheler's Formalismus on "person" and the I of transcendental apperception. Text and note together stage the section's deepest confrontation. The text's question (why must Kant relapse?) is answered by the clue it plants: the I is I-think-something — relatedness omitted; and the note conducts, in small print, a whole quarrel with the era's Kant-renaissance: Heimsoeth's rescue (categories re-applied practically — substance ennobled into person) is refused at the root, for re-application is not revision — the question is the categories' fitness for Dasein at all; and the arc drawn in one clause — the self's groundlessness from Descartes' res cogitans to Hegel's Geist — indicts the entire modern philosophy of subjectivity, with the closing warning aimed at every pious personalism (Scheler included): one may scorn naturalism and still serve the ontology of the substantial, the more fatally for its seeming self-evidence.

The ninth unit locates the omission exactly: world. These representations are for Kant the "empirical" that the I "accompanies" — the appearances to which it "attaches." But Kant nowhere shows the mode of being of this "attaching" and "accompanying"; at bottom it is understood as the constant co-presence-at-hand of the I with its representations. Kant avoided cutting the I off from thinking, yet without positing the "I think" itself in its full essential content as "I think something," and above all without seeing the ontological "presupposition" for the "I think something" as the basic determinateness of the self. For even the approach "I think something" is ontologically underdetermined, because the "something" remains indeterminate: if an innerworldly being is understood by it, then the presupposition of world lies unspoken therein — and precisely this phenomenon co-determines the constitution of being of the I, if indeed it is to be able to be something like an "I think something." Saying-I means the being that in each case I am as "I-am-in-a-world." Kant did not see the phenomenon of world, and was consequent enough to keep the "representations" far from the a priori content of the "I think"; but thereby the I was again forced back to an isolated subject that accompanies representations in an ontologically wholly indeterminate manner. The diagnosis is the book's Kant-critique at its most surgical, and its fairness is its force: Kant's very consistency convicted him — seeing no world, he rightly excluded the empirical from apperception's a priori, and so sealed the I in isolation; the unexamined relation ("accompanying" — a word, not an ontology) defaulted to co-presence. Had the something been thought, world would have surfaced; had world surfaced, the I would have read: I-am-in-a-world. The § 43(a) refutation-of-idealism critique is hereby completed on the side of the subject.

The tenth unit turns to the everyday I and its systematic mendacity. In saying-I, Dasein speaks itself out as being-in-the-world. But does the everyday saying-I mean itself as being-in-the-world? Here one must distinguish: saying I, Dasein does mean the being that it in each case itself is; but the everyday self-interpretation has the tendency to understand itself from the attended "world" — in the ontic meaning-of-itself it mis-sees itself with regard to the mode of being of the being that it itself is, and this holds above all of Dasein's basic constitution, being-in-the-world. The distinction is finely cut: the reference succeeds (the I means me), the self-understanding fails (me read as a worldly item) — everyday I-talk is right de re and wrong de modo essendi; § 5's Rückstrahlung located inside the first-person pronoun.

The eleventh unit names the motive and the mechanism. Whereby is this "fugitive" saying-I motivated? By Dasein's falling, as which it flees before itself into das Man. The "natural" I-talk is performed by the they-self; in the "I" speaks itself out the self that I proximally and mostly authentically am not. For absorption in the everyday manifold and the chasing-after of the attended, the self of the self-forgotten I-attend-to shows itself as the constantly selfsame but indeterminately empty simple — one is, after all, what one attends to. That the "natural" ontic I-talk overlooks the phenomenal content of the Dasein meant in the I gives the ontological interpretation of the I no right to join in this overlooking and to force upon the problematic of the self an inappropriate "categorial" horizon. The paragraph springs the section's trap with a genealogical flourish: the paralogism-predicates (simple, selfsame, empty subject) are re-derived as artifacts of falling — the self-forgotten busy-ness shows itself precisely as the empty constant "I" — so that Descartes' and Kant's phenomenal basis turns out to be das Man's self-report: rational psychology as the ontologization of fugitive I-saying. The closing rule is the section's methodological yield: philosophy may not co-perform the everyday overlooking.

The twelfth unit converts the finding into the positive doctrine of self-constancy. The ontological interpretation of the "I" wins the solution by no means merely through refusing allegiance to everyday I-talk — but it does win the predelineation of the direction of further questioning. The I means the being that one is "being-in-the-world"; but already-being-in-a-world, as being-alongside the innerworldly ready-to-hand, means equiprimordially ahead-of-itself. "I" means the being for which the being of the being that it is, is at issue: with the "I," care speaks itself out — proximally and mostly in the "fugitive" I-talk of concern. The they-self says I-I loudest and most frequently, because at bottom it is not authentically itself and evades the authentic potentiality-of-being. If the ontological constitution of the self can be traced back neither to an I-substance nor to a "subject," but conversely the everyday-fugitive saying of I-I must be understood from the authentic potentiality-of-being, it does not yet follow that the self is then the constantly present-at-hand ground of care. Selfhood is to be read off existentially only from the authentic potentiality-of-being-a-self — that is, from the authenticity of Dasein's being as care. From it, the constancy of the self (Ständigkeit des Selbst), as the supposed persistence of the subjectum, receives its clarification; but the phenomenon of the authentic potentiality-of-being also opens the view for the constancy of the self in the sense of having-won-a-stand (Standgewonnenhaben). The constancy of the self, in the double sense of steadiness and steadfastness (der beständigen Standfestigkeit), is the authentic counter-possibility to the non-self-constancy (Unselbst-ständigkeit) of irresolute falling. Self-constancy (Selbst-ständigkeit) means existentially nothing other than anticipatory resoluteness; the ontological structure of the latter reveals the existentiality of the selfhood of the self. This is the section's summit and one of the book's great re-mintings: the tradition's substrate-constancy (Beharrlichkeit of the subjectum) is replaced by an enacted constancy — Ständigkeit as Standfestigkeit, the stand won and held — and the German word for independence, Selbständigkeit, is split by a hyphen into its buried sense: Selbst-ständigkeit, the self's standing, which "is" only as anticipatory resoluteness. The self is not the ground of care (the loudest I belongs to the least self — the frequency of I-I an index of flight); the self is a way care can be enacted: selfhood as achievement, not substrate. Identity re-founded as fidelity.

The thirteenth unit gives the authentic I its (non-)utterance: Dasein is authentically itself in the original individuation of the reticent resoluteness that exacts anxiety of itself. Authentic being-a-self, as silent, precisely does not say "I-I," but "is," in reticence, the thrown being as which it can authentically be. The self that the reticence of resolute existence unveils is the original phenomenal soil for the question of the being of the "I"; only the phenomenal orientation to the sense of being of the authentic potentiality-of-being-a-self puts one in the position to discuss what ontological right substantiality, simplicity, and personality can claim as characters of selfhood. The ontological question of the being of the self must be twisted out of the fore-having — constantly suggested by the predominant saying-I — of a persistently present-at-hand self-thing. The paragraph completes the acoustics of the chapter: the authentic self is the quiet one — reticence, not the pronoun, is its signature — and the paralogism-predicates are remanded: their possible right can be adjudicated only from the resolute self, not from grammar; the self-thing expelled from the fore-having by name.

The closing unit inverts the founding-order once and for all: care does not need the founding in a self; rather, existentiality, as a constitutive of care, gives the ontological constitution of Dasein's self-constancy — to which, corresponding to the full structural content of care, factical fallen-ness into non-self-constancy belongs. The fully conceived care-structure includes the phenomenon of selfhood; its clarification accomplishes itself as the interpretation of the sense of care, as which Dasein's totality of being was determined. The inversion is total and final: not the self beneath care (the tradition's order — subject bearing its acts) but selfhood within care, as care's authentic enactment, with un-selfhood equally accommodated (falling's non-constancy part of the full structure). The unity-question thus passes intact to § 65: since no self-thing holds care together, the unity must be sought in care's own sense — and the section's last clause hands over exactly there.

##### § 65. Temporality as the Ontological Sense of Care

The opening unit sets the final approach. The characterization of the "connection" between care and selfhood aimed not only at clarifying the special problem of I-hood; it was to serve the last preparation for the phenomenal grasping of the totality of the structural whole of Dasein. The undeviating discipline of the existential question-formulation is needed, if Dasein's mode of being is not, after all, to invert itself for the ontological gaze into a mode — even a wholly indifferent one — of presence-at-hand. Dasein becomes "essential" in the authentic existence that constitutes itself as anticipatory resoluteness; this mode of the authenticity of care contains Dasein's original self-constancy and wholeness. In the undistracted, existentially understanding look upon it, the laying-free of the ontological sense of Dasein's being must accomplish itself. The unit posts the last guard (even now the vorhanden-inversion threatens) and fixes the phenomenal site: care's sense is to be read where care is whole and constant — at anticipatory resoluteness; everything since § 46 was the securing of this one vantage.

The second unit asks what a "sense" is — and answers from § 32. What is ontologically sought with the sense of care? What does sense mean? The investigation encountered the phenomenon in the analysis of understanding and interpretation: according to it, sense is that within which the intelligibility of something holds itself, without coming into view expressly and thematically. Sense means the whereupon (Woraufhin) of the primary projection, from out of which something can be conceived in its possibility as what it is. Projecting discloses possibilities — that is, such as makes possible. The retrieval is exact and load-bearing: sense = the upon-which of the projection, the horizon from which something is intelligible as possible — so "the sense of care" will mean: that upon which care is projected such that its structure becomes intelligible; not a meaning attached to care but care's own enabling horizon.

The third unit converts the definition into the method: to lay free the whereupon of a projection means to disclose what makes the projected possible. Methodically this demands pursuing the projection — mostly unexpress — that underlies an interpretation, in such a way that what is projected in it becomes disclosed and graspable with regard to its whereupon. To set forth the sense of care then means: to follow the projection that underlies and guides the original existential interpretation of Dasein, so that in what it projects, its whereupon becomes visible. The projected is the being of Dasein, disclosed in what constitutes it as authentic potentiality-of-being-whole; the whereupon of this projected — of the disclosed, so constituted being — is what makes possible this constitution of being as care. With the question of the sense of care is asked: what makes possible the totality of the articulated structural whole of care, in the unity of its unfolded articulation? The method is hermeneutics turned upon the analytic itself: the book's own guiding projection is to be interrogated for its horizon — § 63's owned fore-structure now worked, exactly as promised; the question of being's meaning operationalized, for the first time in the book, as a determinate procedure.

The fourth unit widens the concept to being as such: strictly taken, sense means the whereupon of the primary projection of the understanding of being. Being-in-the-world, disclosed to itself, understands, with the being of the being that it itself is, equiprimordially the being of innerworldly discovered beings — though unthematically and even undifferentiated in its primary modes of existence and reality. All ontic experience of beings — the circumspect reckoning with the ready-to-hand as much as the positive-scientific cognition of the present-at-hand — grounds in more or less transparent projections of the being of the respective beings; but these projections harbor in themselves a whereupon, from which, as it were, the understanding of being nourishes itself. The widening is the fundamental-ontological stake declared: every ontic comportment runs on a projection of being, and every such projection has its horizon — the Woraufhin from which Seinsverständnis feeds; the unwritten Division Three (being's own horizon: Temporalität) is visible in this clause as through a doorway.

The fifth unit fixes the order of "having sense": when we say beings "have sense," this means they have become accessible in their being — which being, projected upon its whereupon, first "authentically" "has sense." Beings "have" sense only because, disclosed as being in advance, they become intelligible in the projection of being — from its whereupon. The primary projection of the understanding of being "gives" the sense; the question of the sense of the being of a being makes thematic the whereupon of the understanding of being that underlies all being of beings. The bookkeeping is strict: sense belongs primarily to being, derivatively to beings — things are meaningful only inside a projected being; the § 32 doctrine (only Dasein "has" sense) refined into the two-step that the being-question requires.

The sixth unit applies it to Dasein and blocks the last dualism. Dasein is disclosed to itself, authentically or inauthentically, with regard to its existence; existing, it understands itself — in such a way that this understanding is no pure apprehending but constitutes the existentiell being of the factical potentiality-of-being. The disclosed being is that of a being for which this being is at issue; the sense of this being — of care — which makes care possible in its constitution, originally constitutes the being of the potentiality-of-being. The sense of Dasein's being is not a free-floating other and "outside" of itself, but the self-understanding Dasein itself. What makes possible the being of Dasein, and therewith its factical existence? The guard is decisive: the sense sought is no second entity behind care — no Platonic backdrop, no ground-substance outside — but Dasein itself as self-understanding: the horizon immanent to the projecting; whatever answers must be Dasein's own, not an appended metaphysical support.

The seventh unit derives the future. What was projected in the original existential projection of existence unveiled itself as anticipatory resoluteness. What makes possible this authentic being-whole of Dasein with regard to the unity of its articulated structural whole? Formally-existentially grasped, anticipatory resoluteness is being toward the ownmost distinguished potentiality-of-being. Such a thing is possible only in that Dasein can come toward itself (auf sich zukommen) in its ownmost possibility at all, and endures the possibility, in this letting-itself-come-toward-itself, as possibility — that is, exists. The letting-itself-come-toward-itself that endures the distinguished possibility is the original phenomenon of the future (Zu-kunft). If authentic or inauthentic being toward death belongs to Dasein's being, this is possible only as futural, in the sense now indicated and to be determined more closely. "Future" means here not a now that, not yet become "actual," will one day first be; it means the coming (Kunft) in which Dasein comes toward itself in its ownmost potentiality-of-being. Anticipation makes Dasein authentically futural — in such a way that anticipation is itself possible only insofar as Dasein, as being, always already comes toward itself at all: that is, is futural in its being in general. The derivation is the book's summit-move, executed in four sentences: anticipatory resoluteness requires a coming-toward-oneself that holds the possible open — and this Auf-sich-zukommen, read out of the word Zukunft itself (Zu-kunft, the to-coming), is the future — not a not-yet-now on a line but the self's advent to itself. The order of grounding is then doubled with perfect care: anticipation makes Dasein authentically futural, and presupposes that Dasein is futural as such — the existentiell mode enabled by the existential structure it exhibits. Time enters the book not as a container but as the way the self comes.

The eighth unit derives havingness — beenness — from the future. Anticipatory resoluteness understands Dasein in its essential being-guilty; this understanding means: to take over being-guilty existing, to be the thrown ground of nullity. But taking-over of thrownness means: to be Dasein authentically in how it in each case already was. The taking-over of thrownness is possible, however, only in such a way that futural Dasein can be its ownmost "how it in each case already was" — its "been" (Gewesen). Only insofar as Dasein in general is as "I am-been" (ich bin-gewesen), can it come toward itself futurally in such a way that it comes back (zurück-kommt). Authentically futural, Dasein is authentically been. Anticipation into the uttermost and ownmost possibility is the understanding coming-back upon the ownmost been: Dasein can be authentically been only insofar as it is futural. Beenness springs, in a certain manner, from the future. The paragraph performs the analysis's most counterintuitive stroke and grounds it fully: the past-dimension derived from the future — for the throw is taken over (guilt owned) only by the self that comes toward itself and, coming, comes back upon what it already was. The grammar carries the ontology: Gewesenheit, not Vergangenheit — the perfect of a being that is its having-been (ich bin-gewesen: the "am" inside the "was") — and the closing sentence, scandalous to every common chronology, states the ecstatic order: beenness springs from the future, because only the coming self can own its origin.

The ninth unit derives the present from both: anticipatory resoluteness discloses the current situation of the Da in such a way that existence, acting, circumspectly attends to the factically environmentally ready-to-hand. Resolute being alongside the ready-to-hand of the situation — the acting letting-encounter of what is environmentally present — is possible only in a making-present (Gegenwärtigen) of these beings. Only as the present, in the sense of making-present, can resoluteness be what it is: the undisguised letting-encounter of what it seizes, acting. The third ecstasis completes the triad from § 60's situation: action requires the present — not the now-point but the making-present, the letting-encounter — Gegenwart read as Gegenwärtigen, a deed of disclosure, so that even the "now" is originally something Dasein does.

The tenth unit speaks the definition. Futurally coming back upon itself, resoluteness brings itself, making-present, into the situation. Beenness springs from the future — in such a way that the been (better: beening — gewesende) future releases the present from itself. This phenomenon, unitary as been-making-present future (gewesend-gegenwärtigende Zukunft), we call temporality (Zeitlichkeit). Only insofar as Dasein is determined as temporality does it make possible for itself the characterized authentic potentiality-of-being-whole of anticipatory resoluteness. Temporality unveils itself as the sense of authentic care. The definition-sentence is the book's title cashed: the three derivations gathered into one hyphenated phenomenon — the future that, having-been, releases the present — with the participial coinage gewesend (beening: the having-been as ongoing enactment, not deposit) marking that no member is a thing; and the order inside the formula is doctrine: future first, beenness from it, present released by both. Care's sense found: Zeitlichkeit — and the announcement is exact in its modesty: sense of authentic care; the generalization follows.

The eleventh unit quarantines the vocabulary. The phenomenal content of this sense, drawn from the constitution of being of anticipatory resoluteness, fulfills the signification of the term temporality. The terminological use of this expression must at first keep at bay all the significations of "future," "past," and "present" that press in from the vulgar concept of time; this holds also of the concepts of a "subjective" and "objective," an "immanent" and "transcendent" "time." Insofar as Dasein understands itself proximally and mostly inauthentically, it may be surmised that the "time" of the vulgar understanding presents a genuine phenomenon, but a derivative one: it springs from inauthentic temporality, which has its own origin. The concepts "future," "past," "present" have at first grown from the inauthentic understanding of time; the terminological delimitation of the corresponding original and authentic phenomena struggles with the same difficulty that clings to all ontological terminology. Violences are, in this field of investigation, not arbitrariness but necessity grounded in the matter. To be able to exhibit without gaps the origin of inauthentic temporality from the original and authentic, however, the original phenomenon, so far only roughly characterized, first needs concrete elaboration. The quarantine repeats § 61's warning with the derivation-ledger now open: vulgar time genuine but derivative, twice removed (from inauthentic temporality, which itself derives) — the double descent Chapter Six must trace; and the violence-clause (§ 63's yield) is re-posted where the wrenching of words will be most severe.

The twelfth unit generalizes from the authentic mode to care as such: if resoluteness constitutes the mode of authentic care, while care itself is possible only through temporality, then the phenomenon won in view of resoluteness must itself present only a modality of temporality — which makes possible care as such in general. The totality of Dasein's being as care means: ahead-of-itself-already-being-in (a world) as being-alongside (innerworldly encountered beings). At the first fixing of this articulated structure it was pointed out that, with regard to this articulation, the ontological question must be driven still further back, to the laying-free of the unity of the totality of the structural manifold. The original unity of the care-structure lies in temporality. The generalization discharges § 41's closing question by name: the "still more original phenomenon" sought there is produced — temporality as the unity that no coupling and no self-thing could supply; the demonstration follows member by member.

The thirteenth unit maps the members — and rescues the formula's own words. The ahead-of-itself grounds in the future. The already-being-in... makes known in itself beenness. Being-alongside... becomes possible in making-present. After what has been said, it forbids itself of itself to grasp the "ahead" (vor) in the "ahead-of-itself," and the "already" (schon), from the vulgar understanding of time. The "ahead" does not mean the "before" in the sense of "not-yet-now — but later"; just as little does the "already" mean a "no-longer-now — but earlier." Had the expressions this temporal signification — which they can also have — then care's temporality would say it is something that is "earlier" and "later," "not yet" and "no longer" at once: care would be conceived as a being that occurs and runs off "in time," and the being of a being with Dasein's character would become something present-at-hand. If that is impossible, the temporal signification of these expressions must be another. The "ahead" indicates the future as that which first makes it possible that Dasein can be such that its potentiality-of-being is at issue for it; the self-projection upon the "for-the-sake-of-itself," grounding in the future, is an essential character of existentiality: its primary sense is the future. The mapping executes the twelfth unit's claim on the formula's first member, and the philological scruple is the argument: the care-formula's own prepositions (vor, schon) always carried a temporal sound — but in the ecstatic register, not the sequential; read sequentially, care becomes an occurrence in time (the ruin of the analytic); read ecstatically, the formula was temporality's cipher from § 41 on. Existentiality = future: the first equation posted.

The fourteenth unit posts the second: likewise the "already" means the existential-temporal sense of the being of the being that, insofar as it is, is in each case already thrown. Only because care grounds in beenness can Dasein exist as the thrown being that it is. "As long as" Dasein factically exists, it is never past (vergangen), but always already been, in the sense of "I am-been"; and it can be been only as long as it is. Past, by contrast, we call a being that is no longer present-at-hand. Hence Dasein, existing, can never ascertain itself as a present-at-hand fact that arises and passes away "with time" and is piecemeal already past: it "finds itself" always only as thrown factum. In disposedness, Dasein is assailed by itself as the being that it, still being, already was — that is, constantly is as been. The primary existential sense of facticity lies in beenness. The formulation of the care-structure indicates, with the expressions "ahead" and "already," the temporal sense of existentiality and facticity. The second equation (facticity = beenness) is drawn with the decisive lexical split now formalized: vergangen reserved for the no-longer-vorhanden (things have a past); Dasein is never past while it is — it is its been — and § 29's whole mood-doctrine is re-grounded in one clause: disposedness is how the been assails; attunement as the felt perfect tense of existence.

The fifteenth unit accounts for the missing index: by contrast, such an indication is lacking for the third constitutive moment of care — the falling being-alongside. This is not to mean that falling does not also ground in temporality; it is to intimate that making-present — in which falling at the attended ready-to-hand and present-at-hand primarily grounds — remains, in the mode of original temporality, enclosed (eingeschlossen) in future and beenness. Resolved, Dasein has precisely fetched itself back out of falling, in order to be all the more authentically "there" (da) in the "moment of vision" (Augenblick) for the disclosed situation. The paragraph turns an apparent defect of the formula into doctrine: the third member carries no temporal adverb because the authentic present has none of its own — it is held, enclosed in future and beenness, released by them (the tenth unit's Entlassung); and in the last sentence the book's counter-concept to the now is minted almost in passing: der Augenblick — the moment of vision, the resolutely held present — the Kierkegaardian instant given its ontological seat, to be elaborated in § 68.

The sixteenth unit states the unity-theorem and the deepest scruple. Temporality makes possible the unity of existence, facticity, and falling, and thus constitutes originally the totality of the care-structure. The moments of care are not pieced together by accumulation — as little as temporality itself first composes itself "with time" out of future, beenness, and present. Temporality "is" no being at all: it is not — it temporalizes itself (sie zeitigt sich). Why we nevertheless cannot avoid saying "temporality 'is' — the sense of care," "temporality 'is' — thus and so determined," can be made intelligible only from the clarified idea of being and of the "is" in general. Temporality temporalizes, and indeed possible ways of itself: these make possible the manifold of Dasein's modes of being, above all the basic possibility of authentic and inauthentic existence. The theorem answers § 41 in full (unity without assembly — the anti-composite rule satisfied at last), and then the analysis performs its most vertiginous act of honesty: temporality is exempted from being itself — es ist nicht, es zeitigt sich — while the unavoidable "is" of every sentence about it is flagged as a debt payable only from the clarified idea of being: the book confessing, at its summit, that its own copula outruns its results; the third division's task inscribed in a grammatical apology.

The seventeenth unit names the ecstases. Future, beenness, present show the phenomenal characters of the "toward-itself," the "back-upon," the "letting-encounter-of": the phenomena of the toward..., upon..., alongside... reveal temporality as the ekstatikon pure and simple. Temporality is the original "outside-itself" in and for itself. We therefore call the characterized phenomena future, beenness, present the ecstases of temporality. Temporality is not, prior to this, a being that first steps out of itself; its essence is temporalizing in the unity of the ecstases. What is characteristic of the "time" accessible to the vulgar understanding consists precisely in this, among other things: that in it, as a pure now-sequence without beginning and end, the ecstatic character of original temporality is leveled down. This leveling itself, however, grounds, according to its existential sense, in a determinate possible temporalizing, in accordance with which temporality, as inauthentic, temporalizes the named "time." If, therefore, the "time" accessible to Dasein's common sense is demonstrated to be not original, and to spring rather from authentic temporality, then, in accordance with the principle a potiori fit denominatio, the naming of the temporality now laid free as original time justifies itself. The naming-paragraph is the section's second summit: the three prepositional characters (zu, auf, bei) read as raptures — temporality the ekstatikon, the original outside-itself that has no inside to leave (its essence the standing-out itself, in the unity of the three) — the Greek ekstasis wrested from mysticism into structure. And the counter-image is filed with its derivation-promise: the vulgar now-line as the ecstatic leveled, itself a mode of temporalizing; the title "original time" claimed on the classical maxim: the name goes to the stronger.

The eighteenth unit ranks the ecstases: in enumerating the ecstases we have always named the future first — to indicate that the future has a priority in the ecstatic unity of original and authentic temporality, although temporality does not first arise through an accumulation and succession of the ecstases, but temporalizes itself in each case in their equiprimordiality. But within this equiprimordiality the modes of temporalizing are different, and the difference lies in this: that the temporalizing can determine itself primarily from the different ecstases. Original and authentic temporality temporalizes itself from the authentic future — in such a way that, futurally been, it first awakens the present. The primary phenomenon of original and authentic temporality is the future. The priority of the future will itself vary in accordance with the modified temporalizing of inauthentic temporality, but it will still come to appearance even in the derivative "time." The ranking-doctrine holds equiprimordiality and priority together without contradiction: no ecstasis is earlier (they temporalize as one), yet each temporalizing has a leading ecstasis — and the authentic mode leads from the future (futurally been, awakening the present: the tenth unit's formula as a hierarchy). The claim that the future's primacy survives even into vulgar time is a promissory note § 81 will honor at the now itself.

The nineteenth unit draws finitude: care is being toward death; anticipatory resoluteness we determined as authentic being toward the characterized possibility of the absolute impossibility of Dasein. In such being toward its end, Dasein exists authentically whole, as the being that it can be "thrown into death": it does not have an end at which it merely ceases, but exists finitely (existiert endlich). The authentic future — which primarily temporalizes the temporality that constitutes the sense of anticipatory resoluteness — thereby unveils itself as itself finite. But does "time" not "go on" despite the no-longer-being-there of myself? And can not boundlessly much still lie "in the future" and arrive out of it? The finitude-thesis is stated in its exact register — existiert endlich: finitude as a manner of existing, not a quantity of duration — and the obvious objection is given its full voice for the next unit's classic reply.

The twentieth unit answers it. The questions are to be affirmed — yet they contain no objection against the finitude of original temporality, because they no longer treat of it at all. The question is not what all can still happen "in a time that goes on," and what kind of letting-come-toward can be encountered "out of this time," but how the coming-toward-itself is itself, as such, originally determined. Its finitude means primarily not a ceasing, but is a character of temporalizing itself. The original and authentic future is the toward-itself — toward itself existing as the not-to-be-outstripped possibility of nullity: the ecstatic character of the original future lies precisely in this, that it closes the potentiality-of-being — that is, is itself closed — and as such makes possible the resolute existentiell understanding of nullity. The original and authentic coming-toward-itself is the sense of existing in the ownmost nullity. With the thesis of the original finitude of temporality it is not contested that "time goes on"; the thesis is only to hold fast the phenomenal character of original temporality, which shows itself in what is projected in Dasein's original existential projection. The reply is the section's dialectical jewel: the objection changes the subject — endless time is a fact about the derivative phenomenon, finitude a character of the temporalizing itself: the future finite not because it stops but because it closes (the coming-toward runs toward the possibility that ends possibility — closure as the ecstasis's own form, not its interruption). Finite time and endless time thus never meet on the same level; the quarrel dissolves into the derivation-task.

The twenty-first unit turns the tables on infinity: the temptation to overlook the finitude of the original and authentic future — or to hold it "a priori" impossible — springs from the constant crowding-forward of the vulgar understanding of time. If this rightly knows an endless time, and only this, it is not thereby proven that it already understands this time and its "infinity." What does it mean: time "goes on," "keeps passing away"? What does "in time" mean in general, and "in" and "out of the future" in particular? In what sense is "time" endless? Such things demand clarification, if the vulgar objections against the finitude of original time are not to remain groundless. But this clarification can be accomplished only if, with regard to finitude and in-finitude, an appropriate question-formulation has been won — and this springs only from the understanding look upon the original phenomenon of time. The problem cannot run: how does the "derived," infinite time, "in which" the present-at-hand arises and passes away, become the original finite temporality — but: how does inauthentic temporality spring from the finite authentic one, and how does it, as inauthentic, temporalize from the finite an in-finite time? Only because original time is finite can the "derived" temporalize itself as in-finite. In the order of understanding grasping, the finitude of time becomes fully visible only when "endless time" has been set forth, so as to be set over against it. The paragraph completes the inversion with the book's boldest founding-claim: infinity derived from finitude — endless time a temporalization of the finite (the direction of every philosophical theology reversed: not the finite as limited infinite, but the in-finite as the finite's own leveled self-prolongation) — and the vulgar concept is served notice that its own "endless" is un-understood: the questions battery (what is "in time"? in what sense endless?) is Chapter Six's docket, and the closing methodological note schedules the confrontation: finitude fully visible only against the exhibited endless time.

The twenty-second unit condenses the section into four theses: the analysis of original temporality so far we gather into the following theses — time is original as the temporalizing of temporality, as which it makes possible the constitution of the care-structure; temporality is essentially ecstatic; temporality temporalizes itself originally from the future; original time is finite. The tetralogue is the division's yield in portable form — enabling, ecstatic, futural, finite — four sentences that the rest of the book (and the century's reception) will spend itself unpacking.

The closing unit opens the verification: yet the interpretation of care as temporality cannot remain restricted to the narrow basis won so far, even though it accomplished the first steps in view of Dasein's original authentic being-whole. The thesis — the sense of Dasein's being is temporality — must confirm itself (bewähren) on the concrete stock of the exhibited basic constitution of this being. The closing sentence commissions §§ 66–71: the thesis, won at the authentic summit, must now redeem itself across the whole prior analytic — the Wiederholung as verification; temporality proves original by regenerating everything.

##### § 66. Dasein's Temporality and the Tasks, Springing from It, of a More Original Repetition of the Existential Analysis

The opening unit names the verification's double yield: the laid-free phenomenon of temporality demands not only a farther-reaching confirmation of its constitutive power; through this confirmation it itself first comes into view with regard to the basic possibilities of temporalizing. The demonstration of the possibility of Dasein's constitution of being on the ground of temporality we call, briefly though only provisionally, the "temporal" interpretation. The methodological point is the spiral once more: verification is not mere checking but deepening — only in re-generating the structures does temporality show its own modes; and the scare-quoted term "zeitliche Interpretation" is flagged as provisional, since "temporal" itself awaits its concept.

The second unit sets the first task and the rule of the repetition. The next task is, beyond the temporal analysis of the authentic potentiality-of-being-whole and a general characterization of care's temporality, to make visible the inauthenticity of Dasein in its specific temporality. Temporality showed itself first at anticipatory resoluteness — the authentic mode of that disclosedness which mostly holds itself in the inauthenticity of das Man's falling self-interpretation. The characterization of the temporality of disclosedness in general leads to the temporal understanding of the nearest concernful being-in-the-world, and therewith of Dasein's average indifference, at which the existential analytic first set in. The average mode of being in which Dasein proximally and mostly holds itself we called everydayness: through the repetition of the earlier analysis, everydayness must unveil itself in its temporal sense, so that the problematic enclosed in temporality comes to light and the apparent "self-evidence" of the preparatory analyses vanishes completely. Temporality is indeed to confirm itself on all essential structures of Dasein's basic constitution; yet this does not lead to an external, schematic running-through of the accomplished analyses in their presented sequence. The differently directed course of the temporal analysis is to make the connection of the earlier considerations more distinct and to lift their contingency and apparent arbitrariness; beyond these methodical necessities, however, motives lying in the phenomenon itself make themselves felt, which compel a different articulation of the repeating analysis. The unit legislates for Chapters Four and Five: the Wiederholung is no re-run — its order will differ from Division One's because temporality's own articulation, not the exposition's history, now commands; and the promised gain is retrospective necessity: what looked like the preparatory analysis's contingent sequence will show itself grounded.

The third unit derives the second task: historicity. The ontological structure of the being that I in each case am centers in the self-standing of existence. Because the self can be conceived neither as substance nor as subject, but grounds in existence, the analysis of the inauthentic self, das Man, was left entirely in the train of the preparatory interpretation. Now that selfhood has been expressly taken back into the structure of care, and therewith of temporality, the temporal interpretation of self-constancy and non-self-constancy receives an own weight, needing separate thematic execution. It not only first provides the right securing against the paralogisms and the ontologically inappropriate questions about the being of the I in general; it procures at the same time, corresponding to its central function, a more original insight into the temporalizing-structure of temporality — which unveils itself as the historicity (Geschichtlichkeit) of Dasein. The sentence "Dasein is historical" confirms itself as a fundamental existential-ontological assertion, far removed from the merely ontic ascertainment that Dasein occurs in a "world-history"; Dasein's historicity, however, is the ground of a possible historical understanding, which in its turn carries with it the possibility of an expressly seized development of historiography as a science. The derivation is the book's boldest forward link: the temporal question of the self's constancy — how a self stands and stretches along — is the question of history; Geschichtlichkeit announced as temporality's own deepened self-showing, with the three-tier order (historicity, historical understanding, the science of history) that Chapter Five will unfold; Dilthey's problem inherited and re-grounded in one paragraph.

The fourth unit derives the third task: within-time-ness. The temporal interpretation of everydayness and historicity steadies the view upon original time sufficiently to uncover it itself as the condition of the possibility and necessity of the everyday experience of time. Dasein expends itself (verwendet sich), as the being for which its being is at issue, primarily for itself — expressly or not. Proximally and mostly, care is circumspect concern; expending itself for the sake of itself, Dasein "uses itself up" (verbraucht sich). Using itself up, Dasein uses itself — that is, its time; using time, it reckons with it. Circumspect-reckoning concern first discovers time and leads to the development of a time-reckoning. Reckoning with time is constitutive for being-in-the-world: the concernful discovering of circumspection, reckoning with its time, lets the discovered ready-to-hand and present-at-hand be encountered in time — innerworldly beings become accessible as "being in time." This time-determinateness of innerworldly beings we call within-time-ness (Innerzeitigkeit). The "time" found at first ontically in it becomes the basis of the formation of the vulgar and traditional concept of time. But time as within-time-ness springs from an essential temporalizing-mode of original temporality: this origin says that the time "in which" the present-at-hand arises and passes away is a genuine time-phenomenon — no externalization of a "qualitative time" into space, as Bergson's ontologically wholly indeterminate and insufficient interpretation of time would have one believe. The paragraph is Chapter Six in embryo, and the little chain at its heart is the finest genetic argument in the book: caring for its being, Dasein spends itself; spending itself, it spends its time; spending time, it counts it — clock-time derived from care's self-expenditure in four verbs. The Innerzeitigkeit-coinage names the deposit, and the defense-clause is double-edged: the vulgar time genuine (against every dismissal — the clock is no illusion) yet derivative; Bergson, the era's great time-philosopher, dispatched in a subordinate clause — his spatialization-thesis refused because it concedes too much: common time is not degraded quality but leveled ecstasy.

The closing unit confesses the incompleteness and schedules the deeper repetition. The working-out of Dasein's temporality as everydayness, historicity, and within-time-ness first gives the ruthless insight into the entanglements of an original ontology of Dasein. As being-in-the-world, Dasein exists factically with and alongside innerworldly encountered beings; its being therefore receives its comprehensive ontological transparency only in the horizon of the clarified being of non-Dasein-like beings — which includes also what, neither ready-to-hand nor present-at-hand, only "subsists." The interpretation of the variations of the being of all that of which we say "it is," however, needs a beforehand sufficiently illuminated idea of being in general. So long as this is not won, the repeating temporal analysis of Dasein too remains incomplete and afflicted with obscurities — not to speak at length of the substantive difficulties. The existential-temporal analysis of Dasein demands, for its part, a renewed repetition within the frame of the fundamental discussion of the concept of being. The confession is structural, not modest: the temporal analytic runs inside a horizon (the idea of being) it cannot yet supply — so even Division Two is provisional, and a second repetition is scheduled inside the never-written Division Three; the book here openly declares its own torso-form two hundred pages before breaking off.

#### Chapter Four: Temporality and Everydayness

##### § 67. The Basic Stock of Dasein's Existential Constitution and the Predelineation of Its Temporal Interpretation

The opening unit defends the manifold — and drops the book's most vertiginous aside. The preparatory analysis made accessible a manifold of phenomena which, for all concentration on the founding structural totality of care, must not vanish from the phenomenological view. The original totality of Dasein's constitution, as articulated, so little excludes such a manifold that it demands it: originality of the constitution of being does not coincide with the simplicity and singleness of an ultimate building-element. The ontological origin of Dasein's being is not "less" than what springs from it — it towers over it in advance in power; and all "springing-from" in the ontological field is degeneration. The ontological penetration to the "origin" arrives not at ontic self-evidences for "common sense"; to it opens precisely the question-worthiness of everything self-evident. The paragraph guards the repetition against reductionism (temporality will not dissolve the phenomena into a simple element — origin is not an atom) and then, in one sentence, states a whole metaphysics of ground: alles »Entspringen« im ontologischen Felde ist Degeneration — derivation as decline, the origin mightier than the derived — the anti-constructivist axiom that governs every derivation in the book (assertion from interpretation, presence from readiness, now-time from temporality), and the closing epigram gives ontology its ethos: not the confirmation of the obvious but the opening of its questionability.

The second unit retraces the way: to bring the phenomena won in the preparatory analysis back into the phenomenological view, a reference to its traversed stages must suffice. The delimitation of care resulted from the analysis of the disclosedness that constitutes the being of the "Da"; the clarification of this phenomenon meant the provisional interpretation of being-in-the-world. The investigation began with its characterization, to secure from the outset, against the inappropriate — mostly unexpress — ontological pre-determinations of Dasein, a sufficient phenomenal horizon. Being-in-the-world was first characterized in view of the phenomenon of world: the explication proceeded from the ontic-ontological characterization of the ready-to-hand and present-at-hand "in" the environment to the setting-off of innerworldliness, so as to make visible at it the phenomenon of worldhood in general. But the structure of worldhood, significance, proved itself clasped together with that upon which the understanding essentially belonging to disclosedness projects itself — with Dasein's potentiality-of-being, for the sake of which it exists. The retrospect compresses Division One's Chapters Two and Three into their single arc (things, innerworldliness, worldhood, significance, Worumwillen) — the itinerary the temporal repetition must now re-travel with time as its thread.

The third unit gives the chapter its order: the temporal interpretation of everyday Dasein is to begin with the structures in which disclosedness constitutes itself — understanding, disposedness, falling, and discourse. The modes of temporalizing to be laid free in view of these phenomena give the ground for determining the temporality of being-in-the-world; this leads anew to the phenomenon of world and permits a delimitation of the specifically temporal problematic of worldhood, which must confirm itself through the characterization of the nearest everyday being-in-the-world — falling, circumspect concern. Its temporality makes possible the modification of circumspection into onlooking perceiving and the theoretical cognition grounding therein. The temporality of being-in-the-world thus emerging proves itself at the same time the foundation of Dasein's specific spatiality: the temporal constitution of de-severance and directionality is to be shown. The whole of these analyses unveils a possibility of temporalizing in which Dasein's inauthenticity ontologically grounds, and leads before the question how the temporal character of everydayness — the temporal sense of the constantly used "proximally and mostly" — is to be understood; the fixing of this problem makes plain that and how far the clarification of the phenomenon reached by then does not suffice. The program repeats Division One's order inside the new register — disclosedness, world, concern, theory, space — with two promissory notes flagged: the genesis of theory (§ 69b, the book's sole account of science's birth) and the honest ending: § 71 will fix "everydayness" as a problem that exceeds the chapter.

The closing unit tables it: the present chapter accordingly receives the following articulation — the temporality of disclosedness in general (§ 68); the temporality of being-in-the-world and the problem of the transcendence of the world (§ 69); the temporality of Dasein-like spatiality (§ 70); the temporal sense of Dasein's everydayness (§ 71). The four-station table sets the chapter's frame; § 68 opens immediately.

##### § 68. The Temporality of Disclosedness in General

The opening unit sets the fourfold task: resoluteness, characterized with regard to its temporal sense, represents an authentic disclosedness of Dasein — that disclosedness which constitutes a being in such a way that, existing, it can itself be its "Da." Care was characterized, with regard to its temporal sense, only in its basic traits; to exhibit its concrete temporal constitution means to interpret temporally, in detail, its structural moments — understanding, disposedness, falling, and discourse. Every understanding has its mood; every disposedness is understanding; the disposed understanding has the character of falling; the falling attuned understanding articulates itself, with regard to its intelligibility, in discourse. The respective temporal constitution of the named phenomena leads back in each case to the one temporality, as which it vouches for the possible structural unity of understanding, disposedness, falling, and discourse. The section-plan is Chapter Five of Division One re-opened with its interlocking restated (each moment qualifying all the others — the four-way equiprimordiality) and the target named: one temporality beneath the four, the unity demonstrated by re-derivation.

###### a) The Temporality of Understanding

The opening unit re-fixes the existential: with the term understanding we mean a fundamental existential — neither a determinate kind of cognition, distinguished say from explaining and conceiving, nor cognition at all in the sense of thematic apprehension. Understanding constitutes the being of the Da in such a way that, on its ground, a Dasein can existingly develop the various possibilities of sight, of looking-around, of merely looking-at; all explaining, as understanding discovery of the unintelligible, roots in Dasein's primary understanding. The guard repeats § 31's against the epistemic reading — with the Dilthey-quarrel (Verstehen vs. Erklären) expressly transcended: both are founded developments of the one existential.

The second unit derives its future. Originally existentially grasped, understanding means: projecting-being toward a potentiality-of-being for the sake of which Dasein in each case exists. Understanding discloses one's own potentiality in such a way that Dasein, understanding, in each case somehow knows what it is at with itself — a "knowing" that is no having-discovered a fact, but the holding-oneself in an existentiell possibility; the corresponding not-knowing is not an omission of understanding but a deficient mode of the projectedness of the potentiality-of-being. Existence can be questionable; for the "standing-in-question" to be possible, a disclosedness is needed. Underlying the projecting self-understanding in an existentiell possibility is the future, as coming-toward-itself out of the current possibility as which Dasein in each case exists. The future makes ontologically possible a being that is such that, understanding, it exists in its potentiality-of-being. The projecting that is at bottom futural does not primarily grasp the projected possibility thematically in an opining, but throws itself into it as possibility; understanding, Dasein in each case is as it can be. Resoluteness resulted as original and authentic existing; proximally and mostly, of course, Dasein remains irresolute — closed off in its ownmost potentiality, to which it brings itself only in individuation. Therein lies: temporality does not constantly temporalize itself from the authentic future. But this inconstancy does not mean temporality sometimes lacks the future; it means: its temporalizing is variable. The derivation banks § 65's seventh unit at the level of the existential (understanding = future: the projection is the coming-toward), keeps § 31's anti-thematic clause, and converts the everyday facts into modal doctrine: irresoluteness is not futurelessness — the future never absent, only differently temporalized; variability, not privation, the key to the inauthentic.

The third unit fixes the terminology: for the terminological characterization of the authentic future we hold fast the expression anticipation (Vorlaufen); it indicates that Dasein, existing authentically, lets itself come toward itself as its ownmost potentiality — that the future must first win itself, not out of a present, but out of the inauthentic future. The formally indifferent term for the future lies in the designation of care's first structural moment: the ahead-of-itself. Dasein is factically constantly ahead-of-itself, but inconstantly — according to the existentiell possibility — anticipating. The three-tier lexicon (Sich-vorweg the indifferent structure; Vorlaufen its authentic mode; the inauthentic mode to be named next) is the pattern each ecstasis will receive; and the middle clause carries a fine doctrine: the authentic future is won from the inauthentic, not from the present — modification, never creation.

The fourth unit names the inauthentic future: awaiting. How is the inauthentic future to be set off? This ecstatic mode can unveil itself — as the authentic future did at resoluteness — only in the ontological return from everyday concernful, inauthentic understanding to its existential-temporal sense. As care, Dasein is essentially ahead-of-itself; proximally and mostly, concernful being-in-the-world understands itself from what it attends to. Inauthentic understanding projects itself upon the attendable, the feasible, urgent, unavoidable business of everyday occupation. But the attended is what it is for the sake of the caring potentiality-of-being: this lets Dasein, in concernful being alongside the attended, come toward itself. Dasein does not come toward itself primarily in its ownmost, non-relational potentiality; rather, attending, it is awaiting of itself (seiner gewärtig) from that which the attended yields or refuses. Dasein comes toward itself from the attended. The inauthentic future has the character of awaiting (Gewärtigen). The concernful self-understanding of the they-self, from what one pursues, has in this ecstatic mode of the future the "ground" of its possibility. And only because factical Dasein is thus awaiting of its potentiality from the attended can it expect and wait for...: the awaiting must in each case already have disclosed the horizon and circuit out of which something can be expected. Expecting is a mode of the future founded in awaiting, which temporalizes itself authentically as anticipation; hence in anticipation lies a more original being toward death than in the concernful expecting of it. The analysis is exquisite in its economy: the everyday future as a coming-toward-oneself from the things — I await myself from what the day's business yields or denies (success and failure as the self's messengers) — Gewärtigen minted for it; and § 53's expectation-refusal receives its ground at last: Erwarten is founded in Gewärtigen, twice removed from Vorlaufen — the deathbed calculus a second-order mode of the shop's own future.

The fifth unit brings in the present and mints the Augenblick. Understanding, as existing in the however-projected potentiality-of-being, is primarily futural; but it would not temporalize itself were it not temporal — equiprimordially determined by beenness and present. Everyday concern understands itself from the potentiality that comes toward it from possible success and failure with regard to what is attended; to the inauthentic future (awaiting) corresponds an own being alongside the attended. The ecstatic mode of this present unveils itself when we adduce for comparison this ecstasis in the mode of authentic temporality: to the anticipation of resoluteness belongs a present in accordance with which a resolution discloses the situation. In resoluteness the present is not only fetched back out of the dispersion into the nearest-attended; it is held in the future and beenness. The present held in authentic temporality — hence authentic present — we call the moment of vision (der Augenblick). This term must be understood in the active sense, as ecstasis: it means the resolute rapture (Entrückung) of Dasein — yet held in resoluteness — to what is encountered in the situation of attendable possibilities and circumstances. The phenomenon of the Augenblick can in principle not be clarified from the now. The now is a temporal phenomenon belonging to time as within-time-ness: the now "in which" something arises, passes away, or is present-at-hand. "In the moment of vision" nothing can occur; rather, as authentic present, it first lets encounter what, as ready-to-hand or present-at-hand, can be "in a time." The folded-in note settles with Kierkegaard: he saw the existentiell phenomenon of the Augenblick most penetratingly of all — which does not already mean that the existential interpretation correspondingly succeeded for him; he remains stuck to the vulgar concept of time and determines the moment with the help of the now and eternity. When Kierkegaard speaks of "temporality," he means man's "being-in-time"; time as within-time-ness knows only the now, never a moment of vision. But if the moment is experienced existentielly, a more original temporality is presupposed, though existentially unexpress. (On the "moment," the note adds, compare Jaspers' Psychology of Worldviews and its Kierkegaard-report.) The paragraph is § 65's fifteenth unit made concrete, and every determination is weighed: the Augenblick active (an ecstasis, a deed of rapture — not a point suffered), held (in future and beenness — against curiosity's unheld leaping, and against every mysticism of the instant), and categorially severed from the now: in it nothing occurs, through it beings encounter — the moment is not in time; time's contents are met from it. The Kierkegaard-note is the book's most exact settlement with its nearest creditor: the discovery honored as supreme (am eindringlichsten), the concept convicted — the Øieblikket defined by now-plus-eternity, hence inside vulgar time; the existentiell experience presupposing the original temporality its own theory lacked; the debt acknowledged and the deed re-founded.

The sixth unit completes the present's lexicon: in distinction from the moment of vision as authentic present, we call the inauthentic making-present (das Gegenwärtigen). Formally understood, every present is making-present, but not every present is "momentary" (augenblicklich); when we use the expression making-present without addition, the inauthentic, moment-less-irresolute one is always meant. Making-present will become plain only from the temporal interpretation of falling at the attended "world," which has in it its existential sense; but insofar as inauthentic understanding projects the potentiality-of-being from the attendable, this means: it temporalizes itself from making-present. The moment of vision, by contrast, temporalizes itself conversely, from the authentic future. The bookkeeping fixes the deep asymmetry in one antithesis: inauthentic understanding led by its present (the projection drawn from what presence offers), the authentic present led by its future (released, held) — the direction of temporalizing as the whole difference between the modes.

The seventh unit derives the everyday past: forgetting. Inauthentic understanding temporalizes itself as making-present awaiting, to whose ecstatic unity a corresponding beenness must belong. The authentic coming-toward-itself of anticipatory resoluteness is at once a coming-back upon the ownmost self, thrown into its individuation; this ecstasis makes it possible for Dasein to take over, resolved, the being that it already is. In anticipation, Dasein retrieves itself forward (holt sich... vor) into its ownmost potentiality-of-being. Authentic having-been we call retrieval — repetition (die Wiederholung). But the inauthentic self-projection upon the possibilities drawn from the attended, in making it present, is possible only in that Dasein has forgotten itself in its ownmost thrown potentiality-of-being. This forgetting is not nothing, nor merely the lack of memory: it is an own, "positive" ecstatic mode of beenness. The ecstasis (rapture) of forgetting has the character of a backing-away before the ownmost been, closed off to itself — in such a way that this backing-away before... ecstatically closes the before-which and, in one therewith, itself. Forgottenness (Vergessenheit), as inauthentic beenness, relates itself hereby to one's thrown, own being: it is the temporal sense of the mode of being according to which I proximally and mostly am-been. And only on the ground of this forgetting can the attending, awaiting making-present retain (behalten) — retain, namely, the non-Dasein-like, environmentally encountered beings; to this retaining corresponds a non-retaining, which presents a "forgetting" in the derived sense. The paragraph mints two of the book's great counter-concepts in one breath. Wiederholung — repetition, retrieval — named as the authentic beenness (the § 62 self-repetition of resolve now given its ecstatic seat: the been taken over forward); and Vergessen elevated from psychology to ontology: the primary forgetting is self-forgetting, an ecstatic backing-away that closes both its object and itself (forgetting that it forgets — the perfect crime of everydayness), the ground on which alone the practical memory of things (Behalten) and its lapses (ordinary forgetting) become possible. Memory of the world founded on oblivion of the self.

The eighth unit completes the founding-order and totals the mode: as expectation is possible only on the ground of awaiting, so remembering (Erinnerung) on the ground of forgetting — and not conversely: for in the mode of forgottenness, beenness primarily "discloses" the horizon into which Dasein, lost to the "externality" of the attended, can remember itself. The forgetting-making-present awaiting is an own ecstatic unity, in accordance with which inauthentic understanding temporalizes itself with regard to its temporality; the unity of these ecstases closes off the authentic potentiality-of-being and is thus the existential condition of the possibility of irresoluteness. Though inauthentic concernful understanding determines itself from the making-present of the attended, the temporalizing of understanding accomplishes itself nevertheless primarily in the future. The closing formula — vergessend-gegenwärtigendes Gewärtigen, the forgetting-presenting awaiting — is everydayness's temporal signature, the exact counter-figure to the gewesend-gegenwärtigende Zukunft of § 65; and the two theorems flanking it are precisely weighed: remembering founded on forgetting (recollection a local recovery inside a standing oblivion — Plato's anamnesis inverted into existential analysis), and even this fallen mode still future-led: the primacy of the future holding, as § 65 predicted, into inauthenticity itself.

###### b) The Temporality of Disposedness

The opening unit re-anchors mood in the throw: understanding is never free-floating but always disposed; the Da is in each case equiprimordially disclosed — or closed — by mood. Attunement brings Dasein before its thrownness, and precisely not in such a way that this is cognized as such, but — far more originally — disclosed in "how one is." Being-thrown means existentially: finding-oneself thus or thus. Disposedness therefore grounds in thrownness; mood represents the way in which I in each case primarily am the thrown being. How can the temporal constitution of attunement be made visible — how, from the ecstatic unity of the respective temporality, does the existential connection between disposedness and understanding become intelligible? The recapitulation of § 29 is exact (mood beneath cognition; the wie einem ist as the throw's primary disclosure), and the question posed is the subsection's real quarry: not dating moods but grounding them.

The second unit states the thesis: mood discloses in the manner of turning-toward and turning-away from one's own Dasein. The bringing before the That of one's own thrownness — whether authentically unveiling or inauthentically covering — becomes existentially possible only if Dasein's being, by its sense, constantly is-been. The bringing before the thrown being that one is does not first create the been; its ecstasis first makes possible the finding-oneself in the manner of disposedness. Understanding grounds primarily in the future; disposedness, by contrast, temporalizes itself primarily in beenness. Mood temporalizes itself — that is, its specific ecstasis belongs to a future and a present, yet in such a way that beenness modifies these equiprimordial ecstases. The thesis-sentence pairs with a)'s: the second existential assigned its ecstasis — mood as the beenness-led temporalizing — with the constant rule kept (all three ecstases in every mood; one leads); and the anti-constructivist clause repeated: the bringing-before does not make the been — attunement reveals the perfect tense it presupposes.

The third unit sets the method's limits. We stressed that moods are ontically familiar but not recognized in their original existential function: they count as fleeting lived experiences that "color" the whole "state of the soul." What for an observing has the character of fleeting surfacing and vanishing belongs to the original constancy of existence. But nevertheless — what should moods have in common with "time"? That these "experiences" come and go, run off "in time," is a trivial ascertainment — certainly, and an ontic-psychological one. The task, however, is to exhibit the ontological structure of attunement in its existential-temporal constitution; and at first it can only be a matter of making the temporality of mood visible at all. The thesis "disposedness grounds primarily in beenness" means: the existential basic character of mood is a bringing-back upon... (Zurückbringen auf), which does not first produce the been, but disposedness reveals, for the existential analysis, in each case a mode of beenness. The temporal interpretation therefore cannot intend to deduce moods from temporality and dissolve them into pure phenomena of temporalizing: it is merely to be demonstrated that moods, in what they existentielly "signify" and how, are not possible except on the ground of temporality. The temporal interpretation restricts itself to the preparatorily analyzed phenomena of fear and anxiety. The methodological paragraph does triple guard-duty: against the Erlebnis-psychology (the "fleeting" mood belonging in truth to existence's constancy), against the trivial reading of the thesis (moods "in time" — conceded and dismissed as ontic), and against deductivism (no derivation of moods from time — § 67's anti-reduction axiom applied): the claim is enabling-ground, not generative source.

The fourth unit runs fear — and finds forgetting at its heart. We begin with the exhibition of the temporality of fear, characterized as inauthentic disposedness. How far is beenness the existential sense making it possible — which mode of this ecstasis marks fear's specific temporality? Fear is fearing before something threatening which, detrimental to Dasein's factical potentiality-of-being, nears in the described way within the circuit of the attended ready-to-hand and present-at-hand; fearing discloses, in the manner of everyday circumspection, something threatening — a merely intuiting subject could never discover such a thing. But is this disclosing of fearing-before not a letting-come-toward-oneself; has one not rightly determined fear as expectation of an oncoming evil (malum futurum)? Is fear's primary temporal sense not the future, and nothing less than beenness? Incontestably, fearing not only "relates" to the "future" in the signification of what first arrives "in time"; this self-relating is itself futural in the originally temporal sense — an awaiting manifestly co-belongs to fear's existential-temporal constitution. But this says at first only that fear's temporality is inauthentic. Is fearing-before only an expecting of an oncoming threat? Expecting an oncoming threat need not already be fear — and is so far from it that precisely the specific mood-character of fear is missing from it. This lies in that fear's awaiting lets the threatening come back upon the factically concernful potentiality-of-being. Back upon the being that I am, the threatening can be awaited — and Dasein thereby threatened — only if the whereupon of the back-upon... is at all already ecstatically open. That the fearing awaiting fears "itself" — that fearing-before is in each case a fearing-about — therein lies the mood- and affect-character of fear: its existential-temporal sense is constituted by a self-forgetting (Sichvergessen) — the confused backing-away before one's own factical potentiality-of-being, as which the threatened being-in-the-world attends to the ready-to-hand. Aristotle rightly determines fear as lypē tis ē tarachē — a depression or confusion. The depression forces Dasein back upon its thrownness, yet so that this is precisely closed off; the confusion grounds in a forgetting. The forgetting backing-away before a factical, resolved potentiality holds itself to the possibilities of self-rescue and evasion already circumspectly discovered beforehand: fearing concern, because forgetting itself and therefore seizing no determinate possibility, leaps from the nearest to the next — all "possible," even impossible, possibilities offer themselves; the fearful one halts at none. The "environment" does not vanish, but is encountered in a no-longer-knowing-one's-way in it: to the self-forgetting in fear belongs this confused making-present of the nearest-best. That, for example, the inhabitants of a burning house often "save" the most indifferent, nearest-to-hand thing, is familiar. The self-forgotten making-present of a tangle of hovering possibilities makes possible the confusion that constitutes fear's mood-character; the forgottenness of the confusion modifies also the awaiting, characterizing it as depressed or confused awaiting, distinct from a pure expecting. The analysis is the subsection's masterpiece, and its dialectic is exact. The classical definition (expectatio mali futuri — from Aristotle through the Stoics to the moderns) is granted its future and shown superficial: expectation without the recoil is not fear; the mood begins where the threat comes back upon me — and that return runs through beenness (only a being ecstatically open to what it was can be reached at what it is). And the mode of that beenness is forgetting: fear as self-forgetting confusion — the leaping among all-and-any possibilities, the burning-house vignette (the book's most homely and most terrible example) certifying it phenomenally: panic saves the pillow because the self is forgotten, and with it every order of mattering. Aristotle's tarachē re-derived as the temporal confusion of an oblivious present.

The fifth unit totals fear's formula: the specific ecstatic unity that existentially makes possible self-fearing temporalizes itself primarily from the characterized forgetting, which, as a mode of beenness, modifies the belonging present and future in their temporalizing. Fear's temporality is an awaiting-making-present forgetting (gewärtigend-gegenwärtigendes Vergessen). At first, the common-sense exegesis of fear, in accordance with its orientation to the innerworldly encountered, seeks to determine the before-which as the "oncoming evil" and, correspondingly, the relation to it as expectation; what belongs to the phenomenon beyond that remains a "feeling of pleasure or displeasure." The formula inverts a)'s everyday signature (there: forgetting-presenting awaiting; here: awaiting-presenting forgetting — the lead ecstasis switched to the been) — and the closing jab files the tradition's residue: whatever the expectation-theory cannot place, it books as hedonic tone; the mood-character shredded into affect-psychology.

The sixth unit turns to anxiety and re-fixes its object. How does anxiety's temporality relate to fear's? We called the phenomenon a basic disposedness: it brings Dasein before its ownmost thrownness and unveils the uncanniness of the everyday familiar being-in-the-world. Anxiety, like fear, is formally determined by a before-which and an about-which of the anxious self — but the analysis showed that the two coincide. This is not to say the structural characters melt together, as if anxiety were anxious neither before... nor about...: that before-which and about-which coincide means the being fulfilling them is the same — Dasein. In particular, the before-which does not encounter as something determinate attendable; the threat comes not from the ready-to-hand and present-at-hand, but precisely from this: that everything ready-to-hand and present-at-hand absolutely no longer "says" anything to one. With environmental beings there is no longer any involvement. The world in which I exist has sunk to insignificance, and the world so disclosed can free only beings with the character of non-involvement. The nothing of the world, before which anxiety is anxious, does not mean an absence of the innerworldly present-at-hand were experienced in anxiety; it must precisely be encountered, so that there can be so utterly no involvement with it and it can show itself in an empty mercilessness. Therein lies: the concernful awaiting finds nothing from which it could understand itself — it gropes into the nothing of the world; but, thrust upon the world, understanding is brought by anxiety before being-in-the-world as such — and this before-which is at once anxiety's about-which. The self-anxiety before... has neither the character of an expectation nor of an awaiting at all: the before-which is indeed already "there" — Dasein itself. Is anxiety then not constituted by a future? Certainly — yet not by the inauthentic future of awaiting.
