The paragraph re-runs § 40 in the temporal key with one new word of terrible exactness — leere Erbarmungslosigkeit, the empty mercilessness in which things stand when involvement fails — and draws the decisive temporal cut: anxiety has no awaiting, for nothing is oncoming; what it is "before" is already there. Its future must therefore be of another kind.

The seventh unit finds anxiety's beenness: repeatability. The insignificance of the world disclosed in anxiety unveils the nullity of the attendable — the impossibility of projecting oneself upon a potentiality-of-being primarily founded in the attended. But the unveiling of this impossibility means a letting-flash-up (Aufleuchten-lassen) of the possibility of an authentic potentiality-of-being. What temporal sense has this unveiling? Anxiety is anxious about naked Dasein as thrown into uncanniness; it brings back upon the pure That of the ownmost, individualized thrownness. This bringing-back has neither the character of evasive forgetting nor of remembering; just as little does there lie in anxiety already a repeating taking-over of existence into the resolution. But anxiety does bring back upon thrownness as possibly retrievable (als mögliche wiederholbare) — and in this way it co-unveils the possibility of an authentic potentiality-of-being, which, in retrieval, must, as futural, come back upon the thrown Da. Bringing before the retrievability (Wiederholbarkeit) is the specific ecstatic mode of the beenness constituting the disposedness of anxiety. The derivation places anxiety with jeweler's precision between the modes: not forgetting (no evasion), not remembering (no episode recalled), not yet repetition (no resolve taken) — but the bringing-before-retrievability: the throw shown as takeable, the past lit up as possibility; anxiety as the hinge-mood on which beenness can turn from Vergessenheit toward Wiederholung — and the Aufleuchten-clause pays § 40's deposit: the disclosure of freedom, now dated in the ecstases.

The eighth unit contrasts the presents: the forgetting constitutive for fear confuses Dasein and lets it drift back and forth among unseized "worldly" possibilities; over against this unheld making-present, the present of anxiety is held (gehalten) in the bringing-back upon the ownmost thrownness. By its existential sense, anxiety cannot lose itself at something attendable — if the like happens in a disposedness similar to it, it is fear, which everyday understanding throws together with anxiety. But though anxiety's present is held, it does not yet have the character of the moment of vision, which temporalizes itself in the resolution: anxiety only brings into the mood of a possible resolution. Its present holds the Augenblick — as which it alone is possible — on the leap (auf dem Sprung). The contrast completes the mood-pair's temporal portrait (fear's tumbling present, anxiety's held one) and ends on the book's most coiled image: anxiety's present holds the moment of vision poised, on the spring — the Augenblick not yet leapt but cocked; anxiety as readiness's mood (§ 60's Bereitschaft zur Angst given its temporal figure).

The ninth unit grounds anxiety's power: at the peculiar temporality of anxiety — that it grounds originally in beenness, and future and present first temporalize themselves out of it — the possibility of that mightiness (Mächtigkeit) is shown by which the mood of anxiety distinguishes itself. In it Dasein is taken back completely upon its naked uncanniness and benumbed (benommen) by it; but this benumbedness not only takes Dasein back out of the "worldly" possibilities — it gives it at the same time the possibility of an authentic potentiality-of-being. The unit explains the phenomenological privilege § 40 claimed for anxiety: its power is its temporal shape — the been leading, so that the whole of existence is drawn back to its ground and, exactly there, freed; seizure and gift one movement.

The tenth unit orders the two moods' origins: both moods, fear and anxiety, never "occur" merely isolated "in the stream of experience"; each attunes an understanding, or determines itself out of one. Fear has its occasion in the environmentally attended; anxiety, by contrast, springs from Dasein itself. Fear assails from the innerworldly; anxiety rises out of being-in-the-world as thrown being toward death. This "climbing-up" of anxiety out of Dasein means, temporally understood: anxiety's future and present temporalize themselves out of an original being-been, in the sense of the bringing-back upon retrievability. But authentically, anxiety can rise only in a resolute Dasein. The resolute one knows no fear, but understands precisely the possibility of anxiety as the mood that does not hinder and confuse him: it frees from "null" possibilities and lets one become free for authentic ones. The paragraph seals the pair with the doctrine everydayness inverts (fear from the world, anxiety from existence — assault versus ascent) and closes on the resolute one's economy of moods: fearless not from hardness but because the confusion-mood has no purchase where the self is not forgotten; anxiety kept, welcomed even, as the liberating attunement — § 62's nüchterne Angst confirmed in the ecstatic register.

The eleventh unit extends the thesis across the mood-spectrum. But does the thesis of the temporality of moods perhaps hold only of the phenomena selected for the analysis? How is a temporal sense to be found in the pallid untunedness that rules through the "gray everyday"? And how does it stand with the temporality of moods and affects like hope, joy, enthusiasm, cheerfulness? That not only fear and anxiety are existentially founded in a beenness, but other moods too, becomes plain if we merely name phenomena like satiety, sadness, melancholy, despair — though their interpretation must be placed on the broader basis of a worked-out existential anthropology. Yet even a phenomenon like hope, which seems wholly founded in the future, must be analyzed correspondingly to fear. One has characterized hope, in distinction from fear, which relates to a malum futurum, as expectation of a bonum futurum; but decisive for the phenomenon's structure is not so much the "futural" character of that to which hope relates, as rather the existential sense of hoping itself. The mood-character lies, here too, primarily in hoping as hoping-for-oneself (Für-sich-erhoffen): the one who hopes takes himself, as it were, along into the hope and brings himself toward the hoped-for. But that presupposes a having-won-oneself. That hope relieves, over against the depressing anxiousness, says only that this disposedness too remains related, in the mode of being-been, to the burden. Elevated — better: elevating — mood is ontologically possible only in an ecstatic-temporal relation of Dasein to the thrown ground of itself. The paragraph is the book's sole page on the bright moods, and its argument is a small classic: hope's apparent future-foundation dissolved by the same move that dissolved fear's — the object's tense is not the mood's sense; hoping is a self-hoping, carrying the hoper toward the hoped, which presupposes the self already won (a having-been owned) — and relief itself testifies to the burden it lifts: even elation is a relation to the throw. Gehobene, besser hebende Stimmung — the participial correction doing the phenomenology: the lifting, not the lifted, is the mood.

The twelfth unit reads the gray: the pallid untunedness of indifference, finally — which hangs on nothing and presses toward nothing, abandoning itself to what each day brings, and yet in a certain way takes everything along — demonstrates most penetratingly the power of forgetting in the everyday moods of nearest concern. The living-along (Dahinleben) that "lets" everything "be" as it is grounds in a forgetting self-abandonment to thrownness; it has the ecstatic sense of an inauthentic beenness. Indifference — which can go together with a headlong busy-ness — is to be sharply severed from equanimity (Gleichmut): this mood springs from resoluteness, which is momentary (augenblicklich) toward the possible situations of the potentiality-of-being-whole disclosed in the anticipation of death. The unit answers the eleventh's opening question at its hardest case: the mood that seems to be no mood — the gray drift — is forgetting at full power, unattached and omnivorous at once; and the closing severance is an ethical stroke of the first order: Gleichgültigkeit and Gleichmut, indistinguishable to the observer's eye (both calm), sundered by their temporalizing — the drifter's letting-be from oblivion, the resolute one's equanimity from the anticipated whole; serenity's two sources, one fallen, one won.

The closing unit draws the boundary of affection: only a being that, by the sense of its being, is disposed — that is, existing, in each case already is-been and exists in a constant mode of beenness — can be affected (affiziert werden). Affection ontologically presupposes making-present — such, namely, that in it Dasein can be brought back upon itself as been. How stimulus and stirring of the senses in a merely-living thing are to be ontologically delimited — how and where the being of animals, for example, is constituted by a "time" — remains a problem for itself (ein Problem für sich). The subsection ends by grounding receptivity itself: affectability requires the ecstatic been (only what is its past can be touched in its present) — Kant's Affektion given its existential condition — and then the honest fence: animal time, the mere-living's sensibility, expressly reserved (the problem the 1929/30 lectures would take up under Benommenheit); the privative method's limit marked at the creature.

###### c) The Temporality of Falling

The opening unit assigns the third ecstasis and narrows the theme: the temporal interpretation of understanding and disposedness struck not only upon a primary ecstasis for the respective phenomenon, but always at the same time upon the whole of temporality. As the future primarily makes understanding possible, and beenness mood, so the third constitutive structural moment of care — falling — has its existential sense in the present. The preparatory analysis of falling began with an interpretation of idle talk, curiosity, and ambiguity; the temporal analysis is to take the same course. We restrict the investigation, however, to a consideration of curiosity, because at it the specific temporality of falling is most easily seen; the analysis of idle talk and ambiguity, by contrast, already presupposes the clarification of the temporal constitution of discourse and interpretation. The assignment completes the triad (falling = present) with the whole-clause repeated as constant guard, and the restriction is methodical honesty: curiosity, the seeing-mode, wears its present openly; talk and ambiguity wait upon d).

The second unit derives curiosity's temporal engine. Curiosity is a distinguished tendency-of-being of Dasein, in accordance with which it attends to an ability-to-see; "seeing," like the concept of sight, is not restricted to perceiving through the "bodily eyes." Perceiving in the wider sense lets the ready-to-hand and present-at-hand encounter "in person" (leibhaftig) with regard to their outward look. This letting-encounter grounds in a present, which gives at all the ecstatic horizon within which beings can be bodily present. Curiosity, however, makes the present-at-hand present not in order to understand it, tarrying alongside it; it seeks to see only in order to see and to have seen. As this making-present entangled in itself, curiosity stands in an ecstatic unity with a corresponding future and beenness. The greed for the new is indeed a pressing-forward to a not-yet-seen, but in such a way that the making-present seeks to withdraw itself from the awaiting. Curiosity is utterly inauthentically futural — and this again in such a way that it does not await a possibility but, in its greed, craves it already only as something actual. Curiosity is constituted by an unheld making-present that, only making-present, thereby constantly seeks to run away from the awaiting in which it is nevertheless, unheld, "held." The present "leaps away" (entspringt) from the belonging awaiting — in the emphatic sense of running-off. The analysis catches § 36's phenomenology and gives it its mechanism: the present in revolt — a Gegenwärtigen that bolts from its own future, craving the possible only as instant actuality (the new consumed before it can be awaited); Entspringen re-heard in both its senses at once: the present springs from awaiting (origin) and springs away from it (flight) — the pun carrying the ontology.

The third unit anatomizes the leap. The "leaping-away" making-present of curiosity is so little given over to the "matter" that, in gaining the sight, it already looks away to the next; the making-present that constantly "leaps away" from the awaiting of a determinate seized possibility makes ontologically possible the not-tarrying (Unverweilen) that distinguishes curiosity. The making-present does not "leap away" from the awaiting as though it detached itself, ontically understood, from it and left it to itself: the "leaping-away" is an ecstatic modification of the awaiting, such that the awaiting leaps after (nachspringt) the making-present. The awaiting gives itself up, as it were: it no longer lets even inauthentic possibilities of concern come toward itself from the attended, except only such as are for an unheld making-present. The ecstatic modification of awaiting by the leaping-away making-present into an after-leaping awaiting is the existential-temporal condition of the possibility of dispersion (Zerstreuung). The paragraph is the finest micro-mechanics in the chapter: the future not abolished but demoted to outrider — awaiting leaping after the present it should lead, procuring only fodder for the next glance; distraction founded as an ecstatic inversion, the future in the present's service.

The fourth unit reaches the terminus: through the after-leaping awaiting, the making-present is more and more left to itself; it makes present for the sake of the present. So entangling itself in itself, the dispersed not-tarrying becomes never-dwelling (Aufenthaltslosigkeit). This mode of the present is the most extreme counter-phenomenon to the moment of vision: in it Dasein is everywhere and nowhere; the Augenblick brings existence into the situation and discloses the authentic "Da." The two presents face each other at last in one antithesis — the never-dwelling everywhere-and-nowhere against the held moment that has a where; § 36's Aufenthaltslosigkeit given its temporal deduction, and the pair (Gegenwärtigen um der Gegenwart willen versus Augenblick) fixed as the chapter's polar co-ordinates.

The fifth unit couples the leap to forgetting: the more inauthentic the present is — that is, the more the making-present comes to "itself" — the more it flees, closing off, before a determinate potentiality-of-being; but then the less can the future come back upon the thrown being. In the "leaping-away" of the present lies at once a growing forgetting. That curiosity always already holds at the next and has forgotten the foregoing is not a result that first follows from curiosity, but the ontological condition for it itself. The coupling completes the mode's three-ecstasis portrait and inverts the common causal order once more: oblivion is not curiosity's wake but its enabling ground — the foregoing must already be dropped for the next to glitter.

The sixth unit re-derives falling's four characters. The exhibited characters of falling — temptation, tranquilization, alienation, self-entanglement — mean, with regard to the temporal sense, that the "leaping-away" making-present seeks, by its ecstatic tendency, to temporalize itself out of itself. Dasein entangles itself — this determination has an ecstatic sense. The rapture of existence in the making-present does not mean that Dasein detaches itself from its I and self: even in the most extreme making-present it remains temporal — that is, awaiting, forgetting; even making-present, Dasein still understands itself, though alienated from its ownmost potentiality-of-being, which grounds primarily in the authentic future and beenness. But insofar as the making-present constantly offers "the new," it does not let Dasein come back upon itself, and tranquilizes it ever anew; this tranquilization strengthens in turn the tendency to leap away. Not the endless unsurveyability of what is not yet seen "causes" curiosity, but the falling temporalizing-mode of the leaping-away present: even if one has seen everything, precisely then curiosity invents the new. The paragraph pays § 38's whole kinetics in temporal coin: the fall as the present's attempt at self-temporalizing (the derived ecstasis playing origin — degeneration's exact form per § 67), each character re-derived (temptation as the offered new, tranquilization as the withheld return, alienation as the distance from the leading ecstases, entanglement as the ecstatic self-capture) — and the closing sentence is the definitive refutation of every object-theory of curiosity: not the world's inexhaustibility but the present's flight makes the new; were the world exhausted, curiosity would manufacture novelty. Boredom's modern industries stand indicted in a subjunctive.

The seventh unit grounds the leap in finitude — the subsection's deepest sentence. The temporalizing-mode of the "leaping-away" of the present grounds in the essence of temporality, which is finite. Thrown into being toward death, Dasein flees proximally and mostly before this more or less expressly unveiled thrownness. The present leaps away from its authentic future and beenness, so that Dasein comes to authentic existence only by the detour over itself (auf dem Umweg über sich). The origin of the "leaping-away" of the present — that is, of the falling into lostness — is original, authentic temporality itself, which makes possible thrown being toward death. The paragraph closes the ontological circuit with the book's severest honesty: falling has no second source — the flight is finite time fleeing itself; the present bolts because what the future and been hold (death, the throw) is unbearable proximally and mostly. Hence the strange, redemptive geometry of the Umweg: authenticity reached only by the detour over the fallen present — no path around everydayness, only through it; and the last sentence states the identity that forbids all dualism: the origin of lostness is authentic temporality itself. One time, two temporalizations; the fall inside finitude, not beneath it.

The eighth unit seals the throw's closure: thrownness — before which Dasein can indeed be authentically brought, so as to understand itself authentically in it — remains nevertheless closed to it with regard to its ontic whence and how. This closedness, however, is by no means only a factually subsisting not-knowing; it constitutes Dasein's facticity and co-determines the ecstatic character of existence's abandonment (Überlassenheit) to the null ground of itself. The unit fixes the limit even authenticity cannot cross: the whence of the throw stays dark — and the darkness is promoted from ignorance to constitution: facticity is this closure; § 58's null ground receives its temporal-ecstatic gloss.

The closing unit gives the fall its physics: the throw (Wurf) of being-thrown into the world is at first not authentically caught (aufgefangen) by Dasein; the "movedness" lying in it does not already come to a "stand" through Dasein's now being "there." Dasein is carried along (mitgerissen) in thrownness: as thrown into the world, it loses itself at the "world," in the factical directedness upon what is to be attended. The present, which constitutes the existential sense of this being-taken-along, of itself never wins another ecstatic horizon — unless it be fetched back from its lostness in the resolution, so as, as held moment of vision, to disclose the current situation and, in one therewith, the original "limit-situation" of being toward death. The subsection ends on its strongest image — the throw still in flight: Geworfenheit not a past landing but a standing ballistic, the Da no arrest of the motion, Dasein carried in its own trajectory — falling as the momentum of the uncaught throw; and the sole exit named once more: the resolution's retrieval, the held Augenblick that discloses situation and Grenzsituation in one. Jaspers' word returns, now inside the temporal machinery.

###### d) The Temporality of Discourse

The opening unit places the fourth moment: the full disclosedness of the Da, constituted by understanding, disposedness, and falling, receives its articulation through discourse. Hence discourse does not temporalize itself primarily in a determinate ecstasis. But because discourse factically speaks itself out mostly in language, and speaks at first in the manner of the concernfully-discussing addressing of the "environment," making-present does have a privileged constitutive function. The placement is precise and negative: discourse, articulating the whole, has no ecstasis of its own — the one existential exempted from the assignment-table — with the factical privilege of the present (speech as worldly address) carefully distinguished from an ontological lead.

The second unit claims the tenses — and the note takes on the grammarians. The tenses (Tempora), like the other temporal phenomena of language — "kinds of action" (Aktionsarten) and "temporal stages" — do not spring from the fact that discourse speaks itself out "also" about "temporal" processes, encountered "in time"; nor do they have their ground in that speaking runs off "in a psychic time." Discourse is in itself temporal, insofar as all talking about..., of..., and to... grounds in the ecstatic unity of temporality. The Aktionsarten are rooted in the original temporality of concern, whether or not this relates itself to the within-time. With the help of the vulgar and traditional concept of time, to which linguistics is driven perforce, the problem of the existential-temporal structure of the kinds of action cannot even be posed — the note referring to Wackernagel's Lectures on Syntax and Herbig's study of Aktionsart and Zeitstufe. But because discourse is in each case a talking-over of beings, though not primarily and predominantly in the sense of theoretical assertion, the analysis of the temporal constitution of discourse and the explication of the temporal characters of language-formations can be taken in hand only when the problem of the fundamental connection of being and truth has been unrolled from the problematic of temporality. Then also the ontological sense of the "is" can be delimited — which a superficial theory of sentence and judgment has disfigured into the "copula." From the temporality of discourse — that is, of Dasein in general — can the "arising" of "signification" first be clarified, and the possibility of concept-formation be made ontologically intelligible. The paragraph is a whole philosophy of language in outline, staked against two reductions: tense is not aboutness (grammar temporal not because speech mentions temporal things) nor psychology (not because speaking takes time) — language temporal in itself, because saying is an ecstatic deed; the aspect-systems of the languages (the grammarians' Aktionsarten — perfective, durative, inchoative) claimed as fossilized temporalizations of concern, unreachable by the now-concept linguistics borrows. And the deferrals are the unwritten book in miniature: being-and-truth from temporality, the "is" rescued from the copula, meaning's genesis — the § 33 and § 44 deposits called to a redemption that Division Three never came to pay.

The third unit tables the whole yield: understanding grounds primarily in the future (anticipation or awaiting); disposedness temporalizes itself primarily in beenness (retrieval or forgottenness); falling is temporally rooted primarily in the present (making-present or moment of vision). Nevertheless, understanding is in each case a "beening" present; nevertheless, disposedness temporalizes itself as a "making-present" future; nevertheless, the present "leaps away" from, or is held by, a beening future. Therein becomes visible: temporality temporalizes itself wholly in each ecstasis — that is, in the ecstatic unity of the respective full temporalizing of temporality grounds the totality of the structural whole of existence, facticity, and falling: the unity of the care-structure. The table is the chapter's harvest in nine terms — three existentials, each with its ecstasis and its authentic/inauthentic pair (Vorlaufen/Gewärtigen; Wiederholung/Vergessenheit; Augenblick/Gegenwärtigen) — and the triple "nevertheless" (gleichwohl) guards the harvest's unity: every mode temporalizes whole; the assignments are leads, never partitions. § 65's unity-theorem verified in the concrete.

The fourth unit bars the last misreading in three lines: the temporalizing means no "succession" of the ecstases. The future is not later than beenness, and this not earlier than the present: temporality temporalizes itself as beening-making-present future. The three sentences expel sequence from the origin once and for all — the ecstases not ordered in time because they are the ordering — and the formula returns, now earned across four subsections.

The closing unit hands over to § 69: the disclosedness of the Da, and Dasein's existentiell basic possibilities, authenticity and inauthenticity, are founded in temporality. But disclosedness always concerns, equiprimordially, the full being-in-the-world — being-in as well as world. In the orientation to the temporal constitution of disclosedness, therefore, the ontological condition of the possibility must also let itself be exhibited: that there can be a being that exists as being-in-the-world. The transition names the residue with strict economy: the Da's temporality is banked; the world's is owed — § 69's transcendence-problem posed as the condition of a being that exists as In-der-Welt-sein.

##### § 69. The Temporality of Being-in-the-World and the Problem of the Transcendence of the World

The opening unit re-founds the clearing. The ecstatic unity of temporality — the unity of the "outside-itself" in the raptures of future, beenness, and present — is the condition of the possibility that there can be a being that exists as its "Da." The being that bears the title Da-sein is "cleared" (gelichtet): the light that constitutes this clearedness is no ontically present-at-hand force and source of a radiance occasionally occurring at this being. What essentially clears this being — makes it "open" and "bright" for itself — was determined, before all "temporal" interpretation, as care; in care grounds the full disclosedness of the Da. This clearedness first makes possible all illumination and lighting-up, every perceiving, "seeing," and having of something. The light of this clearedness we understand only when we do not seek an implanted, present-at-hand power, but interrogate Dasein's whole constitution of being, care, as to the unified ground of its existential possibility: ecstatic temporality clears the Da originally. It is the primary regulative of the possible unity of all essential existential structures of Dasein. The paragraph is the book's metaphor of § 28 (the Lichtung, the lumen naturale existentially re-read) given its final ground: the clearing is the ecstatic openness itself — Dasein lit because temporality is the outside-itself, no inner lamp required; and the closing title — primary regulative of all structural unity — hands temporality the office the tradition gave to the transcendental unity of apperception.

The second unit poses the deferred question: only from the rootedness of Da-sein in temporality does the existential possibility of the phenomenon become insightful which was made recognizable at the beginning of the analytic as the basic constitution — being-in-the-world. At the outset it was necessary to secure the untearable structural unity of this phenomenon; the question of the ground of the possible unity of this articulated structure remained in the background. With the intent of protecting the phenomenon against the most self-evident and therefore most fatal splitting-tendencies, the nearest everyday mode of being-in-the-world — concernful being alongside the innerworldly ready-to-hand — was interpreted in detail. Now that care itself is ontologically delimited and led back to its existential ground, temporality, concern can in its turn be expressly conceived from care, or from temporality. The unit is the Wiederholung's charter for the world-chapters: § 12's defensive unity-claim (against the fatal splittings — subject/object first among them) now to be redeemed offensively: the unity grounded, not merely guarded.

The third unit tables the section: the analysis first holds to the mode of circumspect having-to-do with the ready-to-hand, then pursues the existential-temporal possibility of the modification of circumspect concern into the "merely" onlooking discovery of innerworldly beings, in the sense of certain possibilities of scientific research. The interpretation of the temporality of circumspect as well as of theoretically concernful being alongside the innerworldly shows at the same time how the same temporality is in advance the condition of the possibility of being-in-the-world, in which being alongside innerworldly beings grounds at all. The thematic analysis of the temporal constitution of being-in-the-world leads to the questions: in what way is anything like world possible at all; in what sense is world; what and how does the world transcend; how does the "independent" innerworldly being "hang together" with the transcending world? The ontological exposition of these questions is not already their answering; it accomplishes the antecedently necessary clarification of the structures with regard to which the transcendence-problem wants to be posed. The interpretation considers a threefold: a) the temporality of circumspect concern; b) the temporal sense of its modification into theoretical cognition; c) the temporal problem of the transcendence of the world. The table sets the section's ascent — workshop, laboratory, world — with the question-battery of c) posted in advance and the modesty-clause kept: exposition of the transcendence-problem, not yet its answer.

###### a) The Temporality of Circumspect Concern

The opening unit fixes the analytical object and its holism. How do we win the direction of view for the analysis of concern's temporality? Concernful being alongside the "world" we called dealings in and with the environment; as exemplary phenomena of being-alongside we chose the using, handling, producing of the ready-to-hand and their deficient and indifferent modes. Even Dasein's authentic existence holds itself in such concern — even when concern remains "indifferent" for it. The attended ready-to-hand does not cause the concern, as though concern first arose on the ground of the effects of innerworldly beings: being alongside the ready-to-hand can be neither ontically explained from it, nor conversely the latter derived from the former; nor are they merely present-at-hand together. Nevertheless a "connection" subsists between them: from the rightly understood with-which of dealings, a light falls on concernful dealing itself; conversely, missing the phenomenal structure of the with-which entails a misrecognition of the existential constitution of dealing. For the analysis it is already an essential gain if the specific equipment-character of the nearest encountered beings is not leapt over; but beyond this one must understand that concernful dealings never dwell with a single item of equipment. Using and handling a determinate tool remains as such oriented to an equipment-context: when we seek a "misplaced" tool, the circuit of the equipment-whole is already pre-discovered — all "going to work" and reaching does not strike, out of nothing, upon an isolatedly pregiven tool, but comes back, from the always already disclosed work-world, in the grasp upon a tool. The paragraph re-plants § 15's holism at the threshold (no first tool; the reach returns from the disclosed workshop) and posts the two-way ban on causal reduction — with the quiet clause that matters most: authentic existence too dwells in concern; the temporal analysis of the workshop is everyone's, not only das Man's.

The second unit converts involvement into the question. For the analysis of dealings with regard to their with-which, the directive results: to orient the existing being alongside the attended precisely not to an isolated ready-to-hand tool but to the equipment-whole — a grasp enforced also by reflection on the distinguishing being-character of the ready-to-hand, involvement (Bewandtnis). The term is understood ontologically: the phrase "with something it has its involvement at something" is to indicate the ready-to-hand's mode of being, not ontically to state a fact. The relational character of the "with... at..." intimates that one tool is ontologically impossible: a single tool may indeed be ready-to-hand and the others "missing" — but therein announces itself the belonging of the just-ready-to-hand to an other. Concernful dealings can circumspectly let ready-to-hand beings encounter at all only if they already understand something like involvement: the circumspectly-discovering being alongside... of concern is a letting-be-involved (Bewendenlassen), that is, an understanding projecting of involvement. If letting-be-involved constitutes the existential structure of concern; if concern, as being-alongside, belongs to care's essential constitution; and if care grounds in temporality — then the existential condition of the possibility of letting-be-involved must be sought in a mode of temporalizing. The syllogism at the close sets the subsection's whole task in one chain, and the lemma en route — ein Zeug ist ontologisch unmöglich, one tool is ontologically impossible — re-mints § 15's dictum with the proof attached: even the solitary hammer announces its absent fellows.

The third unit performs the derivation. In the simplest handling of a tool lies the letting-be-involved: its at-which has the character of the toward-which (Wozu); with a view to it, the tool is usable or in use. The understanding of the toward-which — of the at-which of involvement — has the temporal structure of awaiting. Awaiting the toward-which, concern can alone at the same time come back upon something with which it has the involvement: the awaiting of the at-which, in one with the retaining of the with-which, makes possible, in its ecstatic unity, the specifically handling making-present of the tool. The derivation is the subsection's core, achieved in three sentences: use temporally decomposed — the Wozu awaited, the Womit retained, the tool presented in their unity — hammering as a temporalizing: gewärtigend-behaltendes Gegenwärtigen, the awaiting-retaining making-present, the workshop's ecstatic signature.

The fourth unit guards the terms: the awaiting of the toward-which is neither a contemplating of the "end" nor an expecting of the imminent completion of the work to be produced — it has no character of thematic apprehension at all; nor does the retaining of that with which the involvement is mean a thematic holding-fast. Handling dealings relate no more merely to the at-which than to the with-which: letting-be-involved constitutes itself rather in the unity of awaiting retention, in such a way that the making-present springing from this makes possible concern's characteristic absorption in its equipment-world. The "authentic," wholly devoted busying-oneself with... is neither only at the work, nor at the tool, nor at both "together": the letting-be-involved grounding in temporality has already instituted the unity of the relations in which concern circumspectly "moves." The guard bars the intellectualist relapse on both ecstases (no contemplated telos, no held representation — the temporality is enacted, not entertained), and the closing sentence answers a question as old as the workshop: where is the absorbed worker? Neither at hammer nor at house nor at their sum — in the instituted unity that temporality has already opened.

The fifth unit finds forgetting in the workshop: for the temporality that constitutes letting-be-involved, a specific forgetting is essential — in order to be able to go to work and handle "actually," "lost" to the equipment-world, the self must forget itself. But insofar as an awaiting in each case leads in the unity of concern's temporalizing, the concernful Dasein's own potentiality-of-being is nevertheless, as we shall yet show, placed in care. The little paragraph carries a large doctrine: absorption's condition is self-oblivion — § 68a's Vergessenheit found at the bench, essential (not a defect) to devoted work — with the counter-clause holding the balance: even the self-forgotten hammering serves, through its leading awaiting, the Seinkönnen; the worker forgotten to himself, not lost to care.

The sixth unit converts familiarity and sets up the disturbance-analysis: the awaiting-retaining making-present constitutes the familiarity in accordance with which Dasein, as being-with-one-another, "knows its way about" in the public environment. Letting-be-involved we understand existentially as a letting-"be"; on its ground the ready-to-hand can encounter for circumspection as the being that it is. The temporality of concern can therefore be further clarified if we attend to the modes of circumspect letting-encounter earlier characterized as conspicuousness, obtrusiveness, and obstinacy. The ready-to-hand tool, with regard to its "true in-itself," encounters precisely not for a thematic perceiving of things, but in the inconspicuousness of the "self-evidently" "objectively" findable. But when, in the whole of these beings, something becomes conspicuous, therein lies the possibility that the equipment-whole as such obtrudes itself along with it. How must letting-be-involved be existentially structured, so that it can let something conspicuous encounter? The question aims not at factical occasions that direct attention to something pregiven, but at the ontological sense of this directability as such. The unit banks § 16's triad for temporal re-derivation and re-poses its question one level down: not what turns the head, but what makes a head turnable — Lenkbarkeit itself as the phenomenon.

The seventh unit derives the broken tool's time. The unusable — for example the determinate failing of a tool — can be conspicuous only in and for a handling dealing: even the sharpest and most sustained "perceiving" and "representing" of things could never discover anything like a damage of the tool; handling must be able to be disturbed, so that the unhandy can encounter. But what does that mean ontologically? The awaiting-retaining making-present is held up (aufgehalten), with regard to its absorption in the involvement-relations, by what afterwards exposes itself as damage: the making-present — equiprimordially awaiting the toward-which — is held fast at the used tool, in such a way that now for the first time the toward-which and the in-order-to expressly encounter. The making-present itself, however, can only meet something unsuited-to..., insofar as it already moves in an awaiting retention of that with which there is an involvement at something. That the making-present is "held up" means: it displaces itself, in unity with the retaining awaiting, still more into itself, and so constitutes the "checking," testing, and removal of the disturbance. Were concernful dealings merely a succession of "experiences" running off "in time," and were these ever so intimately "associated," a letting-encounter of the conspicuous, unusable tool would remain ontologically impossible: letting-be-involved must as such, whatever it makes accessible in equipment-contexts, ground in the ecstatic unity of the awaiting-retaining making-present. The paragraph pays § 16's deposit in the promised currency: the broken hammer's revelation (the express Wozu and Um-zu) is a temporal event — the presenting detained at the tool while the awaiting still runs, the friction between the ecstases making the reference visible; and the closing refutation buries associationism in one clause: no sequence of experiences, however glued, could be surprised by a tool — disturbance requires the ecstatic stretch it interrupts.

The eighth unit derives missing: and how is the "ascertaining" of what is lacking — the un-ready-to-hand, not merely the unhandily ready-to-hand — possible? The un-ready-to-hand is circumspectly discovered in missing (Vermissen). Missing — and the "ascertaining" of something's not-being-present-at-hand founded in it — has its own existential presuppositions: it is by no means a not-making-present, but a deficient mode of the present in the sense of the un-making-present (Ungegenwärtigen) of something expected or always already available. Were circumspect letting-be-involved not "from the house out" awaiting of the attended, and did the awaiting not temporalize itself in unity with a making-present, Dasein could never "find" that something is lacking. The analysis is a small phenomenological triumph: absence experienced is not experience absent — Vermissen a positive presenting-of-the-un-present, possible only inside a standing awaiting; the empty tool-hook as an ecstatic accomplishment. (Husserl's frustrated intention is nearby; here it receives its temporal ground.)

The ninth unit derives surprise: conversely, the possibility of being-surprised by something grounds in this — that the awaiting making-present of one ready-to-hand thing is unawaiting (ungewärtig) of another that stands in a possible involvement-context with the first. The unawaiting of the lost making-present first discloses the "horizonal" play-space within which the surprising can assail Dasein. The pair completes itself with the same fine grammar: as missing is a mode of presenting, surprise is a mode of awaiting — the un-awaited strikes only a being whose awaiting has left room; astonishment's ontology in two sentences.

The tenth unit derives resignation and resistance. What concernful dealings do not master — as producing, procuring, but also as turning-away, keeping-distant, protecting-oneself against... — unveils itself in its insurmountability; concern comes to terms with it (findet sich damit ab). Coming-to-terms-with... is an own mode of circumspect letting-encounter: on the ground of this discovering, concern can find the inconvenient, disturbing, hindering, endangering — the somehow resistant in general. The temporal structure of coming-to-terms lies in an awaiting-making-present non-retaining (Unbehalten): the awaiting making-present does not "count on" the unsuited that is nevertheless available. Not-counting-with... is a mode of taking-account of that to which one cannot hold oneself: it is not forgotten but retained, so that it remains ready-to-hand precisely in its unsuitedness. Such ready-to-hand things belong to the everyday stock of the factically disclosed environment. The unit extends the temporal lexicon to the workshop's stoicism — the Unbehalten that keeps what it discounts — and quietly re-derives § 43(b)'s resistance-analysis: the widerständig met within concern's ecstatic economy, not before it.

The eleventh unit totals the yield: only insofar as the resistant is discovered on the ground of concern's ecstatic temporality can factical Dasein understand itself in its abandonment to a "world" of which it never becomes master. Even if concern remains restricted to the urgency of the everyday needed, it is never a pure making-present, but springs from an awaiting retention, on whose ground — or as which "ground" — Dasein exists in a world: hence factically existing Dasein always already knows its way about, in a certain manner, even in a foreign "world." The paragraph draws the subsection's deepest consequence: finitude legible in the shop — the never-mastered world understood as such only by an ecstatically stretched being — and the closing observation (oriented even in the strange city) certifies the a priori: familiarity precedes every particular acquaintance because the awaiting-retaining structure travels with Dasein.

The closing unit marks the level and the transition: the letting-be-involved founded through temporality is a still wholly pre-ontological, unthematic understanding of involvement and readiness-to-hand; how far temporality in the end also founds the understanding of these determinations of being as such will be shown in what follows. First the temporality of being-in-the-world is to be demonstrated still more concretely: with this intent we pursue the "arising" of the theoretical comportment toward the "world" out of circumspect concern. Both the circumspect and the theoretical discovering of innerworldly beings are founded on being-in-the-world; the existential-temporal interpretation of the former prepares the temporal characterization of this basic constitution. The boundary-clause is the whole book's ladder in one line: temporality has grounded the pre-ontological understanding; whether it grounds the ontological one (the understanding of readiness and presence as such) is Division Three's question, here left standing in the "will be shown" that never came.

###### b) The Temporal Sense of the Modification of Circumspect Concern into the Theoretical Discovery of the Innerworldly Present-at-Hand

The opening unit fixes the question's genre — the existential concept of science. When, in the course of the existential-ontological analyses, we ask after the "arising" of theoretical discovering out of circumspect concern, this already implies that the ontic history and development of science, its factical occasions and proximate aims, are not made the problem. Seeking the ontological genesis of the theoretical comportment, we ask: which are the existentially necessary conditions of possibility, lying in Dasein's constitution of being, for Dasein's being able to exist in the manner of scientific research? This question aims at an existential concept of science, distinguished from the "logical" concept, which understands science with regard to its result and determines it as a "founding-context of true — that is, valid — propositions." The existential concept understands science as a way of existence, and thus as a mode of being-in-the-world that discovers or discloses beings or being. A fully sufficient existential interpretation of science, however, can be carried through only when the sense of being and the "connection" between being and truth have been clarified from the temporality of existence: the following reflections prepare the understanding of this central problematic, within which alone the idea of phenomenology, in distinction from the introductory pre-concept, will also first be developed. The paragraph founds an entire discipline in passing — the existential Wissenschaftsbegriff against the logician's (science as proposition-system: the neo-Kantian and positivist consensus dismissed as the result-concept) — science as an existence-way; and the two deferrals at the close are among the book's most consequential unpaid notes: being-and-truth from temporality, and the idea of phenomenology itself, both remanded to the missing division — the method's final self-understanding never delivered.

The second unit restricts the case: corresponding to the level reached, a further restriction is imposed — we investigate only the switch-over (Umschlag) of circumspect concern with the ready-to-hand into the research of the innerworldly findable present-at-hand, with the guiding intent of penetrating to the temporal constitution of being-in-the-world in general. The restriction is honest: not a theory of all science (the historical and human sciences expressly wait for Chapter Five), but the one classical switch — workshop to physics — as the transcendence-problem's approach.

The third unit destroys the abstinence-theory. It is tempting to characterize the switch-over from "practical" handling to "theoretical" research thus: pure looking-at beings arises through concern's abstaining from every handling — the decisive element of the "arising" of theory would lie in the vanishing of praxis. Precisely if one posits "practical" concern as factical Dasein's primary mode of being, "theory" would owe its ontological possibility to the absence of praxis — to a privation. But the suspension of a specific handling in concernful dealings does not simply leave the guiding circumspection behind as a remainder: concern then displaces itself rather expressly into a mere-looking-around. Yet therewith the "theoretical" attitude of science is by no means reached; on the contrary, the tarrying that sets in with the suspension of handling can take the character of a sharpened circumspection — as "checking," reviewing the achieved, surveying the "operation just now at a standstill." Abstaining from tool-use is so far from being already "theory" that the tarrying, "considering" circumspection remains wholly bound to the attended ready-to-hand. "Practical" dealings have their own ways of tarrying; and as praxis has its specific sight ("theory"), so theoretical research is not without its own praxis: the reading-off of measurement-numbers as the result of an experiment often needs a complicated "technical" construction of the experimental arrangement; observation with the microscope depends on the production of "preparations"; the archaeological excavation preceding the interpretation of the "find" demands the crudest handlings; and even the "most abstract" working-out of problems and fixing of results handles, for example, writing-equipment. However "uninteresting" and "self-evident" such components of scientific research may be, they are ontologically by no means indifferent. The express reference to the fact that scientific comportment, as a way of being-in-the-world, is not only "purely spiritual activity" may seem circumstantial and superfluous — if only it did not become plain at this triviality that it by no means lies in the open where, then, the ontological boundary between "theoretical" and "atheoretical" comportment actually runs! The paragraph is one of the book's great destructions, executed symmetrically: theory is not praxis-minus (the stopped hand yields inspection, stock-taking, the foreman's survey — sharpened circumspection, not science), and praxis is not theory-minus (its own sight); while science's own hands are inventoried with affectionate concreteness — apparatus, preparations, spades, pens — the laboratory as workshop. Every praxis has its theory, every theory its praxis: the ancient bios-theoretikos boundary erased as an ontological line and reposed as a problem; the sociology and philosophy of experiment (Duhem behind, decades ahead) given their charter in a parenthesis about microscope-slides.

The fourth unit finds the tradition's clue — the primacy of seeing. One will urge that all handling in science stands only in the service of pure contemplation, of the investigating discovery and disclosure of the "things themselves"; "seeing," taken in the widest sense, regulates all "arrangements" and retains the priority. "In whatever way and by whatever means a cognition may relate to objects, that through which it relates to them immediately, and at which all thinking as means aims, is intuition" — Kant's sentence, with the author's own emphasis on abzweckt. The idea of the intuitus has guided all interpretation of cognition since the beginnings of Greek ontology until today, whether it be factically attainable or not. In accordance with the priority of "seeing," the exhibition of the existential genesis of science must set in with the characterization of the circumspection that leads "practical" concern. The unit concedes the objection its whole truth and converts it into the method: seeing does lead — from the noein through the intuitus to Kant's Anschauung, one unbroken regency (§ 36's dossier recalled) — so the genesis of theory must be traced through sight's own modification; the objector's premise becomes the analysis's path.

The fifth unit analyzes circumspection upward: overview and deliberation. Circumspection moves in the involvement-relations of the ready-to-hand equipment-context; it stands itself under the guidance of a more or less express overview (Übersicht) of the equipment-whole of the current equipment-world and its belonging public environment. The overview is not merely a subsequent raking-together of the present-at-hand: its essential element is the primary understanding of the involvement-totality within which factical concern in each case sets in; it receives its "light" from that potentiality-of-being of Dasein for the sake of which concern exists as care. The "overviewing" circumspection brings the ready-to-hand nearer to Dasein, in each use and handling, in the manner of an interpretation of the sighted. The specific circumspect-interpreting nearing of the attended we call deliberation (Überlegung); its peculiar schema is the "if—then": if this or that is to be produced, taken into use, prevented, then these or those means, ways, circumstances, opportunities are needed. Circumspect deliberation illuminates Dasein's current factical position in its attended environment; it never merely "ascertains" the presence-at-hand of a being or its properties. Deliberation can also accomplish itself without what it circumspectly nears being itself palpably ready-to-hand and present in the nearest sight-range: the bringing-near of the environment in circumspect deliberation has the existential sense of a making-present — for envisaging (Vergegenwärtigung) is only a mode of this; in it deliberation directly catches sight of the un-ready-to-hand needed. Envisaging circumspection does not relate to "mere representations." The paragraph builds the bridge's first span: circumspection given its two upper stories — the Übersicht (lit from the Worumwillen: even the shop's survey borrows care's light) and the Überlegung with its wenn—so schema, practical inference as temporalized interpretation — and the imagination re-founded in passing: Vergegenwärtigung a mode of presenting the absent thing itself, not a traffic in inner pictures; representationalism refused even for planning.

The sixth unit grounds the schema and redeems the as-structure. Circumspect making-present, however, is a multiply founded phenomenon. First, it belongs in each case to a full ecstatic unity of temporality: it grounds in a retaining of the equipment-context, of which Dasein is concernfully awaiting a possibility; what is already opened up in awaiting retention the deliberating making-present or envisaging brings nearer. But for deliberation to be able to move in the schema of the "if—then," concern must already understand an involvement-context "overviewingly": what is addressed with the "if" must already be understood as this and that. For this it is not required that the understanding of equipment express itself in a predication: the schema "something as something" is already predelineated in the structure of pre-predicative understanding. The as-structure grounds ontologically in the temporality of understanding. Only insofar as Dasein, awaiting a possibility — that is, here, a toward-which — has come back upon a for-this — that is, retains a ready-to-hand thing — can, conversely, the making-present belonging to this awaiting retention, setting in at the retained, bring it expressly nearer in its reference to the toward-which. The nearing deliberation must, in the schema of making-present, measure itself to the mode of being of what is to be neared: the involvement-character of the ready-to-hand is by deliberation only so neared — not first discovered — that it lets that at which something has its involvement be circumspectly seen as this. The paragraph pays one of the book's oldest debts by name: § 32's question — whether the as-structure hangs existential-ontologically together with projection — is answered: the "as" grounds in the ecstatic-horizonal unity of temporality; the hermeneutic as is the shape the presenting takes when it returns from the awaited Wozu over the retained Dazu — interpretation's schema deduced from the ecstases.

The seventh unit banks it and schedules the copula: the rootedness of the present in future and beenness is the existential-temporal condition of the possibility that what is projected in circumspect understanding can be brought nearer in a making-present, in such a way that the present must thereby measure itself to what encounters in the horizon of awaiting retention — that is, must interpret itself in the schema of the as-structure. Therewith the answer is given to the earlier question whether the as-structure stands in an existential-ontological connection with the phenomenon of projection: the "as," like understanding and interpretation in general, grounds in the ecstatic-horizonal unity of temporality. In the fundamental analysis of being — in connection with the interpretation of the "is," which as copula gives "expression" to the addressing of something as something — the as-phenomenon must be made theme anew, and the concept of the "schema" existentially delimited. The unit closes the receipt and issues the next promissory note: the copula-analysis (from § 33's deposit) and the existential concept of the schema — Kant's schematism to be re-founded — both assigned to the fundamental analysis of being; the Kantbuch would attempt precisely this, the missing division never did.

The eighth unit weighs the yield and sets the experiment. What, however, is the temporal characterization of circumspect deliberation and its schemata to contribute to answering the pending question of the genesis of theoretical comportment? Only this much: it clarifies the Dasein-like situation of the switch-over from circumspect concern to theoretical discovering. The analysis of the switch-over itself may be attempted along the guiding thread of an elementary assertion of circumspect deliberation and its possible modifications. The unit is methodological honesty in miniature — the deliberation-analysis supplies the launch-site, not the launch — and the chosen instrument is announced: one everyday sentence, tracked through its modifications; the destruction of the theory/praxis boundary to be conducted philologically, on eight words.

The ninth unit stages the modification on that sentence. In circumspect tool-use we can say: the hammer is too heavy — or too light. Even the sentence "the hammer is heavy" can give expression to a concernful deliberation and mean: it is not light, it demands force for its handling, it will make the handling difficult. But the sentence can also mean: the being lying before us, which we circumspectly already know as a hammer, has a weight — the "property" of heaviness: it exerts a pressure on what lies beneath it; upon removal of this, it falls. Talk understood in this way is no longer spoken in the horizon of the awaiting retention of an equipment-whole and its involvement-relations: what is said is drawn from looking at what is proper to a "massy" being as such. What is now sighted is proper to the hammer not as tool, but as corporeal thing subject to the law of gravity. The circumspect talk of "too heavy" or "too light" now has no "sense" any more: the being now encountered offers, of itself, nothing with respect to which it could be "found" too heavy or too light. The staging is the book's most famous single example after the hammer's first appearance — the same sentence, der Hammer ist schwer, spoken twice across an ontological watershed: once inside the involvement-horizon (heavy = hard to swing), once from the look at mass as such — and the deepest index of the switch is the loss: "too heavy" becomes senseless, for the too belongs to use; the vanishing of the comparative is the vanishing of the workshop.

The tenth unit locates the switch and tests it. Whereby does the about-which of the modified talk — the heavy hammer — show itself otherwise? Not because we take distance from handling, nor because we merely look away from the tool-character, but because we look at the encountering ready-to-hand "anew" — as present-at-hand. The understanding of being that guides concernful dealings has switched over. But is a scientific comportment already constituted by our "apprehending" the ready-to-hand as present-at-hand instead of circumspectly deliberating it? Moreover, the ready-to-hand too can be made the theme of scientific investigation — for instance in the research of an environment, a milieu, in connection with a historical biography; the everyday ready-to-hand equipment-context, its historical arising, its exploitation, its factical role in Dasein, is the object of the science of economics. The ready-to-hand need not lose its equipment-character to become "object" of a science: the modification of the understanding of being seems not necessarily constitutive for the genesis of theoretical comportment "toward things." Certainly — if modification is to mean: change of the mode of being understood, in understanding, of the being lying before us. The paragraph fixes the switch in the Seinsverständnis (not in conduct or abstraction — the look re-tuned) and then, with the book's characteristic scruple, limits its own thesis: the human sciences (economics named, history implied) thematize the ready-to-hand as ready-to-hand — so the Umschlag to Vorhandenheit is one genesis of theory, the physicist's, not theory's essence; the restriction of the second unit shown to be substantive, not merely economical.

The eleventh unit completes the physicist's case: de-bounding. For the first characterization of the genesis of the theoretical comportment we took as basis a mode of theoretical grasping of innerworldly beings — physical nature — in which the modification of the understanding of being amounts to a switch-over. In the "physical" assertion "the hammer is heavy," not only is the tool-character of the encountering being overlooked, but in one therewith that which belongs to every ready-to-hand tool: its place. The place becomes indifferent — not that the present-at-hand loses its "location" altogether: the place becomes a space-time-position, a "world-point" distinguished before no other. Therein lies: the environmentally bounded place-manifold of the ready-to-hand is not only modified into a pure position-manifold — the beings of the environment are altogether de-bounded (entschränkt). The all of the present-at-hand becomes theme. The analysis catches the birth of physical space in the hammer's fall: the Platz (the tool's belonging-place, § 22) leveled to a Stelle, any point as good as any other — and with the place goes the boundary: the workshop's closed region opened into the universe; the All des Vorhandenen, nature as totality, born of the de-bounding. Isotropy and homogeneity derived, not assumed.

The twelfth unit adds the counter-movement: to the modification of the understanding of being belongs, in the present case, a de-bounding of the environment. But along the guiding thread of the now-leading understanding of being in the sense of presence-at-hand, the de-bounding becomes at the same time a delimitation (Umgrenzung) of the "region" of the present-at-hand: the more appropriately the being of the beings to be investigated is understood in the leading understanding of being — the more the whole of beings is articulated, in its basic determinations, as a possible subject-field of a science — the surer becomes the respective perspective of methodical questioning. The dialectic is exact: boundless and bounded in one act — the environment's walls fall and the region's conceptual fences rise; § 3's regional ontologies and § 10's Grundbegriffe re-derived as the de-bounding's own discipline.

The thirteenth unit gives the classical case — the mathematical projection of nature. The classical example for the historical development of a science, and equally for its ontological genesis, is the arising of mathematical physics. What is decisive for its formation lies neither in the higher esteem for the observation of "facts," nor in the "application" of mathematics in determining natural processes — but in the mathematical projection of nature itself. This projection discovers in advance something constantly present-at-hand (matter) and opens the horizon for the guiding regard upon its quantitatively determinable constitutive moments (motion, force, location, and time). Only "in the light" of a nature so projected can anything like a "fact" be found and set up for an experiment regulatively delimited from the projection. The "founding" of the "science of facts" became possible only through the researchers' understanding that there are in principle no "bare facts." In the mathematical projection of nature, again, the primarily decisive thing is not the mathematical as such, but that it discloses an a priori: the exemplary character of mathematical natural science consists accordingly not in its specific exactness and bindingness for "everyone," but in this — that in it the thematic beings are discovered in the way beings alone can be discovered: in the antecedent projection of their constitution of being. With the fundamental-conceptual working-out of the leading understanding of being, the guiding threads of the methods, the structure of the conceptuality, the belonging possibility of truth and certainty, the manner of founding and proof, the mode of bindingness and the kind of communication determine themselves: the whole of these moments constitutes the full existential concept of science. The paragraph is the twentieth century's philosophy of science in embryo, written in 1926: Galileo's revolution located not in observation nor in applied mathematics but in the Entwurf — nature projected as constant presence quantifiable in motion, force, place, time — so that facts are made findable by the projection (keine »bloßen Tatsachen«: the theory-ladenness of data, stated as the founders' own insight); exactness demoted (a consequence, not the essence — the human sciences hereby pre-acquitted of the charge of inexactness, § 7's remark redeemed); and the full concept tabled in six registers, from method to communication. Kuhn's paradigms and the Kantbuch's reading of the Critique as ontology of nature both stand in this unit's light.

The fourteenth unit names the act: thematization. The scientific projection of beings that always already somehow encounter lets their mode of being be expressly understood, in such a way that the possible ways to the pure discovering of innerworldly beings become manifest. The whole of this projecting — to which belong the articulation of the understanding of being, the delimitation of the subject-field guided by it, and the predelineation of the conceptuality appropriate to the beings — we call thematization. It aims at a freeing of the innerworldly encountering beings in such a way that they can "throw themselves against" a pure discovering — that is, become objects. Thematization objectifies — not that it first "posits" the beings: it frees them so that they become "objectively" questionable and determinable. The objectifying being alongside the innerworldly present-at-hand has the character of a distinguished making-present, distinguished from circumspection's present above all in that the discovering of the respective science is solely awaiting of the discoveredness of the present-at-hand. This awaiting of discoveredness grounds existentielly in a resoluteness of Dasein by which it projects itself upon the potentiality-of-being in "truth"; this projection is possible because being-in-the-truth constitutes a determination of Dasein's existence. The origin of science out of authentic existence is not to be pursued further here; it is now only to be understood that, and how, the thematization of innerworldly beings presupposes the basic constitution of Dasein, being-in-the-world. The appended note gives the thesis its temporal coin and its phenomenological genealogy: the thesis that all cognition aims at "intuition" has the temporal sense that all cognizing is making-present — whether every science, or even philosophical cognition, aims at a making-present remains here still undecided; Husserl uses the expression "Gegenwärtigen" for the characterization of sense-perception; the intentional analysis of perception and intuition in general could not but suggest this "temporal" characterization of the phenomenon — that and how the intentionality of "consciousness" grounds in Dasein's ecstatic temporality, the following division will show. The unit mints the concept that names science's founding deed — Thematisierung, the triple projection (being articulated, field bounded, concepts predelineated) that frees beings into objecthood: the Gegenstand read literally from the entgegenwerfen, objectivity as a mode of liberation, not of positing — and, in the boldest clause, roots research in resoluteness: the awaiting-of-discoveredness an existentiell projection upon being-in-truth; science a child of authentic existence, its origin saluted and reserved. The note is a double landmark: the whole intuition-tradition (fourth unit's dossier) translated into one temporal sentence — cognition is presenting — with philosophy's own exemption left open (the later "tautological thinking" gestates here); and Husserl credited at the exact point of nearest approach, with the enormous promissory note attached: intentionality grounded in ecstatic temporality — der folgende Abschnitt, the division that never appeared, cited here by name for its central theorem.

The fifteenth unit draws the hinge to transcendence: for the thematization of the present-at-hand — the scientific projection of nature — to become possible, Dasein must transcend the thematized beings. Transcendence does not consist in objectification; rather, objectification presupposes transcendence. But if the thematization of the innerworldly present-at-hand is a switch-over of circumspectly discovering concern, then a transcendence of Dasein must already underlie "practical" being alongside the ready-to-hand. The inference is the subsection's yield handed to c): objectivity founded on a prior beyond — and, since theory is a modification of praxis, the beyond must already carry the workshop; transcendence democratized: the carpenter transcends.

The closing unit generalizes: if, further, thematization modifies and articulates the understanding of being, then the thematizing being — Dasein — must, insofar as it exists, already understand something like being. This understanding can remain neutral: readiness-to-hand and presence-at-hand are then not yet distinguished, still less ontologically conceived. But for Dasein to be able to deal with an equipment-context, it must understand something like involvement, though unthematically: a world must be disclosed to it. This world is disclosed with Dasein's factical existence, if indeed this being essentially exists as being-in-the-world. And if, finally, Dasein's being grounds in temporality, then temporality must make possible being-in-the-world, and therewith Dasein's transcendence, which in its turn carries the concernful — whether theoretical or practical — being alongside innerworldly beings. The chain closes the subsection where c) must open: understanding of being (even neutral, pre-modal), hence world, hence transcendence, hence temporality — the ladder that the last subsection will climb as the derivation of the world's horizonal constitution.

###### c) The Temporal Problem of the Transcendence of the World

The opening unit re-poses the world-question: the understanding of an involvement-totality enclosed in circumspect concern grounds in a prior understanding of the relations of the in-order-to, toward-which, for-this, for-the-sake-of; the context of these relations was earlier set forth as significance, whose unity constitutes what we call world. The question arises: how is anything like world, in its unity with Dasein, ontologically possible — in what way must world be, so that Dasein can exist as being-in-the-world? The § 18 apparatus is recalled entire and re-interrogated at the new depth: not what the world is (answered) but how it can be — the mode of being of significance itself.

The second unit compresses § 18 into three sentences: Dasein exists for the sake of a potentiality-of-being of itself; existing, it is thrown, and as thrown delivered over to beings which it needs in order to be able to be as it is — namely for the sake of itself. Insofar as Dasein factically exists, it understands itself in this connection of the for-the-sake-of-itself with a current in-order-to. That wherein existing Dasein understands itself is "there" with its factical existence; the wherein of the primary self-understanding has Dasein's mode of being: Dasein is, existing, its world. The closing sentence is the doctrine at maximal compression — das Dasein ist existierend seine Welt — the world not had but been; the copula carrying what two chapters argued.

The third unit derives the horizonal schemata — the section's summit. Dasein's being was determined as care, whose ontological sense is temporality; that and how temporality constitutes the disclosedness of the Da was shown, and in the Da's disclosedness world is co-disclosed. The unity of significance — the ontological constitution of world — must then likewise ground in temporality. The existential-temporal condition of the possibility of world lies in this: that temporality, as ecstatic unity, has something like a horizon. The ecstases are not simply raptures toward...; to the ecstasis belongs rather a "whither" of the rapture — this whither we call the horizonal schema. The ecstatic horizon is different in each of the three ecstases: the schema in which Dasein, futurally, comes toward itself — authentically or inauthentically — is the for-the-sake-of-itself; the schema in which Dasein is disclosed to itself, as thrown, in disposedness, we grasp as the before-which of thrownness, or the to-which of abandonment — it characterizes the horizonal structure of beenness; existing for the sake of itself, in abandonment to itself as thrown, Dasein is, as being-alongside, at the same time making-present — the horizonal schema of the present is determined by the in-order-to. The paragraph introduces the book's last great concept: the ecstases have destinations — each rapture opens onto its schema (future onto the Worumwillen, beenness onto the Wovor/Woran of the throw, present onto the Um-zu) — so that the world's relational skeleton (§ 18's significance-chain) turns out to be temporality's own horizon-system: the for-the-sake-of and the in-order-to not added to time but the whithers of its ecstases. Transcendence about to be read off this geometry; GA 24's horizontale Schemata and the praesens-analysis grow from this unit.

The fourth unit welds the schemata into world: the unity of the horizonal schemata of future, beenness, and present grounds in the ecstatic unity of temporality. The horizon of the whole of temporality determines that whereupon the factically existing being is essentially disclosed: with factical Da-sein, a potentiality-of-being is in each case projected in the horizon of the future; "already-being" is disclosed in the horizon of beenness; and the attended is discovered in the horizon of the present. The horizonal unity of the schemata of the ecstases makes possible the original connection of the in-order-to relations with the for-the-sake-of: therein lies — on the ground of the horizonal constitution of the ecstatic unity of temporality, to the being that is in each case its Da there belongs something like a disclosed world. The weld is the answer to § 18's hardest question (how do the reference-chains hang on the Worumwillen?): the connection is temporality's own — the schemata unified because the ecstases are; significance as the unity of time's three whithers.

The fifth unit speaks the theorem. As the present springs, in the unity of temporalizing, from future and beenness, so, equiprimordially with the horizons of future and beenness, the horizon of a present temporalizes itself. Insofar as Dasein temporalizes itself, a world is too (Sofern Dasein sich zeitigt, ist auch eine Welt). Temporalizing itself with regard to its being as temporality, Dasein is, on the ground of its ecstatic-horizonal constitution, essentially "in a world." The world is neither present-at-hand nor ready-to-hand: it temporalizes itself in temporality; it "is" there with the outside-itself of the ecstases. If no Dasein exists, no world is "there" either. The paragraph is the transcendence-doctrine's core, and its categorial care is total: the world exempted from both innerworldly modes (weder vorhanden noch zuhanden — the last temptation of reification barred) and given the only verb that fits: die Welt zeitigt sich — the world temporalizes, worlds with time's own self-timing; and the closing conditional repeats § 43(c)'s scandal in the new register, with the same scare-quotes bearing the whole weight: no Dasein, no world "there" — the Da lapses, the beings do not.

The sixth unit derives factical discovery and its freedom: factical concernful being alongside the ready-to-hand, the thematization of the present-at-hand, and the objectifying discovery of these beings already presuppose world — they are possible only as ways of being-in-the-world. Grounding in the horizonal unity of ecstatic temporality, the world is transcendent: it must already be ecstatically disclosed so that innerworldly beings can encounter from it. Ecstatically, temporality holds itself already in the horizons of its ecstases and comes back, temporalizing itself, upon the beings encountering in the Da. With Dasein's factical existence, innerworldly beings too already encounter: that such beings are discovered with the Da of existence does not stand at Dasein's discretion; only what it in each case discovers and discloses, in which direction, how far, and how, is a matter of its freedom — though always within the limits of its thrownness. The unit balances necessity and freedom with jurist's exactness: that beings encounter is no choice (the throw delivers a discovered world); the what, whither, how-far, and how are freedom's whole domain, thrown freedom's — the phenomenological answer to both idealism (no world-positing) and fatalism (no closed disclosure).

The seventh unit dismantles the form-net and re-poses the problem. The significance-relations that determine the world's structure are therefore no network of forms that a worldless subject pulls over some material: factical Dasein, understanding itself and its world ecstatically in the unity of the Da, comes back from these horizons upon the beings encountering in them. The understanding coming-back upon... is the existential sense of the making-present letting-encounter of beings, which are therefore called innerworldly.
